title: The Entire Marquis Manor Hangs Themselves, Begging the Fake Rich Daughter to Return for the Banquet
author: Zi Lu
synopsis:
Jiang Miao: Drop the savior complex, mock other people's destinies.
That being said, as long as the pay is right, I can help you stab destiny twice!

Jiang Miao dumped three heavenly deities and fled to the mortal realm when her actions came to light, borrowing the shell of the Marquis Xuanxuan's fake rich daughter while suffering from amnesia.

The Marquis Manor had fallen so low it was nearly stripped of its peerage; it was her working her magic behind the scenes to alter their fortune and revive the family's prestige.

As soon as the true rich daughter returned, she was kicked out of the Marquis Manor, leaving with empty hands.

The entire capital was watching Jiang Miao make a fool of herself.

Staring at the black fog shrouding the sky above the Marquis Manor, she smiled crookedly: You guys are celebrating too early!

After no longer being a young rich lady, Jiang Miao's life reached an unhinged peak.

Reading fortunes, catching ghosts, digging up ancestral graves, beating people up, cursing, and scamming the emperor, the whole capital followed her into madness!

With the motto "If I have a bowl of rice, you'll have a bowl to wash," aristocratic youths fought to be her underlings.

By the time the Jiang family's luck hit rock bottom and they came to their senses, begging her to return to the manor, she had already become the capital's universally adored pet.
The entire family of the Marquis of Xuanxuan finally realized that without Jiang Miao, they were nothing.

The Marquis led his whole family in hanging themselves to force Jiang Miao back to the manor.

Jiang Miao smiled brightly and kicked away the stools from under their feet: As long as I have no morals, morality cannot blackmail me.

She had also celebrated too early, the heavenly deities were chasing her with their swords drawn...

One day, the three heavenly deities intercepted her with iron-cold faces: Pick one, or we all perish together!

chapters.title: Is the Fate of a Fake Rich Daughter Not Life Too?
chapters.content:
"Jiang Miao, our real sister has been found back. It's time for you, a fake, to give up your spot."

"Our family has raised you for fourteen years, and we've done our absolute best. Don't even think about clinging to the Jiang family any longer."

"This is also Father and Mother's wish. I advise you not to be ungrateful. Not pressing charges against you for deceiving high-ranking officials of the imperial court is already out of consideration for the affection of these past years."

"Get lost! Who do you think you are, daring to impersonate the Marquis's legitimate daughter!"

Jiang Miao looked at the three youths glaring at her with hostile brows, looking utterly shocked.

No, did the people of the Marquis Xuanxuan's manor flip their faces this fast?

Just yesterday, she was still their dear, beloved good sister. Just because their father found his biological daughter and verified that she was a fake swapped by the midwife, love just vanished like that?

Love is like a wind, blowing away once it's done...

Yet when she transmigrated here, she had already said she wasn't the biological one, but the moment Madam Jiang heard that, she searched the whole house for a rope to hang herself. How could she dare bring it up again?

Besides, having occupied the original owner's body, she hadn't spared any effort behind the scenes over the past decade, using her Daoist arts to ensure the Jiang family's smooth and peaceful passage, thus reviving the declining Marquis Manor that had almost been stripped of its peerage by the emperor.

Yet human hearts are unpredictable. The true daughter was just found, and they wanted to kick her out!

She didn't even get a single glance to see if the real daughter was pretty or not.

Good, good, good, playing it like this, huh?

Since you are heartless, I shall cast you aside. She wanted to see how long the Marquis Xuanxuan's manor could remain glorious without her!

Jiang Miao looked at the wisps of black qi faintly emerging from the faces of the three youths, especially the eldest, whose face was outstandingly black, and silently crushed the peace talisman she had stayed up late to draw yesterday into fragments.

"Hold on! Hand over all the jewelry and silver on you! You aren't taking a single copper coin from our Marquis Manor!"

The Third Young Master of the Jiang family looked at her with disgust, terrified she might still live a good life after leaving.

If he hadn't been worried that acting too harshly would damage the Marquis Manor's reputation, coupled with his younger sister's soft-heartedness in pleading for Jiang Miao, he would have planned to send Jiang Miao straight to prison!

Consider herself lucky!

Jiang Miao peeked at the faint black fog floating above the main courtyard of the Marquis Manor, invisible to ordinary people...

Tsk, the Jiang family was about to suffer a massive disaster!

She kindly reminded them: "Why don't you leave me a little? Leave a way out for others when doing things so we can meet nicely in the future! Leave a retreat for yourselves, too."

The three young masters laughed out of anger.

"Still trying to extort us?"

"Who wants to see you ever again? Disgusting!"

"Get lost! Remember to walk around us if you see us in the future, or don't blame us for not leaving a way out!"

With that, they ordered the maidservants to strip her of her jewelry, leaving not even the copper coins tucked into her waistband, and shoved her right out of the Marquis Manor.

The heavy gates of the Marquis Manor slammed shut behind her with a "bang."

Jiang Miao: "..."

Heartless!

They could at least have left her some meal money!

Wasn't the fate of a fake rich daughter considered a life?

Though, from another perspective, the Jiang family was surprisingly nice, kicking her out before disaster struck so she wouldn't have to exert herself.

No wonder she had calculated a minor tribulation for herself recently, yet the contradictory divination pointed to her fortune rising; it turned out to have been fulfilled by this matter.

This body wasn't her original one, causing every divination she made about herself to be shrouded in mystery, but she had forgotten who she was anyway.

She only vaguely remembered that she came here to hide from someone. The person who made her willing to borrow a shell just to squeak by alive was definitely, a fierce, badass monster blazing trails of fire and lightning.

She must owe that person a lot, lot of money... otherwise she wouldn't have run.

The mere thought of money put Jiang Miao in a terrible mood Σ_(???」∠)

Fortunately, she still had these silk and satin robes, which could probably be pawned for around twenty taels of silver. Dead-pawned, they might fetch a bit more, allowing her to scrape by for several months if she was frugal...

Self-improvement or whatever could wait until the month after next month.

Suddenly, the gates of the Marquis Manor opened again.

Did they regret it?

Jiang Miao proudly lifted her chin.

That wasn't entirely out of the question; they would have to kneel, apologize, write a thirty-thousand-word self-reflection essay, and undergo a probationary period...

"Splash~" A basin of cold water was dumped straight over her head, soaking her into a drowned rat.

A stout, dark-faced wet nurse stood akimbo and scolded, "The master tells you to get lost, or we'll report you to the official authorities!"

Jiang Miao: "..." Oh well, I guess these clothes can only be pawned for ten taels now.

Her small hands hidden behind her back rapidly formed a seal, and the fat matron let out a miserable shriek, falling backward with an "ouch" and knocking out her front teeth.

Jiang Miao: Never holding grudges is my fine quality!

...

"Shopkeeper, take another look. This is the newest pattern of the year, and the fabric is top-tier..."

"Five taels, not a single coin more. Other places are even more cutthroat than mine."

Direct and straightforward, she liked it!

Jiang Miao: "Then you have to give me a set of cloth garments." This was her final stubbornness!

"Deal!"

Jiang Miao changed into a set of rough, skin-pricking cloth clothes, casually tied her hair into a Daoist bun, and instantly transformed from a wealthy young miss into a bizarre little Daoist priest. Clutching her five taels of silver, she walked into the inn across the street.

Jiang Xiaomiao when her mental state is stable

Leaving the capital was completely out of the question. She wanted to watch the Marquis Manor step-by-step march toward ruin, write a documentary novel about it, and leave a notorious legacy for ten thousand years!

Also, her decennial pact with the local City God was approaching. As long as that fellow cherished his life, she should be able to figure out who she actually was.

Only by figuring out her identity could she effectively dodge her creditors, right? Who knows, maybe she had a life-and-death blood feud and couldn't even beat the person, she had better run early!

It's just that everything in the capital was expensive; five taels of silver wasn't enough for her to lie flat.

In order to stay alive and watch the Jiang family's good show, she was forced to reopen for business.

Setting a small goal: make a hundred taels first!

Jiang Miao asked the shopkeeper for a piece of canvas, some brush and ink, and scavenged a dusty bamboo pole, nimbly making a sign: Fortune Telling!

She was kicked out of her home in the morning, set up her stall at noon, highlighting pure efficiency.

Little master, there's more to this chapter, please click the next page to continue reading, more excitement awaits!

"Fortunes told! Ten copper coins per reading, no pay if not accurate." Jiang Miao lazily hawked her services.

"Jiang Miao!"

A voice rang out from the side.

Jiang Miao whipped her head around and saw two gorgeously dressed young maidens walking toward her, followed by their respective maidservants.

One of them was precisely Sun Yue'er, the granddaughter of the Imperial Academy's chief physician, with whom she used to greet each other's families and ancestors the moment they met.

The other maiden she had never seen before, though a glance made her look somewhat familiar.

Sun Yue'er excitedly pulled the maiden beside her over, "Jiang Miao, we meet again!"

Jiang Miao gave her a sideways look. "Why don't you poke your eyes out? Then you won't have to see me."

Sun Yue'er's adrenaline spiked, talking to herself the whole way as her mental state gradually unraveled.

"Tsk tsk, how do you even have the face to linger in the capital? If I were you, I would have died of shame and hanged myself from a tree long ago!"

Barely an hour had passed, and the news that Jiang Miao had impersonated a Jiang family miss and been driven out of the house after her deception was exposed had already spread across every manor.

To avoid public criticism, the Marquis of Xuanxuan had first spun public opinion to place his own family on the moral high ground.

He claimed that Jiang Miao had a brutal temperament, frequently beating servants to cripple them, throwing tantrums at home whenever things didn't go her way, and refusing to stop until she achieved her goals.

Upon learning that the Marquis Manor had found their true daughter, she had even threatened to deal with her...

See? It wasn't that they were heartless; it was just that this fake daughter was truly malicious and vicious!

He also claimed that the true rich daughter of the Marquis Manor, Jiang Jinhua, had been wandering outside for fourteen years, yet not only did she not resent Jiang Miao, she even begged her parents not to press charges against Jiang Miao for her impersonation. Comparing the two, the gap was stark.

Jiang Miao, who had never liked mingling with noble young misses in the first place, was instantly labeled with vanity and wretched morals.

Seeing Jiang Miao dressed in coarse cloth clothes that even the rough-work matrons in the manor would look down upon, Sun Yue'er was wildly excited, "Jiang Miao, you must tell me when you're sad, so I can know you're having a day like this too!"

She tugged at the sleeve of the maiden beside her and laughed maliciously:

"Huahua, this is the fake who impersonated you and enjoyed fourteen years in the Jiang family. She's the one who caused you to wander outside, suffering from hunger and cold."

The true rich daughter of the Marquis Manor, Jiang Jinhua?

Jiang Miao finally looked the girl over carefully.

The maiden before her had a face like peach blossoms, eyes brimming with spring water, and a dark, cloud-like bun adorned with pearls and jade. Her light green gauze dress made her look like Longjing tea from '82, a certified aged green tea.

Her chest was plump and full, unlike hers, which was always poor and starving!

Yet why was the aura around this person so chaotic?

Malice mixed with resentment, yin energy, a bloody stench, and a flickering, unstable protective white light, even she couldn't see through the girl's past and destiny.

Attracting evil yet repelling it all at once; it was enough to baffle a ghost...

Sisters, deposit your brains here.

chapters.title: Pay Off Grudges Immediately
chapters.content:
While Jiang Miao was sizing up Jiang Jinhua, the other girl was doing the same to her.

Eyes like bright pearls, a high-bridge nose, red lips and white teeth, she certainly had a fine appearance.

It was just a pity that her brows were a bit too sharp and her facial contours too defined, lacking the gentle charm of a woman. It made her rather androgynous, not the kind of look men liked.

And looking at her now, slouching against the wall with a ruffian's posture, completely devoid of any young lady of a noble house's deportment, it seemed her years of etiquette training had all gone to waste.

Just as expected, you can't carve rotten wood!

Seeing Jiang Miao glare at Jiang Jinhua with a frown, Su Yue'er immediately scolded her with displeasure:

"Why are you looking at Hua'er like that? What kind of wicked scheme are you hatching?"

Jiang Miao: "Guess?"

Su Yue'er: "......" Jiang Jinhua spoke up first.

She gave Jiang Miao a pitiful look and said softly:

"Yue'er, don't scold her. When she was swapped by the midwife back then, she was just an ignorant infant. Even though the midwife told her the truth later, it's only natural that she couldn't bear to leave the marquis's estate and her parents, who would want to go out and suffer? It's just a pity that the midwife didn't know the identity of the woman she bribed to swap her own daughter with mine, otherwise I could tell Jiang... Jiang Miao, and let their family reunite."

With just a few words, Jiang Jinhua firmly pinned the crimes of concealing the truth, coveting vanity, and impersonating the true daughter of the Marquis of Xuanyuan onto Jiang Miao, while simultaneously highlighting her own kindness and magnanimity.

Jiang Miao slapped her thigh, this bitch was no good!

Could the calamity facing the Jiang family be brought about by her?

She stood up and bowed to her. "My mistake. I previously thought you were 1982 Longjing aged green tea, but now I realize you're a Patek Philippe, what a watch!"

Jiang Jinhua: "???"

Su Yue'er curled her lip in disdain. "Hua'er, don't speak up for her. Look at her, does she have even a shred of guilt? Right now, she's definitely calling you a fool in her heart!"

Jiang Miao sneered. "Today I learned that Miss Su is the roundworm in my belly. Was she just pulled out of me? Why is her grievance so big?"

"You!"

Disgusted by her, Su Yue'er flushed red. But she absolutely could not lower herself to a shouting match with Jiang Miao. Furious, she ordered the maid behind her, "Slap her mouth for me!"

Jiang Jinhua stopped her, saying, "Yue'er, she has already fallen to... to such a state, spare her this once."

Though full of resentment, Su Yue'er remembered that she was currently in marriage talks with the second young master of the Jiang family and feared earning a reputation for being overbearing, so she had no choice but to endure it.

Jiang Miao raised an eyebrow at her provocatively, only to see Jiang Jinhua adopt a compassionate expression and say to her:

"I know you're hurting inside right now. I've tried to persuade my father, mother, and brothers to forgive you and welcome you back to the estate, but they're still in the heat of anger. Just wait a little longer..."

If she didn't bring this fake daughter back to the Jiang family, how could she highlight her own kindness and excellence?

More importantly, this Jiang Miao was of great use to her!

The dozen or more years of happiness Jiang Miao had stolen from her would have to be repaid with the fortune of the rest of her life...

Hearing this, Jiang Miao said excitedly:

"Wow, what a big, round pie in the sky! Draw a few more, and I can use them to set up a street stall!"

Jiang Jinhua's brain stalled for a moment. She looked at Jiang Miao in bewilderment, taking a good while to realize the other girl was mocking her.

Too lazy to deal with her, Jiang Miao began drumming up business on her own: "Fortunes told! Ten copper coins a divination, no fee if it's not accurate."

Just then, some busybodies gathered around.

"Huh, since when can wet-behind-the-ears brats tell fortunes?"

Jiang Miao's eyes lit up, business was here!

The speaker was a tall, sturdy man looking at her with a mocking expression.

Jiang Miao clicked her tongue. The top of his head was covered in a green prairie, yet he still had the nerve to stand there and mock her.

Seeing the strange look in her eyes, the man smiled wickedly. "Ten copper coins, is it? Read mine. If it's not accurate, I'll smash your stall."

Jiang Miao held out an open palm. "Pay first. No fee if it's not accurate."

"You haven't even told it yet, how do I know if it's accurate?" the man said with dissatisfaction.

"No fee if it's not accurate, think about it." As soon as Jiang Miao said this, several people burst into laughter.

"Pfft~ She can tell fortunes? Open your eyes wide and take a good look, everyone, this is a fraud. She was kicked out onto the street for impersonating the Marquis of Xuanyuan's daughter, and now she's come up with such a scummy trick to swindle people."

Su Yue'er wished she could expose Jiang Miao's crimes to the whole world; she would only feel satisfied if everyone treated her like a street rat that everyone wanted to beat.

Hearing this, a look of hesitation appeared on the man's face.

Judging by how this girl spoke, she looked like the young lady of a wealthy and powerful family at first glance; she shouldn't be lying.

Normally, Jiang Miao wouldn't stoop to the level of ordinary mortals like Su Yue'er.

Letting the other person vent her tongue was one thing, but cutting off her livelihood was like killing her parents, this could not be tolerated.

With a "whoosh," she stood up and reached out to roll up her sleeves.

Being kind-hearted, the man hurriedly grabbed her and whispered, "Just bear with it, you can't afford to offend her..."

Jiang Miao replied, "I bore with it..."

The man breathed a sigh of relief.

Su Yue'er curled the corners of her lips in smug triumph, full of disdain. Finally realized her own status, did she?

A mere commoner dared to fight with an official's daughter?

Before she could even enjoy her triumph for a full second, she heard Jiang Miao say: "But I couldn't hold it in!"

With one hand behind her back, she rapidly formed a hand seal and smiled sinisterly at Su Yue'er:

"Today, this Great Immortal will teach you what it means to bring disaster upon yourself through your words!"

Su Yue'er glanced at her sideways with contempt. "This young lady would like to see what you can, ah~~"

Before she could finish, a miserable scream tore from her throat.

The next instant, large tears welled up in Su Yue'er's eyes as she clutched her mouth and jumped up and down in pain.

Panicked, Jiang Jinhua supported her shoulders. "Yue'er, what's wrong?"

Unable to speak, Su Yue'er lowered her hands and opened her mouth to show her.

Her tongue had been bitten in half, and fresh blood was gushing out as if it were worthless.

My lord, there is more to this chapter; please click the next page to continue reading, the rest is even more exciting!

Her heart hammering wildly, Jiang Jinhua hastily signaled the maid to help Su Yue'er toward the medical clinic.

After taking only a few steps, she looked back at Jiang Miao, her heart trembling inexplicably.

If Jiang Miao also knew sorcery, she couldn't be left alive!

The onlookers were slightly dazed, wasn't this matter a bit too bizarre?

Did the little Daoist priest really know magic?

The man reacted first and immediately counted out ten copper coins for her. "Read mine."

Jiang Miao casually pinched two copper coins and tossed them into the air. The coins landed on the stall board simultaneously, both tails.

The corners of the onlookers' eyes twitched violently, and they burst into laughter.

"She doesn't even have her own working tools, she's using the copper coins you gave her to tell fortunes."

Well, the previous scene must have just been a coincidence.

The man's face darkened instantly. Just as he was about to reach out and smash Jiang Miao's stall, he heard Jiang Miao say:

"Your wife is eight years younger than you and has just conceived a child. Today, she will definitely suffer a miscarriage, and her life will be in danger..."

The man's expression changed. "How do you know about my family's affairs?"

With her hands behind her back, Jiang Miao projected the image of an unfathomable expert. "That requires extra money."

The man asked anxiously, "Will my wife really miscarry today?"

Squinting at the sun, Jiang Miao said, "If you rush back now, you can still hire a doctor to save her life."

Hearing this, the man turned around and walked away without a word.

The onlookers were astonished, did this kid really guess right?

No, that man must have been a plant!

Refusing to believe in the supernatural, someone immediately fished out copper coins and handed them to Jiang Miao. "I'll do one too."

Just as Jiang Miao was about to reach out to take the copper coins, she saw a young man approaching from not far away, his tall and straight figure as upright as green bamboo.

The faint purple qi lingering around the youth immediately made her eyes turn to money, a genuine imperial successor, a walking golden ingot!

Without mercy, she pushed the person in front of her aside and walked toward the young man.

She blocked his path and said excitedly:

"Want a fortune told? Ten taels a divination, no fee if it's not accurate."

chapters.title: Put Down the Savior Complex, Respect the Destiny of Others
chapters.content:
The young man's handsome, proud brows wrinkled slightly, and he said impatiently, "Don't block the way."

Jiang Miao's lips flipped rapidly. "An elder in your family has been tortured by illness for years and is nearing the end. You came to the capital to seek medical treatment, didn't you?"

Hearing this, the young man's attractively contoured eyes suddenly shot out a cold, piercing glint, staring intently at Jiang Miao's face.

Quickly, he reined in his gaze and let out an amused, light chuckle.

"Then why don't you, tell me, fortune teller, if this trip to seek a doctor will go smoothly."

Jiang Miao stared at him hard, taking him in from top to bottom.

Broad shoulders, narrow waist, "dog-genitals" waist, fair skin, handsome looks, and long legs.

He looked bureaucratic yet smiled with a ruffian's air. If this were a livestream, he'd be killing it with both men and women; the top donors would be fighting every day!

His sword-like eyebrows slanted diagonally into his temples, lost among a few strands of dark hair falling by his ears. His facial contours were near perfect.

Appearance rating: 9.9.

She didn't give him a 10 out of pride for him.

Having finished her appreciation, Jiang Miao shook her head and babbled, "Within three days, there will definitely be news." It's a pity the person you're looking for is a swindling jianghu con artist.

Of course, she wouldn't say that unless she was paid extra.

As it happened, today the marquis's estate had taught her a lesson: put down the savior complex and respect the destiny of others.

Jiang Miao extinguished her desire to be helpful.

Looking at her with an obscure and unfathomable gaze, the young man dropped a silver ingot into her outstretched palm. "If it's not accurate, I'll come find you in three days." To settle accounts.

Tossing the silver ingot in her hand, Jiang Miao chuckled.

She could afford to slack off for another half a month...

Her small goal could wait for the second half of the month.

Returning to her stall, she immediately began packing up.

"Hey, hey, read mine."

"Not doing it anymore, I'm off work."

Off work?

The crowd stared in utter bewilderment, unable to understand what she was saying, and watched helplessly as she packed up her sign, her cloth banner, and the wooden plank used as a stall table, tucked them under her arm, and walked away.

The handsome young youth stood not far away and whispered to his subordinate, Shen Nan, who was behind him:

"Go follow her and see what background this kid has."

...

Jiang Miao walked and shopped all the way, buying plenty of snacks and delicacies, and even picking out a few storybooks.

She watched sugar-blowing for a bit, joined crowds watching cricket fights to shout encouragement, and observed chest-boulder-smashing with keen interest for a long time.

Her cheers were the loudest of all, but the moment someone brought around a brass gong asking for tips, she ran faster than a monkey.

She was dirt poor, possessing skills in divination, geomancy, physiognomy, miraculous healing, ghost-catching and demon-slaying, and spirit-channeling, but alas, no business came knocking.

Having been led around on a leash by her all afternoon, Shen Nan's mind was practically cracking. Which proper Daoist priest was this bored?

She was basically a street punk!

Seeing that the sun was about to set, Jiang Miao finally remembered to attend to business.

She ran through several shops to buy cinnabar, yellow paper, and white boar-bristle brushes, then ducked into a jade shop, intending to buy some white jade to make a few small magical artifacts. With any luck, she'd achieve her small goal soon.

"Shopkeeper, give me a few pieces of white jade, the cheapest kind."

Glancing at her coarse cotton clothes, the shopkeeper fetched a piece of white jade from the corner and offered an official smile: "Three taels of silver a piece, how many do you want?"

"Three taels?!"

Jiang Miao's voice shot up abruptly. This thing had neither luster nor moistness, and impurities made up the majority of it, yet he dared sell it for three taels?

Truly worthy of study!

The shopkeeper's expression turned cold, and without a word, he put the white jade away.

Jiang Miao spun around abruptly, startling Shen Nan, who had been staking her out outside, into rigidly grabbing a random passerby to pretend to ask for directions.

With a wicked smile, Jiang Miao walked straight toward him.

"Hey, little brother, lend me some silver to spend."

Shen Nan subconsciously looked around, then met Jiang Miao's eyes.

"Are you asking *me* to borrow money?"

Jiang Miao rolled her eyes. "Well, who else? You've been following me all this time, if I don't borrow from you, who do I borrow from?"

Shen Nan: "...... I don't even know you."

"Sometimes you should look for the reason within yourself, alright? You don't even know me, did you even study properly to be a scout?"

Shen Nan: "......"

"Right, your complexion is dim, and a horizontal line has appeared on your forehead. You will definitely face bloodshed within a day. I'll draw a talisman for you later."

Saying this, Jiang Miao blinked and held out her hand to him. "Let's consider it making a friend."

In a daze, Shen Nan extended his hand. "Pleased to meet you."

Jiang Miao: "You're celebrating too early. Where's the money?"

"?" Shen Nan felt his brain wasn't quite keeping up, and as if possessed by a ghost, he fished out his money pouch and placed it in Jiang Miao's palm.

Curving her eyes into crescents, Jiang Miao immediately turned around and stepped back into the jade shop.

"Shopkeeper, give me ten pieces of white jade!" Her spine felt straight as a board.

It wasn't until she returned the money pouch to Shen Nan that he finally snapped back to his senses.

Wait, why on earth had he just handed his money pouch to her?

Jiang Miao shoved the banner and stall board into his arms. "Hold these for me, come back to the inn with me, and I'll draw the talisman for you."

Inwardly, Shen Nan wanted to refuse. After the money-borrowing incident just now, he felt this youth was a bit bizarre.

Yet remembering his master's instructions, he had to bite the bullet and follow Jiang Miao to the inn.

If you don't enter the tiger's den, how can you catch the tiger's cub?

After folding the yellow paper and cutting it to the size of ordinary talisman paper, Jiang Miao directed Shen Nan: "Dissolve the cinnabar."

Struggling mildly for a moment, Shen Nan gave up resistance.

To gather intelligence, he would endure!

He wanted to see how long this little con artist could keep up the act!

Silently reciting a spell in her heart, Jiang Miao dipped her brush in cinnabar and struck the paper swiftly and steadily. Her brush danced like a swimming dragon, sweeping out a set of complex and obscure talisman characters with a vigor that pierced the back of the paper.

As if a flash of golden light had zipped past, the arcane, esoteric lines on the paper instantly came to life.

Shen Nan rubbed his eyes; just now, he seemed to have seen golden light...

It must have been because he had stared unblinkingly at the little con artist drawing the talisman all this time, causing him to hallucinate.

Right, that must be it.

Pinching the talisman paper, Jiang Miao blew on it. Not a bad amount of power, she was satisfied.

She casually handed it to Shen Nan.

"Keep it close to your body. It will turn misfortune into fortune, make big troubles small, and small troubles disappear."

Shen Nan scoffed inwardly, she put on quite an act.

Still, he took it and tucked it casually into his robes, asking suspiciously:

"Are you really a Daoist priest?"

Jiang Miao nodded firmly. "I come from a renowned school!"

"Which renowned school?"

"Less gossiping about matters of the jianghu."

"You knew all those things about our young master just by taking one look at him?"

"Not at all. I also performed sorcery, it's just that you mortals couldn't see it."

Shen Nan: "...... What a blower!"

Having shopped until she was tired and wanting nothing more than to sprawl on the bed and read storybooks, Jiang Miao waved her hand to chase him out.

"You can leave now. Come find me if anything comes up, though next time it won't just be a matter of ten taels of silver."

Shen Nan laughed out of anger. "You still owe me thirty taels."

Jiang Miao said triumphantly, "So now I'm your master."

With that, she shoved Shen Nan out the door.

Standing outside, Shen Nan felt utterly bewildered.

The little con artist looked so frail and weak, why had he been pushed out without any ability to resist?

Retaining a shred of suspicion, Shen Nan went straight to the innkeeper to inquire about Jiang Miao. Upon learning that she had paid for half a month's rent in advance, he felt slightly more at ease.

Since the little con artist was so poor, she surely wouldn't abandon her room rent and run away, right?

Lowering his head to gaze at the talisman paper in his hand, Shen Nan felt more and more convinced he had been swindled.

He had seen plenty of talisman paper in his time, but he had never seen any drawn with such chaotic methodology.

Gritting his teeth, he thought: "She's a fraud!"

And that nonsense about facing bloodshed within a day, whoever believed that was an absolute idiot!

chapters.title: This Great Immortal Will Never Be a Simp
chapters.content:
Inside the Prince靖南 (Jingnan) Manor in the capital.

The man whose path Jiang Miao had blocked for fortune-telling slightly furrowed his brows as he listened to Shen Nan report the beginning and end of tracking Jiang Miao.

The setting sun filtered through the window, outlining his three-dimensional silhouette. The golden-red light made him so breathtakingly handsome that he didn't seem like a mortal.

The man was the second son of the Prince of Jingnan, Prince Ye of the Commandery, Mo Beishu.

Shen Nan confessed his fault:

"This subordinate is dull and failed to uncover her background."

Mo Beishu put down the document in his hand and tapped his fingers lightly on the small side table next to him.

"You said she drew a talisman for you?"

Shen Nan hurriedly presented the talisman paper with both hands. "She said it can ward off evil and turn big disasters into small ones, and small disasters into nothing."

Mo Beishu took the talisman paper and looked at it for a long time, unable to make out any tricks to it.

"It is indeed different from ordinary talisman paper."

"You see it too? This subordinate also felt she was fooling me. Whose talisman paper is drawn like ghost-drawn peach charms?"

Mo Beishu lowered his eyes, wondering what he was thinking.

He handed the talisman paper back to Shen Nan. "Thirty taels have already been spent; throwing it away is an even greater loss."

Shen Nan thought that made sense. The little swindler probably didn't have the money to pay him back anyway, and not everyone was as easily fooled as the little prince... no, as magnanimous.

He casually tucked the talisman paper into his bosom.

Mo Beishu said again: "You don't need to investigate that youth anymore. I'll have people in the capital look into it. These past two days, keep asking around for the whereabouts of that divine doctor."

Shen Nan accepted the order and left.

Mo Beishu called another person over and instructed them to investigate Jiang Miao's background.

Without figuring out why that youth knew he had come to the capital to seek medical treatment, he wouldn't be at ease. He hadn't told anyone about this matter except for his closest confidants.

At night, the manor's silence was shattered by a sharp shout.

"Assassins! Protect the Little Prince!"

A group of men in black with masked faces seemed to descend from the sky, densely pouring into the manor and engaging the guards in a bloody battle.

Drawing his sword, Shen Nan blocked three masked men in black, his entire body exuding a piercingly cold aura. Where was there any trace of his daytime, slow-witted appearance?

The assassins' moves were bizarre, and they coordinated closely with one another. Even with Shen Nan's high martial arts, he was caught off guard.

Shen Nan narrowly dodged a long sword that grazed his neck, but his back was left wide open. An assassin seized the opportunity, the long sword in his hand thrusting straight toward Shen Nan's back with speed and ruthlessness.

By the time Shen Nan sensed the fierce wind behind his back, it was too late to dodge. He managed to shift three inches, his heart already prepared to be stabbed.

However, the assassin could never have imagined that his accomplice, who had originally been in seamless coordination, would also inexplicably and rigidly turn around and stab toward Shen Nan's back.

The two long swords collided halfway. With a crisp "clang," both men were simultaneously jolted a step backward.

Seizing the opportunity, Shen Nan swung his long sword back in a reverse grip, remarkably slicing across the necks of both assassins at the same time...

Standing not far away, Mo Beishu watched this scene, his eyes widening in shock.

This was simply a miracle!

A situation of certain death was actually forcefully reversed!

Soon, the manor guards gained the upper hand, and the assassins fell one by one.

Mo Beishu said in a deep voice, "Leave a living captive!"

He looked at Shen Nan with a complex gaze. "Come with me."

Entering the room, Mo Beishu asked, "Where is the talisman paper?"

Shen Nan hurriedly fished it out. Mo Beishu took it and looked, only to feel that the lines, which had looked so lively and full of spirit during the day, now seemed somewhat stagnant.

The space between his brows immediately furrowed.

The Master did not speak of strange phenomena, physical exploits, disorder, and spiritual beings; he clearly didn't believe that defying-heaven techniques truly existed in the world, yet at this moment, he hesitated.

Could that youth truly be an expert?

Yet not only did he not look like an expert, but he looked like, like a glib little ruffian!

Was it a coincidence?

At this moment, Shen Nan also thought of the scene where they had just narrowly escaped disaster, and his eyes suddenly widened. "Master, you don't actually think this ghost-drawn talisman is useful, do you?"

Mo Beishu looked at him with eyes like deep pools.

Twirling his fingers, he said calmly, "Perhaps it's just a coincidence. Leave the talisman with me for now, I'll ponder over it."

With that, he instructed Shen Nan to handle the aftermath.

Obeying the order, Shen Nan walked out, inexplicably feeling a sense of emptiness in his heart...

...

Jiang Miao slept until the sun was high in the sky before waking up. The first thing she did was climb onto the roof of the inn to observe the Marquis's Mansion.

The gray fog shrouding the main courtyard had expanded by a small circle, though it wasn't obvious.

Touching her chin, Jiang Miao muttered to herself, "How strange. This calamity of the Jiang family came out of nowhere; their ancestors were not vicious or evil people either. By all rights, they shouldn't suffer such retribution."

It seemed she would have to find a way to look at the changes in the Jiang family's physiognomy to determine whether this calamity was brought by Jiang Jinhua.

However, this calamity still had to wait a few days before descending; it wasn't without room for maneuver, provided she was willing to intervene.

Immediately, she cursed and swore, "Bah! A good horse doesn't turn back to graze on old pasture; this Great Immortal will never be a simp!"

Huh, why did she say "this Great Immortal"?

Unable to remember, Jiang Miao simply stopped thinking about it.

It's just that waiting for these days meant she still had to continue doing business to earn room and board so she could watch the joke from up close.

Still, it wasn't a big problem; that purple-smoke-emitting kid would bring money over.

Jiang Miao yawned and went back to reading her popular romance novel. She had fallen asleep yesterday just as the vixen was trying to seduce the scholar for ages without success, which was rather frustrating...

The Jiang Mansion.

Marquis Xuanyuan looked at his newly found biological daughter, Jiang Jinhua, and the more he looked, the more satisfied he became.

She truly was seed of his Jiang family; this fine appearance was rare even in the capital, taking after her mother's looks.

Not at all like that fake Jiang Miao. Although Jiang Miao's facial features were delicate, her cheeks were too thin, completely lacking the auspicious physiognomy of their Jiang family. He had actually been hoodwinked for over a decade.

With Hua'er's fine appearance, coupled with the Marquis's Mansion's lineage, she was even capable of entering the palace to become a imperial concubine.

It was a pity the Emperor was getting old, and he couldn't bear to let his daughter suffer grievances.

However, there was a good opportunity right now, and he had to grasp it tightly.

Holding her handkerchief, Jiang Jinhua sat gracefully in the lower seat below Madam Jiang, a subtle pride blooming in her heart.

She had been swapped by that midwife and sold as a daughter to a deaf-mute man. Her adoptive father was a carpenter with superb craftsmanship, and many wealthy people came by name to hire him to make furniture.

All the money her adoptive father earned was spent on her.

He had hired a female tutor to teach her reading and writing, taught her to play the zither and go, and instructed her in etiquette, all to find her a good husband's family in the future.

Now, this etiquette had come in handy first. After changing into brocade and fine silk, who could still say that Jiang Jinhua was not a noble young lady of a high-ranking family?

As for her adoptive father...

Jiang Jinhua lowered her eyes, banishing the last trace of unease in her heart. Father had given him silver as compensation for raising her; not charging him with the crime of secretly buying a high-born official's daughter was already an act of benevolence.

Everyone had their own destiny; she and her adoptive father were ultimately not people of the same social strata.

"Hua'er, Prince Ye has come to the capital, and the Emperor intends to grant him a marriage. You have returned at just the right time. If you can marry into the Prince of Jingnan's Manor, you will enjoy boundless glory and wealth for a lifetime, and Father will finally be at ease."

Marquis Xuanyuan was sincerely planning for his beloved daughter.

The Prince of Jingnan's Manor?

Suppressing her excitement, Jiang Jinhua asked, "Could it be the Prince of Jingnan's Manor whose fief is in Ningzhou?"

"Oh? Hua'er knows of the Prince of Jingnan's Manor?" Madam Jiang was somewhat surprised.

Jiang Jinhua nodded.

Her adoptive father had once been hired by a wealthy merchant in Ningzhou to build a house. Not at ease leaving her alone at home, he had taken her along as well.

She had once laid eyes on that overwhelmingly regal and extraordinarily handsome youth, and heard people say that he was Mo Beishu, the little prince of the Prince of Jingnan's Manor, granted the title 'Ye' by the Emperor.

Who didn't know that Ningzhou was the most fertile land in the Dafeng Dynasty, with miles of fertile fields and prosperous commerce? It wasn't hard to imagine how wealthy the Prince of Jingnan's Manor was.

That single fleeting glance back then had haunted her dreams for a long time, making her feel that she would even be willing to be a concubine to the little prince. Never did she expect that she would now have the opportunity to become his legal wife!

As expected, even if Jiang Jinhua was a bright pearl covered in dust, there would be a day when she shone brilliantly!

Acting with ladylike restraint, she said, "Your daughter has only heard people mention it, I don't really understand it."

Marquis Xuanyuan smiled lovingly, his eyes full of heartache.

It was all his fault for being hoodwinked by Jiang Miao for many years, giving the best of everything to Jiang Miao while letting his own biological daughter suffer hardship outside.

"It's not strange that you don't understand since you haven't lived in this circle. Father will tell you about him."

chapters.title: The Jiang Family's Scheming
chapters.content:
"When Prince Ye was born, the sky over Ningzhou was covered with auspicious clouds. The National Preceptor personally certified that this child carries great fortune and is extremely important to our Dafeng Dynasty, so the Emperor has also showered him with special affection."

"Prince Ye has lived up to expectations: talented in both civil and martial arts. At a young age, he has already governed Ningzhou in an orderly manner, earning endless praise from the common people. If he didn't have an older brother, the Emperor would have already named him the Heir Apparent."

"However, him being named Heir Apparent is only a matter of time; otherwise, the Emperor wouldn't have suppressed the matter for so many years without naming his older brother as Heir Apparent."

Upon hearing this, Madam Jiang could not help but feel some worry.

"Although Prince Ye is outstanding, after all, succession goes to the legitimate and the eldest. It's not certain he will be named Heir Apparent. If he ultimately fails to inherit it, wouldn't our Hua'er be wronged by marrying him?"

Marquis Xuanyuan waved his hand.

"Madam, you speak incorrectly. His older brother is mediocre and ordinary, completely incomparable to him. The Emperor will definitely not name his older brother Heir Apparent."

Pausing, he waved his hand to dismiss all the maidservants and mamis.

Only then did he lower his voice and say:

"I've also heard that Prince Ye is actually..."

Marquis Xuanyuan pointed toward the sky, "...that person's biological son."

！！！

Madam Jiang and Jiang Jinhua abruptly widened their eyes, their hearts nearly leaping out of their chests for a moment.

Marquis Xuanyuan gave two light coughs and said solemnly:

"This matter is of great importance. I am telling you both so that Hua'er can have a clear idea in her mind and seize this opportunity well. Under no circumstances must a third person know of this!"

Madam Jiang patted her chest, unable to conceal the excitement in her eyes.

"If that's the case, even if he isn't the Heir Apparent, the Emperor will surely have other, better arrangements. Who's to say that that position..."

She tightly grasped Jiang Jinhua's hand. "My Hua'er is blessed!"

Jiang Jinhua's face flushed slightly, and she bashfully lowered her head...

No one saw the scheming in her eyes.

She had to marry Prince Ye; the Luban Book passed down from her adoptive father's ancestors was in her hands. She refused to believe there was anything Jiang Jinhua could not get!

Meanwhile, in the Prince of Jingnan's Manor, an immortal-like old Daoist priest in green robes with a crane's appearance and a child's complexion sat to the right of Mo Beishu, his fingers rapidly pinching to calculate.

A draft blowing through the hall fluttered the old Daoist's snow-white beard and hair, making him look even more ethereal.

Before long, the old Daoist withdrew his hands, pondered, and said:

"The Elder Princess's destiny favors metal and avoids earth; indeed, she is unsuited to live in Ningzhou for long. The capital belongs to the north and its attribute is metal, which is much more advantageous for the Elder Princess."

Mo Beishu couldn't help raising his brows slightly, puzzled.

"You are a doctor, why do you act like a Daoist priest?"

The old Daoist glanced at him, his expression neither humble nor arrogant, and stroked his beard.

"The Prince may not know this, but those who practice Daoism go against the heavens. What they cultivate is this present life, and what they seek is longevity and immortality, so naturally they understand the human body extremely well."

He added: "The Daoist sect has five arts: mountain, medicine, destiny, physiognomy, and divination, propagating the Dao through these arts. This poor Taoist is a Daoist physician; I know how to calculate destiny, and even better, how to save lives."

Mo Beishu nodded slightly. "Thank you for the explanation, Sir. By your meaning, should this Prince bring my grandmother to the capital?"

"Precisely. This poor Taoist just calculated it: if the Elder Princess's illness is to be cured, her treatment must be carried out in the metal position favorable to her. Only then can nothing go wrong."

After a brief thought, Mo Beishu agreed.

"In that case, I must ask you to stay in the capital for a few more days, until my grandmother arrives."

"Easily done. The Elder Princess is also blessed; recently, this old Daoist agreed with the abbot of Qingfeng Temple outside the city to discuss the Dao, which is why I appeared in the capital and was sought out by the Prince."

Mo Beishu was not good at flattering people and only gave a faint smile.

Suddenly, a thought arose in his heart. He took out the talisman drawn by Jiang Miao and handed it to the old Daoist.

"Sir, take a look at this. Is this talisman real?"

Taking it, the old Daoist furrowed his brow high up, speaking with a hint of disdain:

"Can this even be called a talisman? This poor Taoist has practiced for nearly a hundred years and has never seen such a spell. The Prince bringing this kind of thing to test this old Daoist, is he looking down on people?"

Mo Beishu waved his hand. "Sir, please do not misunderstand. This was bought by my subordinate on the street; I am only asking you to distinguish the true from the false."

The old Daoist's expression cleared slightly as he handed the talisman paper back to Mo Beishu. "I advise the Prince not to keep these messy things around him, lest they disrupt your own fortune."

With that said, the old Daoist did not dawdle. Leaving behind a contact address, he drifted away.

Shen Nan thought to himself that it was just as expected; he had known that youth was a little swindler!

Watching the old Daoist's steady gait, he couldn't help exclaiming, "Now this is a proper Daoist priest!"

Unlike that little swindler, who bounced around like a monkey.

A Daoist priest?

If that little swindler could sit quietly in meditation for a quarter of an hour, he would do a handstand and eat shit!

Three jin of it!

Mo Beishu looked at the talisman paper in his hand. Just as he wanted to return it to Shen Nan, for some reason he felt a bit reluctant, and tucked it back into his own bosom.

As for the old Daoist's claim that a single piece of talisman paper would disrupt his fortune, he didn't believe it.

He thought to himself that the youth had indeed guessed right: Divine Doctor Mu was found within three days.

Little did he know that the "Divine Doctor Mu" in his mouth was currently panicked to the extreme, fleeing the manor and running straight out of the city.

He headed directly to Qingfeng Daoist Temple on West Mountain.

Finding Abbot Changsongzi who was meditating, he went down with a "thud" and knelt.

Clutching the other's leg, he cried out, "Brother, a big job has come in."

Upon learning that his scamming had actually reached the Prince's head, Changsongzi flew into a rage and kicked him quite a distance away.

Sternly, he rebuked: "Trick ordinary people if you must; left and right, it won't kill anyone. But are people of the imperial family someone you can hoodwink?"

The old Daoist put on a crying face. "I didn't want to either, but what they offered was simply too much. The moment I heard a hundred taels of gold①, my legs decided not to listen and followed him home..."

"What did you say? A hundred taels of gold!!!"

Changsongzi's eyes instantly gleamed with greed, his face blooming into a smile like a chrysanthemum as he stepped forward to help him up.

Smiling broadly, he said, "Goudan ah, we'll take this job. Brother will help you find out about the Elder Princess's illness, you hurry up and read the medical books."

The heavy stone in Goudan's heart fell, and he obediently went to sharpen his spear at the last minute.

"Come back, your hair and beard need to be dyed," Changsongzi reminded him.

...

Over on Jiang Miao's side, after paying the room rent, she had only half a tael of silver left in her pocket. She wouldn't starve to death going a few days without food, but she absolutely could not sleep on the streets.

After a few days of lying flat, she had no choice but to shoulder her sign and cloth banner and go out to set up a stall to earn money.

Her intestines were turning green with regret. Actually, sleeping under a bridge arch wasn't entirely unacceptable; she still hadn't remembered who she was, and if she starved to death she would be a clueless ghost, that was simply unbearable.

Besides, if she didn't watch Marquis Xuanyuan's mansion collapse step-by-step, she would die with her eyes open!

"Fortune-telling! Ten cash a divination, no money if it's not accurate!"

In the private room on the third floor of the teahouse opposite, Mo Beishu and a youth in brocade sat by the window watching Jiang Miao.

That youth was laughing so hard his stomach hurt. "Second Brother, is this the expert with high Daoist cultivation you thought she was? She's the fake daughter just driven out of the family by Marquis Xuanyuan, rotten to the core since childhood!"

The tips of Mo Beishu's ears turned slightly red.

So the youth he had imagined was actually a woman.

He hadn't been able to tell that day.

Yet this couldn't entirely be blamed on him; she had a gender-ambiguous face, and in her speech and actions, there was not a trace of a woman's demeanor. It was no wonder he misjudged.

The youth continued:

"It's not strange that she knew about the Elder Princess's illness; she must have heard it from Marquis Jiang."

Mo Beishu shook his head.

"Then how did she know I returned to the capital to seek the divine physician An?"

"She guessed, of course! Her words are like an old woman's teeth, not many of them are true!" the youth said through gritted teeth.

Mo Beishu let out an "oh" and asked curiously, "Judging by the sound of it, are you very familiar with her?"

The youth immediately drew a clear line, his face full of disgust. "Who's familiar with her? If it weren't for..."

Note ①: In this novel, one tael is designated as 16 grams, so a hundred taels of gold is roughly equivalent to around 750,000 today.

chapters.title: Ah, the guy with the purple smoke is here again
chapters.content:
The boy suddenly stopped in mid-sentence, and Mo Beishu asked, "Except for what?"

The boy awkwardly turned his head away, "Nothing."

Mo Beishu smiled knowingly. It looked like he had suffered a heavy loss, so much so that the word "grudge" was practically written all over his face.

Knowing that he cared about his pride, Mo Beishu didn't press further and turned to look at Jiang Miao.

Just at that moment, the tall, burly man who had come to Jiang Miao for fortune-telling a few days ago hurried over, followed by a large group of people.

Seeing him beaming with radiant joy, Jiang Miao was completely baffled.

Logically speaking, when this man went home that day, he should have just caught his wife in the act of adultery. Why was he looking as joyful as a devoted simp who finally held the hand of his goddess?

There wasn't even the slightest sign of a new romance!

The man walked up, looked at Jiang Miao with a face full of gratitude, and said:

"Little Master, thanks to your timely reminder that day, I brought a doctor home with me and he saved my wife just in time. The doctor said if we had been even a moment later, my wife probably would have suffered a uterine hemorrhage, and not even immortals could have saved her then."

Jiang Miao chuckled and asked, full of gossip, "And then?"

The man's large face instantly turned beet red, and he said coyly and tactfully, "My wife said we'll live a good life together from now on..."

Jiang Miao: (???)?

Good grief, she had encountered a pure-love warrior, a live one!

The man hurriedly changed the subject and pointed to the people behind him, "These are all my neighbors. Hearing that your fortune-telling is miraculous, they all want to come and have theirs read..."

The neighbors had already heard of Jiang Miao's divine fortune-telling skills from the man and eagerly placed copper coins on her stall board.

Jiang Miao happily collected the coins, "Don't push, don't push, everyone gets a turn."

Her fortune-telling speed was extremely fast, dismissing one person in an average of three sentences, which could only be described as quite perfunctory.

Yet everyone who had their fortune told wore an expression of extreme astonishment, bowing to her repeatedly as they left, proving that her predictions were accurate.

Mo Beishu was extremely astonished at this sight.

This...

How could a young lady raised in an Marquis's estate know how to fortune-tell?

Recalling the intelligence he had gathered, how Su Yue'er bit off half her tongue right after Jiang Miao said, "This immortal will teach you what it means for disaster to come from the mouth", and connecting it to the scene where Shen Nan should have been severely injured but turned danger into safety, Mo Beishu became increasingly eager to figure out whether all of this was mere coincidence or if she truly possessed real skills.

After thinking for a moment, he stood up, called over the boy opposite him, and walked toward Jiang Miao's stall.

The neighboring fortune-seekers had all left, and Jiang Miao was counting copper coins.

"One hundred and ten, one hundred and twenty, one hundred and thirty... that's it?"

Tragic beyond description; she hadn't even earned a single day's rent.

Fortunately, she had given a few pointers to two neighbors who showed signs of internal family strife, telling them to handle matters properly and nipping two impending disasters in the bud. That should earn her a bit of merit.

However, this low-margin, high-volume marketing method didn't quite suit her current survival status.

She couldn't cut down on expenses; she could only generate new revenue sources.

As her gaze swept across her surroundings, her eyes instantly lit up.

Ah, the kid with the purple smoke is here again!

That wasn't the main point. The main point was the unlucky fellow next to him with blackened *Yintang* (space between the eyebrows). Clad in brocade and crowned with jade, he was the Grand Princess's only beloved son, Chi Ge.

A wealth-delivering boy!

A live one!

Jiang Miao enthusiastically greeted Mo Beishu, "Young master, I didn't lie to you, did I? The person you were looking for has been found!"

Mo Beishu nodded slightly.

"Your name is Jiang Miao?"

Jiang Miao clicked her tongue, looking full of admiration, "You even knew that? The young master is truly brilliant, knowledgeable, and outstanding..."

Chi Ge sneered, "Didn't your teacher ever teach you that idioms aren't used so carelessly?"

Jiang Miao smiled and said, "He taught them. He just didn't teach me."

Chi Ge: "..." You're still proud of that?

Mo Beishu couldn't help laughing, imagining a scene where a tutor was so angered by Jiang Miao that he had to press his temples.

Chi Ge let out a "hum" and said dismissively, "No wonder you were driven out of the Marquis Xuan-Yuan's estate. Right now, people in the Jiang family probably need an extra bowl of rice to celebrate."

Jiang Miao crossed her legs and remained unconcerned, "They're celebrating too early."

Realizing that Chi Ge was no match for Jiang Miao in a war of words, Mo Beishu timely cut into their conversation, "Please read my fortune again..."

Jiang Miao waved her hand, "I know you're in a hurry, but don't be in a hurry. The time hasn't come yet."

Saying this, she pointed at Chi Ge and said, "He's the one who needs his fortune read."

Chi Ge gave her a contemptuous look, "Not doing it. The Master does not speak of strange phenomena and chaotic gods; this young master doesn't believe in these things, and definitely doesn't believe you!"

Jiang Miao shook her head in disapproval and said:

"The Master didn't speak of them, meaning he didn't talk about them, not that he didn't believe them. Do you think someone would tell you if something good is coming?"

"Slick-tongued and deceitful!"

"Thank you for the compliment. I'll give you a discount, the total is one hundred taels," Jiang Miao said briskly. "Don't go to the outskirts within three days, and don't touch inexplicable things. Otherwise, the next time you come looking for me, it will be one thousand taels."

Chi Ge's handsome face darkened instantly.

"Can you not understand human speech? I said I'm not doing it!"

"That's right, you don't count, I count."

Jiang Miao wore a mischievous look, her gaze tinged with a bit of gloating.

Chi Ge was so angry he gnashed his teeth, "This young master is going to go to the outskirts just to spite you, and I'm going to touch inexplicable things! Do you really think you can swindle this young master's silver?"

Still as foolish as when he was a child, truly adorable.

Jiang Miao clapped her hands, "I just admire your rebellious spirit!"

In a fit of anger, Chi Ge grabbed Mo Beishu and pulled him away, "Let's go!"

Mo Beishu gave Jiang Miao a deep look and followed him.

Deep down, he was half-skeptical of Jiang Miao's words. With a solemn expression, he advised Chi Ge, "Better safe than sorry. It's only three days, don't leave the city."

Chi Ge dismissed it with disdain, "Whether I go or not depends on my mood."

Mo Beishu wanted to advise him further, but upon second thought, this was precisely an opportunity to test whether Jiang Miao was talking nonsense.

Since Jiang Miao had said that, it meant that even if something happened, she would be able to resolve it. At worst, he would just pay her a thousand taels, his aunt had plenty of money.

If she was talking nonsense, then naturally nothing would happen.

Prompted by a slight twinge of conscience, he pondered for a moment and said, "Haven't you had your eye on that dagger of mine for a long time? I'll give it to you."

Chi Ge's displeasure instantly vanished into thin air. Excitedly hooking his arm around Mo Beishu's neck, he said, "I knew Second Brother is good to me!"

...

Jiang Miao touched her rumbling stomach and quickly cast a fortune for herself.

Though it might not necessarily be accurate, there was a chance it would be.

The copper coins spun around on the stall board for a long time before stopping simultaneously, overlapping without the slightest discrepancy. Both sides faced upwards.

"Oh, there's income today after all. I suppose I can stay hungry for now."

A few hours later, Jiang Miao called out weakly, "Fortune telling, ten copper coins a fortune, no charge if it's inaccurate."

However, reality went against the divination; not a single soul patronized her the entire afternoon.

Passersby at most glanced at her curiously, with looks resembling those given to an idiot.

She had to admit, the people of the capital had overly strong anti-fraud awareness!

Seeing that the sun was setting, Jiang Miao decided not to grind it out any longer and packed up her stall to return to the inn.

Just as she stepped into the inn, she caught sight of a familiar figure.

It was none other than Jiang Huai, the third young master of the Jiang family.

As the former siblings' gazes locked, Jiang Huai's previously calm expression instantly turned fierce.

Pointing at Jiang Miao, he accused, "What did you say to Hua'er that day? You made her cry."

chapters.title: I have a different kind of fireworks
chapters.content:
Jiang Miao uttered an "oh," and replied, "Even if your Jiang family begged me on their knees, I wouldn't step foot into the Jiang family estate again! There you have it, word for word."

Clenching his fists, Jiang Huai walked toward her, gritting his teeth:

"Why didn't I know you were so vicious before? Hua'er even begs our parents to bring you back to the estate every day. Not only do you show no gratitude, but you also humiliated her in front of outsiders. Do you have any idea how heartbroken she is?"

"No idea."

Jiang Miao stared at his fists, pondering which posture would look better when she lay down later.

Her small goal depended entirely on this fall.

The black Qi on this fellow's *Yintang* had deepened a bit more, and his physiognomy really had changed. The once smoothly contoured cheekbones now protruded slightly; if things continued to develop this way, it was destined to be a death by unnatural causes!

Jiang Huai cast a look of disgust at her, suddenly turned around, and shouted at the innkeeper:

"This person is a swindler driven away by the Marquis Xuan-Yuan's estate. How dare you accommodate someone of such wretched character?"

The innkeeper looked surprised, "It's not like she didn't pay."

Jiang Huai choked, pulled out a fifty-tael silver ingot, and slammed it onto the counter, "Kick her out, unless you want to offend our Marquis's estate."

The innkeeper's eyes lit up as he rubbed his hands and looked at Jiang Miao, "Would you like to pay extra rent?"

Jiang Miao was dumbfounded, "Lining up to fleece me?" I respect you as a man!

Before the innkeeper could react, she raised her voice and shouted at the top of her lungs, "Innkeeper, the skin on your face is dark and scorched, your fingers are swollen and your footsteps are unsteady, the so-called bedroom whirlwind, done in under a minute..."

"Oh, dear lord~" The innkeeper immediately leaped over and clamped a hand over her mouth. Although he didn't understand what "a minute" meant, he fully understood that she was exposing his erectile dysfunction.

Didn't he have any pride?

Turning a fierce glare toward Jiang Huai, the innkeeper waved his hand impatiently and snapped, "The Marquis Xuan-Yuan is hot stuff? Why don't you go find out who our master is!"

Jiang Huai's expression stiffened. Suddenly remembering something, he left a parting threat, "Jiang Miao, you just wait!"

Then, clenching his fists in frustration, he stormed off.

Only then did the innkeeper let go of his hand, bowing and scraping as he said to Jiang Miao, "Ancestor, would ten days of free rent suffice?" Please, stop blabbing!

Jiang Miao stroked her chin, staring at him maliciously, thinking that even if her divination failed her eight times, it was bound to be right twice.

Look at that, business had arrived!

"Fifty taels, and I can have you regain your manly vigor today!"

Jiang Miao lifted her chin proudly.

Naturally, the innkeeper didn't believe it. Thanks to his master's connections, he had even consulted the chief imperial physician of the Imperial Hospital, and it hadn't been cured.

Even if this little brat had some eye for spotting chronic ailments, could she be better than an imperial physician?

This was clearly extortion!

He jumped up and pointed at her nose, "Fifty taels, why don't you just go rob someone?"

Jiang Miao shrugged and spread her hands, "Aren't I doing that right now?"

The innkeeper was so angry he wanted to chase her out, but fearing she would go outside and run her mouth, he had to swallow his pride and say, "One tael, consider it hush money. I advise you to take it and quit while you're ahead!"

"Hey, looking down on people, are you?" Jiang Miao slammed her signboard cloth banner onto the counter. "If I can't cure you, you can tear down my signboard!"

The innkeeper rolled his eyes all the way to the back of his head, "I gave you that canvas banner in the first place."

"Let's not sweat the small details. How about this, I'll treat you first, and you can pay me after you're cured?" Jiang Miao said with absolute confidence, "One centipede, thirty snakegourd seeds, eight qian of licorice, one liang of fresh wolfberry leaves, one pair of sheep kidneys, six qian of epimedium..."

Upon hearing this, the innkeeper thought: aren't these the exact ingredients in the prescription given by the imperial physician?

How did she know?

Could she actually understand medicine?

Yet he heard Jiang Miao continue, "That's the prescription the best doctors around can come up with, and as for the effect... well, it leaves much to be desired. But I am different."

The innkeeper couldn't help asking, "How are you different?"

"I have a different kind of fireworks!" Jiang Miao grabbed the innkeeper by the arm, "Today, I'll broaden your horizons!"

Before the innkeeper could react, an incense stick appeared out of thin air in her hand.

With a swift rub of her slender fingers against the tip of the incense, it ignited.

The innkeeper's eyes nearly popped out of his skull, what kind of ungodly sorcery was this?

With lightning speed, Jiang Miao thrust the burning tip of the incense straight against a spot an inch below his navel, right through his clothes.

"Ah..."

The innkeeper let out a miserable scream.

It wasn't from pain; it was from sheer terror.

The next instant, however, he felt a wave of warmth surge from bottom to top, circulate through his body, and finally settle back below his navel. Instantly, his mind snapped alert.

He felt as though he had an endless reservoir of energy.

Jiang Miao blew on the incense, and it extinguished.

"There, you can go test it out now."

The innkeeper dazed out, "That's it?"

Jiang Miao waved her hand, "Hurry back and forth, I'll be waiting for your silver... I mean, your good news."

The innkeeper couldn't quite believe it, but how was he to explain this youthful vigor?

Unable to suppress his excitement, he complained discontentedly, "How can you call a thing like this 'hurry'?"

Leaving behind instructions to "Keep an eye on the shop for me,"

He eagerly bolted out the door, literally running.

Jiang Miao leisurely seated herself on the counter and instructed the waiter, who had been hiding in the back hall watching the commotion, "Boil up two taels of noodles for me, and add extra vinegar."

The waiter: "..."

However, Jiang Miao had underestimated the innkeeper's competitive spirit. Having endured complaints from his wife countless times over the years, how could he not thoroughly subdue her now that he had made a comeback?

Consequently, it wasn't until the dawn of the next day that Jiang Miao saw the innkeeper return.

As soon as he stepped through the door, he bowed deeply to her, "Many thanks, Divine Doctor, for helping me reclaim my status."

Seeing the lingering satisfaction all over his face, Jiang Miao twitched the corner of her mouth.

It seemed she might have over-treated him a little...

Coughing lightly, she said, "No need for thanks, just as long as the money is paid."

Hearing this, the innkeeper looked at her with a somewhat embarrassed expression and stammered, "Treating this illness over the years meant I really haven't saved up that much silver. Could I pay you five taels first?"

Terrified that Jiang Miao would think he was reneging on the debt, he hurriedly added, "In a few days, I'll ask the master to advance my end-of-year bonus, and I'll definitely pay you the rest in full."

Jiang Miao swept her gaze across his face twice, thinking to herself that she had been careless and forgotten to read his physiognomy beforehand.

This fellow truly didn't have much family wealth.

With no other choice, she said, "Fine. But you'll be responsible for my meals these next few days."

The innkeeper readily agreed, it was just an extra mouth to feed, hardly a problem.

Having resolved her food and lodging, Jiang Miao resumed her habit of lying flat and slacking off in her room. Once she finished reading her storybooks, she would send the waiter out on errands to buy her new ones...

The true ideal of life was to have zero cares in the world while at home.

All success was the result of acquired effort, so today and tomorrow, she would simply rest.

With the innkeeper taking care of her feeding, she would somehow manage to live long enough to remember who she was. The City God would most likely tell her the truth; if he didn't, she'd beat him until he did!

Three days later, Jiang Miao stayed up late finishing a storybook, dreaming she had transformed into an emissary of light propagating love and justice, transmigrating into a novel to thrash scumbags, only to be awakened by a flurry of pounding on her door.

Jiang Miao rolled herself up in the quilt, burying her head to ignore it. As long as I fall asleep fast enough, the dream can continue...

"Master Jiang, save me!"

The person outside was frantic, hammering on the door as if on the verge of tears.

With a *swish*, Jiang Miao yanked off the quilt, sat up, and roared:

"Without a hundred taels, this matter isn't over!"

With that, she slipped into her clothes and went to open the door.

The moment she laid eyes on the visitor, her eyes narrowed into happy slits.

"My friend, are you here to deliver money to me?"

Covered in sweat, Shen Nan panicked, "Quick, Master Jiang, come with me, something's terribly wrong with the Heir!"

chapters.title: Enduring It Means Making Another Two Thousand Five Hundred
chapters.content:
It took Jiang Miao a beat to realize he was talking about Chi Ge.

Originally, according to the ancestral system of the Dafeng Dynasty, the children of the Grand Princess were considered imperial relatives and held no titles they could inherit.

However, this Grand Princess was an exception. Half of the prosperity and glory the Dafeng Dynasty enjoyed today was thanks to her.

Therefore, the Emperor had conferred the title of Heir upon her son, with a princedom to follow in the future.

Jiang Miao chuckled and held up a single finger.

Shen Nan understood instantly. "One thousand taels! Her Royal Highness the Grand Princess has agreed!"

Only then was Jiang Miao satisfied as she called the servant to fetch water for washing and grooming.

Shen Nan was burning with anxiety, but he didn't dare to rush her.

Watching Jiang Miao's lazy and unhurried movements, for some reason, the impatience in his heart gradually subsided.

By the time they reached the Grand Princess's Mansion, two hours had already passed.

The washing didn't take long, but Jiang Miao insisted on taking a detour outside the city, and even mischievously snapped off two willow branches to drag back with her.

Whenever asked, her answer was that mortals shouldn't pry into the affairs of immortals.

What could Shen Nan do?

His master had given strict orders: he must be respectful and polite to the little scam artist, commit no rudeness, and make sure to invite her to save the Heir.

And he had even called her a master...

This was Jiang Miao's first time facing the Grand Princess at close range.

She couldn't help taking a few extra glances.

A broad forehead, a prominent nasal bridge, and full cheekbones.

The picturesque brows and eyes did not convey gentleness and charm, but rather a tenacity and composure rarely seen in ordinary women.

At this moment, when her beloved son's life was hanging by a thread, she still maintained a calm expression and relaxed features, exuding a natural, unforced resilience, as if nothing in this world could knock her down.

What a domineering female CEO.

"Slurp~"

Jiang Miao quietly swallowed her saliva, almost wanting to rush over and hug her thighs. "Big sister, let's cuddle. Big sister, please keep me."

The Grand Princess had already learned about Jiang Miao from Mo Beishu. Although she was mentally prepared, she hadn't expected her to look so... frivolous.

The cross-body bag made of various patches of fabric hanging across her shoulder gave her the aura of a drifter with no fixed home.

It was completely impossible to connect her with the neatly behaved young girl sitting upright before the palace hall in her memory.

Suddenly recalling something, a trace of warmth surfaced in her eyes.

Right, how could a little girl bold enough to steal His Imperial Majesty's koi fish ever truly abide by the rules?

She raised a hand, and a maid behind her stepped forward holding a tray filled with pure white silver ingots.

In a tone without a single ripple, she said, "Save the Heir, and all of these are yours."

Jiang Miao smiled shyly. "Look at what you're saying. Even if there were no money, I would still save him..."

The Grand Princess also smiled. "If you can't save him, I'm afraid I won't be able to control myself from charging you with the crime of swindling and deception!"

The smile on Jiang Miao's face vanished instantly. "Five thousand taels!"

Shen Nan gasped sharply. *Ancestor, you really must have a death wish!*

How dare you sit and raise the price on the spot right in front of the Grand Princess, whose power and status were second only to the reigning Emperor!

Even Mo Beishu, who was always composed and self-contained, twitched the corner of his cheek.

He finally understood a little why Chi Ge held such deep resentment toward her...

Just when the two of them thought the Grand Princess was going to get angry, they heard her laugh heartily.

"Very well! Only capable people are qualified to bargain with me. Now, let me see your skills!"

Jiang Miao never went against money, nor did she hold a grudge over the threat the other party had just made.

If she had the other party's power and wealth, she would act so arrogantly that even her grandmaster would want to come down from the heavens and strangle her!

The tea isn't bitter, the heart isn't blocked, endure it and make another twenty-five hundred!

She immediately said briskly, "Lead the way!"

As expected of the Grand Princess's beloved son, Chi Ge's bedchamber was larger than the main hall of the Jiang family mansion, in fact, it was overly large, retaining no wind or gathering auspicious energy at all.

At this moment, three elderly imperial physicians stood with hands folded by Chi Ge's bed, their faces full of sorrow.

The Emperor had already given his word: if they couldn't cure the Heir, they would be bringing their heads to see him.

One of the elderly physicians was none other than Su Yue'er's grandfather, the Chief Physician of the Imperial Hospital, Dr. Su.

The day Su Yue'er bit her tongue, she went home and wrote a lengthy, sweeping "declaration" accusing Jiang Miao, every word dripping with blood!

The Su family had originally planned to report her to the authorities and send Jiang Miao to prison on fraud charges.

However, Su Yue'er wrote a passionate letter in blood stating that she wanted revenge with her own hands to vent the frustration in her heart, which was why Jiang Miao had been left at large for a few days.

Since the Su family walked in the same circles as the Marquis of Xuanyuan's residence, he recognized Jiang Miao.

He had never expected that the "expert" whom Commandery Prince Ye claimed he was going to invite to treat the Heir would turn out to be Jiang Miao.

Seeing her now, an immediate sense of excitement washed over him, *there is a path to heaven which you refuse to walk, and no door to hell yet you crash right in.*

It was one thing to swindle ordinary folks on the street, but how dare she come and pull her charlatan tricks in front of the Grand Princess! Today, he would rid the Jiang family of this scourge!

Stepping forward righteously, he pointed a finger at Jiang Miao and proclaimed sternly:

"Reporting to Your Royal Highness the Grand Princess, this person is the abandoned daughter of the Marquis of Xuanyuan's estate. She impersonated the Marquis's legitimate daughter, and after her ruse was exposed, she was driven out of the family. Now she roams the streets under the guise of fortune-telling to swindle the hard-earned money of commoners. Please, Your Highness, rid the people of this pest!"

"And restore a bright and clear sky to the capital!" This line was added by Jiang Miao herself, who felt that without it, her wickedness wouldn't be fully reflected.

Dr. Su: ?

The Grand Princess: "..."

Glancing indifferently at Dr. Su, she said, "Are you implying that I am a fool?" An oppressive aura belonging to those in supreme power radiated from her entire being.

Dr. Su's spine curved instantly, and sweat broke out on his forehead. He stammered in a rush, "Your Highness, you've misunderstood, this humble subject..."

"Since you know you are a humble subject, then stop talking." The Grand Princess impatiently cut him off.

Based solely on the fact that Mo Beishu had told her three days ago how Jiang Miao had warned Chi Ge not to wander around or touch inexplicable things, she was willing to take this gamble.

This old man couldn't cure her son, yet he still came to block her son's path to survival!

Jiang Miao put on a smug little expression and made a mocking *bleh* face at Dr. Su.

Sparks of fury practically shot out of the old man's eyes, but constrained by his status (and fear of the Grand Princess), he held his breath and remained silent.

He wanted to see how this stinking girl was going to clean up this mess later!

And when the time came, he would stomp on her hard!
