Seeing that he wouldn't speak, Jiang Miao lost interest and turned her attention to her major client.

Chi Ge lay flat on his back on a gold-traced, large wooden bed intricately carved with auspicious patterns, his hands crossed over his chest.

His expression was quite serene.

However, Jiang Miao spotted a female figure right beside him at a glance, leaning her head on her elbow and gazing foolishly down at him.

If not for the fact that the flesh on the woman's face was almost completely rotted away and her eyeballs were dangling loosely as if they might drop at any moment, the scene would have been quite heartwarming...

This was a ghost, visible only to Jiang Miao.

She asked, "How long has he been in this condition?"

The Grand Princess's voice came out gloomily from behind her.

"Two days and two nights. He hasn't moved an inch, and no matter how anyone calls him, he won't wake up. The physicians say he must have suffered some sort of trauma and is unwilling to wake up on his own."

"If he weren't still breathing, I would have already started ordering a coffin for him."

Jiang Miao nodded. "It certainly sounds like quite a trauma."

Everyone else: ?

Then, to their astonishment, they watched her reach out and grab thin air beside Chi Ge as if she had caught something, before rolling and kneading it into a ball.

Immediately afterward, she looked left and right, very casually picked up a teacup, opened the lid, and stuffed the ball inside.

Since they couldn't see the female ghost, they only thought that while Jiang Miao's series of actions flowed like water, she certainly looked gravely mentally ill.

The Grand Princess held back her tongue and instinctively glanced toward the physicians: *for this kind of condition in the little girl, do the physicians have any solutions?*

---

chapters.title: You Childhood Nightmare is Back Again
chapters.content:
Only Mo Beishu's eyes flashed with a sharp light, as if he had guessed something.

Jiang Miao fished out a piece of yellow paper and a white bristle brush from her patchwork beggar bag, licked the tip of her brush with her tongue, and began waving the brush to draw with the fluidity of a dragon in flight.

As she dropped the final stroke, a flash of golden light flickered and vanished, too fast for anyone to capture.

Shen Nan rubbed his eyes. *An illusion, it must be an illusion!*

He instinctively covered his mouth, caught in a tangle of inner conflict: *The little scam artist is fooling people again, should I expose her?*

But she called him friend, y'all...

If the Grand Princess got angry, the little scam artist would lose her head.

And he only had this one friend.

Jiang Miao shook the freshly minted talisman in her hand, and the talisman actually burst into self-combustion, making Shen Nan forget his internal struggle entirely.

The Grand Princess remained calm and collected; petty tricks like this were not something she hadn't seen before.

Jiang Miao looked around the room, finding no maids or attendants anywhere, and smiled sweetly at a kind-looking elderly physician. "Grandpa, would you be so kind as to fetch me a bowl of water?"

The old physician was startled, then suddenly remembered something and asked vigilantly, "What are you going to do?"

"Drink the talisman water, and he'll wake up," Jiang Miao replied.

"Absurd!" The old physician rebuked with a darkened face.

He had tolerated her previous mumbo-jumbo, but he could not tolerate using a charlatan's street tricks to trifle with the Heir's precious body.

So angry his facial features distorted, he snapped, "You're just messing around!"

Another physician disdained to speak with Jiang Miao directly. Instead, he bowed to the Grand Princess with a solemn expression and said:

"Your Highness, the few of us have practiced medicine for decades, and we are certain the Heir has merely suffered some sort of shock. Given time, he will wake up on his own. We must never allow such an unlearned, incompetent charlatan to ravage the precious body of the Heir."

Dr. Su kept a reserved silence; he had a mouthpiece!

The Grand Princess pondered for a moment. "Only the living possess a precious body; once dead, it's just a pile of white bones. I have an impatient temperament and cannot afford to 'give it time'."

Physicians: "..."

Dr. Su exchanged glances with the other two, signaling them to endure. When that stinking girl's true colors were exposed, that would be their best moment to beat a dog that had fallen into the water.

The Grand Princess walked straight over to the crescent table beneath the window, pulled out a blooming white bellflower from a white jade carved vase, and handed the vase to Jiang Miao.

"The water in here is changed daily; make do with it."

Jiang Miao: *...Actually, you really don't have to be in such a rush...* After all, that's your biological son.

The Grand Princess waved a hand. "It's fine, this child has been tough as nails since he was little."

Since the boy's own mother didn't mind, Jiang Miao naturally went along with it.

After pouring out half the water, she shoved the talisman paper inside and shook it vigorously.

Then she walked up to Chi Ge, grabbed his jaw in a tight grip, and brutally forced the flower-infused talisman water down his throat...

Strangely enough, not a single drop of the water was wasted; it all went straight into Chi Ge's stomach.

Watching this scene, the Grand Princess felt a subtle surge of excitement.

Her son had been unconscious for two days, his teeth clenched shut so tightly that not even liquid medicine could be forced down, yet he swallowed this talisman water quite happily.

This girl Jiang Miao had been able to manage him since childhood; it seemed she had found the right person this time!

Jiang Miao muttered incantations under her breath, speaking at lightning speed, softly and indistinctly, making everyone assume she was chanting some spell.

In reality, what she was saying was: *"Didn't expect it, did you, brat? Your childhood nightmare is back again!"*

Having finished her muttering, she smacked Chi Ge right across the forehead, producing a crisp slapping sound.

Chi Ge's fair forehead instantly flushed bright red over a large patch.

"Audacious!" The elderly physicians cried out in unison, their voices cracking with indignation.

Not only was this little scam artist playing the ghost-whisperer to fool Her Royal Highness the Grand Princess, but she actually dared to strike the Heir's head!

This was outright rebellion!

Jiang Miao turned back to look at them and smiled amiably. "I'm done letting it out."

One of the elderly physicians pointed a trembling finger at her and spoke to the Grand Princess in grief and indignation:

"Please, Your Highness, punish this frantic scoundrel for the crime of great disrespect!"

The Grand Princess, however, ignored them completely and strode over to Chi Ge's bed in a few swift steps.

She thought she had just seen her son's long eyelashes twitch...

Sure enough, Chi Ge slowly opened his eyes, his attractive peach-blossom eyes filled with bewilderment.

The next second, with a sharp shriek of "Ah!", he sat bolt upright and scrambled backward as if he had seen a ghost.

Glaring at Jiang Miao, he roared, "Don't you come any closer!"

Jiang Miao didn't lower herself to his level. She had never met someone so timid yet so holding of grudges!

With an air of unconcern, she stepped aside to leave the space to the Grand Princess, deeply concealing her merits and fame.

As for the three elderly physicians, they were so shocked they doubted their entire lives.

Dr. Su was grinding his back teeth almost to dust.

*How on earth can this stinking girl be so lucky... just happening to hit the exact moment the Heir woke up by himself.*

The Grand Princess touched Chi Ge's reddened forehead and asked softly, "My son, does it hurt?"

Chi Ge nodded with a wronged expression. "It hurts."

The Grand Princess sighed. "It's good that it hurts. Remember to be polite the next time you see Miao-miao, understand?"

Wait... *Miao-miao*?

She hit him, and yet she wanted *him* to be polite?

Was *she* polite?!

Chi Ge was speechless. He pointed at Jiang Miao and demanded, "Why is she here?"

Jiang Miao chuckled. "Your mother spent five thousand taels to invite me. Isn't that a surprise?"

Chi Ge had only been trapped and unable to wake up by the female ghost; his mind had remained clear all along, and he immediately recalled Jiang Miao's earlier words: *"Otherwise, next time you come looking for me, it'll cost a thousand taels."*

He understood more or less what was going on.

His face turned a mixture of green and white instantly, the look in his eyes akin to wanting to devour her alive. He gritted his teeth and said, "How dare you arbitrarily raise the price!"

"You possess a body worth ten thousand gold, and I only asked for half of that. That's already a friendly discount," Jiang Miao replied with a righteous and natural expression.

Suddenly remembering something, she turned to the Grand Princess and added, "Oh right, the five thousand taels I mentioned? That's in gold."

The Grand Princess smiled as she refused, "It's too late for supplementary explanations now."

Jiang Miao wasn't flustered in the least. She raised her chin toward Chi Ge.

"Ask him what he ran into."

Hearing this, Chi Ge's expression shifted. He immediately collapsed straight back onto the bed, clutched his forehead, and declared, "Mother, my head hurts, I can't remember anything."

No one knew a son better than his mother; the moment Chi Ge raised his tail, the Grand Princess knew whether he was going to defecate or urinate. At a glance right now, she knew things were far from simple.

Her image of a gentle mother vanished instantly. She commanded sternly, "Speak!"

Chi Ge closed his eyes and played dead, the tips of his ears burning red.

Talking was out of the question, he would rather die than talk about it in this lifetime.

The Grand Princess's fists hardened...

Jiang Miao, being very understanding, stepped in to block the hot-tempered mother and tried to persuade her with kind words: "Calm down, please don't lower yourself to the level of a delinquent bear child."

The bear child: ? *Is she talking about me?*

The Grand Princess changed her expression in a second, reaching out to stroke Jiang Miao's head affectionately. "That's a good word, very vivid. Miao-miao is truly clever."

*You could call me meow-meow all you want,* Jiang Miao thought to herself, *but you're not getting away without paying a single coin of that five thousand taels of gold.*

She turned to the three elderly physicians and said, "Your Highness, why don't you have them step outside? What happens next is going to be quite terrifying!"

Before the Grand Princess could speak, the three elderly physicians stubbornly shook their heads. *Want to chase them away so she can continue swindling Her Royal Highness the Grand Princess?*

Not a chance! They were fiercely loyal ministers!

Dr. Su straightened his back and proclaimed resolutely, "This old man is not afraid!"

*I want to see what other tricks you're going to pull. With this old man's piercing eyes of discernment, can't I see right through your parlor tricks?!*

chapters.title: This little scoundrel is done for!
chapters.content:
“I’m not worried that you’ll be scared; I simply don’t want to show you,” Jiang Miao said, with the deadpan ability to piss people to death.

The veteran imperial physicians: “You! You! You!”

The Grand Princess laughed good-naturedly to smooth things over. “Alright, Miao’miao, let them stay. It’ll broaden their horizons.”

Jiang Miao rolled her eyes. “It’s not out of the question. It’s just that if they get scared and faint later, I’ll have to administer first aid.”

“This palace will pay.” The Grand Princess was very cooperative and felt a bit sorry for Jiang Miao.

She was originally a young noble miss pampered in the Marquis’s residence, but now she was reduced to such a pitiful state of having no fixed abode and struggling for her next meal. That Marquis Xuanyuan was far too cruel.

After all, they had raised her for fourteen years; even a cat or a dog wouldn’t be thrown away so ruthlessly, right?

If she had known earlier, she would have taken Miao’miao to be her own daughter back then, at least it would have been nice to have someone keep her son in line every now and then.

Jiang Miao was satisfied.

She fished two sheets of yellow paper out of her bag and began to draw effortlessly, without the slightest bit of strain... No matter how you looked at it, it looked thoroughly unreliable.

Then, with a flick of her small hand, the talisman paper once again spontaneously combusted without wind, turning to ashes in the blink of an eye.

This time was different from the last. Once the talisman paper burned down, the room instantly turned chillingly cold.

Even Shen Nan, who had the sturdiest physique, couldn’t help but shiver.

Immediately following this, Jiang Miao opened the teacup containing the female ghost and shouted, “Get out here!”

Her expression was detached, yet her voice carried a dense, murderous intent that made people’s hearts pound with fear and caused them to hold their breath involuntarily.

Upon hearing her voice alone, the female ghost began to tremble, her spiritual body destabilizing.

She drifted out in a crooked, unsteady fashion.

Everyone present was dumbfounded, hardly believing their own eyes.

Only Chi Ge rolled his eyes back, desperately wishing he could faint dead away.

Covering his face, he wailed in his heart: It’s over, his reputation and chastity were about to be ruined!

Mo Beishu was so shocked that he took a large stride forward. “There really are ghosts in this world?!”

Aside from Jiang Miao, who could see the female ghost’s terrifying true form, everyone else saw a completely different sight.

The female ghost was draped in a translucent pink gossamer, her exquisite and graceful figure faintly discernible, making her appear all the more alluring.

Her countenance was stunning and vibrant, and at this moment, she knelt before Jiang Miao with tears welling in her eyes, her shoulders trembling slightly, looking utterly pitiful.

The veteran imperial physicians struggled to tear their gazes away from the female ghost. They tried to cover their faces, but couldn’t cover their eyes, it was simply too indecent to behold!

Jiang Miao looked down at her from on high. “Speak. What have you been up to?”

The female ghost didn’t know who Jiang Miao was, but her experience as a ghost told her she had run into a true master this time.

She had an instinctive feeling that if she dared to deceive this person, she would die a particularly miserable death, a true death this time, the kind where nothing of her soul would be left.

She could only say timidly:

“This humble servant has drifted for many years and was truly unbearably lonely. By pure chance, I ran into the Heir Apparent, fell in love with him at first sight, and formed a bond with him.”

Hearing this, the Grand Princess snapped her head around to glare at her own son, a mix of fury and disgust on her face.

This little scoundrel really was done for!

Chi Ge had already burrowed his entire body beneath the covers, roaring internally: *Jiang Miao, this young master and you are irreconcilable!*

A human and a ghost?!

Jiang Miao’s small face was sallow and grim; she had never heard of a human-ghost conjugal union before.

Suppressing her excitement, she put on a beastly-in-human-guise expression.

She leisurely seated herself on a chair and said coldly:

“Tell me in detail. What were the specifics? How did the process go?”

The female ghost wore a mournful expression, casting a resentful, cautious glance at Jiang Miao.

*If you had arrived just a tiny bit later, there would have been specifics!* she thought.

Regretfully, she said, “The details hadn’t had time to unfold yet. As for the process, it was just this humble servant and the Heir Apparent going from acquaintance to mutual understanding. We were just about to get to the main event when you interrupted us.”

*So it’s my fault?*

“You even know how to build emotional attachment...” Jiang Miao was utterly disgusted. *All the good fun was delayed by you.*

The female ghost said with a hint of haughtiness, “This humble servant is not some superficial person who only knows how to enjoy physical pleasures.”

The Grand Princess raged, “You’re a ghost!”

Jiang Miao hadn’t heard the juicy parts, which left her slightly displeased.

She let out a cold snort. “Humans and ghosts walk different paths. Do you know that if he doesn’t wake up today, he will die?”

The female ghost widened her eyes in envy. “Ah? Once he dies, will there be lots of incense, candles, and paper ingots for him?”

“Snap~”

A willow branch materialized out of thin air in Jiang Miao’s hand and lashed against the female ghost’s body.

The female ghost let out a shrill, miserable scream. Her spiritual body visibly paled by two shades, and she collapsed to the ground in pain, twitching.

Jiang Miao stared at her with fierce eyes and said icily:

“So this was what you were plotting all along!”

Enduring the severe pain, the female ghost struggled to climb up and groveled before Jiang Miao, her expression innocent and foolishly cute, her attitude humble yet her tone a bit stubborn.

“Great Immortal, spare my life! This humble servant truly didn’t know the Heir Apparent would die. I’m really not the superficial, vanity-driven sort.”

Seeing that she didn’t seem to be faking it, Jiang Miao shook the willow branch in her hand. “Then start from the beginning. What kind of person were you in life? Why didn’t you go reincarnate after death?”

The female ghost hastily agreed.

As it turned out, she had been the top courtesan of the most flourishing brothel in the capital, and her name was Yingge.

Though trapped in a brothel, she refused to bow her head to fate and had always wanted to find an opportunity to escape this fiery pit.

She originally thought that once she saved up enough silver, she could redeem herself. But the brothel madam was unwilling to let go of this cash cow and demanded an exorbitant sum, an amount she could never earn in a lifetime.

Filled with utter despair, Yingge had spent a period in deep depression.

The turning point came a month later.

A dashing young scholar came to the brothel and took a fancy to her.

The young man was handsome and sweet-talking; after a few visits, he actually made Yingge fall in love with him.

What followed was a clichéd, melodramatic plot.

The young man swore with absolute certainty that once he passed the imperial examinations and gained an official post, he would pressure the madam and redeem her.

Yingge believed him, even subsidizing his studies with her own savings.

A year and a half later, the young man came to her in high spirits, announcing that he had placed in the top tier of the imperial examinations and would soon receive an official title to fly away with her wing-to-wing.

However, he urgently needed a large sum of silver for bribes in order to secure a post with real political power.

Jiang Miao’s cheek twitched slightly as she was reminded of a common internet joke:

*【I am Qin Shi Huang. I have 100 tons of gold in Xi’an, and I urgently need 2,000 yuan to unfreeze my gold. Transfer it to me, and tomorrow I will make you commander of the three armies.】*

Yingge wept pitifully. “This humble servant suspected nothing. Without even verifying his claims, I gave him my entire life’s savings.”

The result, naturally, was that she was cheated down to her last thread...

She waited and waited, but the young man never came back for her. Instead, she received the madam’s cold announcement that she had been swindled, the young man had long since vanished without a trace, taking her silver with him.

Only then did Yingge realize that the madam had known all along that she was being cheated, yet had looked on with cold indifference, hoping that once she lost her money, she would abandon the thought of leaving.

Yingge hated the madam to the core and refused to entertain any more clients from that day forward.

At first, the madam tried to coax her with kind words to take clients, but when she grew impatient later on, she had her thugs beat Yingge.

Yingge had a stubborn backbone and endured the beating fiercely, only to be beaten to death right then and there...

“This humble servant has suffered terribly...”

Yingge let out a miserable wail and, without warning, reverted to her true form.

Her entire body was covered in rotting flesh that kept sloughing off in chunks.

On her left face, which was missing half a skull, an eyeball popped right out of its socket and rolled in a circle until it stopped at the foot of a veteran imperial physician.

The three veteran imperial physicians were so terrified that their hearts seized; rolling their eyes back, they fell backward in a neat, synchronized row...

***

chapters.title: Both cowardly and lustful
chapters.content:
Shen Nan scrambled around frantically, having no idea who he should catch, so he simply pulled his hands back.

*Forget it, I won’t catch any of them. Offending anyone right now is a bad idea.*

Yingge immediately drifted over, picked up her eyeball, and jammed it back into her eye socket, transforming back into a beauty in the blink of an eye.

She obediently returned to kneel before Jiang Miao, her face plastered with a flattering expression.

Jiang Miao suppressed her twitching eyelids, not daring to laugh out loud.

This female ghost was quite something; seeing that the imperial physicians hadn’t fainted from the first scare, she had deliberately frightened them out cold just to help her earn money.

The Grand Princess: “...”

Flauntingly making her spend money like this right in front of her, did she really think she wouldn’t notice?

True to the saying, the dead were to be respected above all else!

Jiang Miao temporarily ignored the imperial physicians; they weren’t going to die anytime soon.

Putting on a stern face, she asked seriously: “Then why did you latch onto the Heir Apparent? He never harmed you. If you want revenge, you should go find that madam and the scoundrel who swindled your money.”

Flames of hatred ignited in Yingge’s eyes.

She gnashed her teeth. “That madam somehow found a high-level Taoist priest to cast spells, and this humble servant couldn’t get anywhere near the Wanhua Brothel. As for the man who cheated me, I have no idea where he went. In this vast sea of humanity, where am I supposed to look for him?”

“I was unwilling to go reincarnate. After dodging the grim reapers, I just wandered all over the capital.”

“That day, as usual, I was idling about when I suddenly caught a familiar scent, so I followed it to its source.”

“And there I saw the Heir Apparent holding a sachet I had embroidered during my lifetime and toying with it. I fell in love instantly, this was clearly destiny between the Heir Apparent and me...”

The Grand Princess ground her teeth, strode over to Chi Ge’s bed, and yanked off his blanket.

She roared: “Where is the sachet? Where did you get it?”

Chi Ge swiftly fished a sachet out from beneath the bedcovers and flung it away in disgust...

His peach-blossom eyes were red-rimmed as he looked innocently at his mother. “This child didn’t know it was a ghost thing either.”

Under the tyrannical pressure of the Grand Princess, Chi Ge finally confessed.

After meeting Jiang Miao that day, he had quickly tossed everything she said to the back of his mind.

As fate would have it, on his way home, he happened to pick up this sachet.

Normally, he wouldn’t have deigned to look at such a trinket, let alone pick it up.

However, the sachet happened to be embroidered with two characters: “Yuan Hao,” which was his courtesy name, so he had curiously picked it up.

Yingge’s brows and eyes were full of affection as she cast a flirty wink at the Heir Apparent.

“The Heir Apparent and that heartless wretch share the exact same name. If this isn’t destiny, what is?”

Chi Ge: *Yue~*

Yingge immediately looked deeply wounded, pouting her small mouth. “Earlier, you called me your little darling...”

“Ahhhhh, that’s because you put a dark spell on this young master earlier!”

Chi Ge was terrified out of his wits; if he hadn’t woken up in time, his chastity would have been defiled by a female ghost!

Jiang Miao’s gaze turned cold as she looked at Yingge, who immediately shut her mouth and crouched submissively at Jiang Miao’s feet.

Jiang Miao frowned. “Was this sachet the one you gave to that man?”

Yingge looked immensely proud. “That’s right! He even praised this humble servant for having nimble fin, ”

“Did you ever stop to think how this sachet ended up in the capital?” Jiang Miao interrupted her nonsense.

Yingge replied with a shy expression, “This humble servant did think about it, and originally intended to ask the Heir Apparent where he got it. But the moment I saw the Heir Apparent’s peerless grace, I completely forgot.”

The Grand Princess said uncharitably, “With brains like yours, being cheated out of your money and virtue was hardly undeserved.”

Yingge refused to concede. “You’re the one lacking discernment! I don’t lack brains; my brains were literally beaten into mush...”

The Grand Princess was left between laughter and tears.

Although this female ghost had almost gotten her son killed, she was indeed pitiful. Given her brain capacity, she couldn’t possibly have harbored malicious intent to kill anyone, she was simply, purely lustful.

Pondering for a moment, the Grand Princess said in a deep voice:

“The man who cheated you is named Yuan Hao?”

Yingge nodded. “That’s what he told this humble servant.”

“Where is he from?”

“Qinzhou.”

“Do you know where your corpse was buried?”

Yingge drooped her mouth, aggrieved. “A pauper’s graveyard outside the city walls. It cost this humble servant a lot of effort just to crawl back into town.”

Jiang Miao truly couldn’t bear to listen anymore.

“Can you focus on the main point? Why don’t you hurry up and ask the Grand Princess to help you get revenge?”

Yingge’s eyes lit up. “Ah, such a good thing is possible too?”

Everyone else: “...”

With a mind as carefree as hers, they almost wanted to cheat her of something too.

The Grand Princess turned stern. “According to the laws of our dynasty, even indentured servants and brothel courtesans cannot be killed arbitrarily by their masters or brothel owners. That madam disregarded human life and is utterly odious!”

“Considering that you died an unjust death, this palace will have officials investigate the matter. If what you say is true, those involved will be dealt with according to the law. But as for that man, this palace is powerless to help.”

Since one was willing to beat and the other was willing to take the beating, fraud cases of that nature were difficult to settle.

Yingge gazed blankly at the Grand Princess, a layer of mist welling up in her beautiful eyes.

She desperately wanted to cry, but she had no tears.

After a long while, Yingge lowered her head and pressed a deep kowtow toward the Grand Princess.

Choking up, she said, “You are a good person. If this humble servant has a next life, I will definitely come back to be your daughter-in-law and serve you in your old age.”

“...”

The Grand Princess covered her face with both hands, her temples throbbing with pain.

Jiang Miao chuckled aloud. “You’re quite the dreamer. Stop daydreaming for a moment and settle the score for almost getting someone killed!”

“Ah!”

Yingge knelt and pivoted to face her instead. “Then this humble servant will be your daughter-in-law to serve you in your old age, so can we just forget about settling the score, okay?”

Jiang Miao blinked.

Suddenly, she felt a bit reluctant to let this walking comedy go off to reincarnate.

Keeping such a featherbrained ghost by her side would surely make life very interesting.

Thinking it, she acted on it.

She beckoned to Yingge. “Come here.”

Yingge timidly crawled on her knees closer to Jiang Miao’s side.

Jiang Miao raised her hand and placed it on top of Yingge’s head. Yingge was so terrified her ghostly form froze stiff; the Great Immortal surely didn’t want her to be a daughter-in-law, but she couldn’t very well be a son-in-law either!

*Wuu wuu wuu~~~*

The next instant, however, she felt her spiritual body grow solid and substantial.

The chilling, dreary sensation lingering around her soul vanished in an instant, replaced by a feeling as though she had regained a real body once more, her five senses returning to her.

The most direct sensation was that she could now smell the dragon-saliva incense worn by the men in the room, a scent she hadn’t been able to perceive before.

She couldn’t help but twitch her nose and take a deep sniff. *How truly sexy...*

Noticing that Yingge’s mind had drifted, Jiang Miao tapped the willow branch against the floor and said:

“Now I’ll give you two choices. First, stay by my side. Perhaps you’ll have the chance to accumulate merits, and when you finally go to reincarnate, you’ll, ”

“One! One! This humble servant chooses one!”

Before Jiang Miao could even finish, Yingge displayed a rare flash of wit, decisively choosing to cling to the thigh of a powerhouse.

She wasn’t stupid; a meat pie had been delivered straight to her mouth, how could she not bite down?

The Grand Princess chimed in faintly, “Aren’t you going to be this palace’s daughter-in-law anymore?”

Yingge’s pretty face flushed, and she cast a flirtatious glance at Chi Ge. “If you don’t object, this humble servant wouldn’t mind.”

“I object!”

Chi Ge sprang up from the bed.

Barefoot, he rushed over to Jiang Miao, gritting his teeth as he said, “This young master will pay a thousand liang! Hurry up and get her out of here!”

Jiang Miao instantly grinned from ear to ear. “With pleasure!”

Immediately afterward, Yingge felt her spiritual body pulled uncontrollably into Jiang Miao’s cloth bag.

Jiang Miao extended her palm toward the Grand Princess. “Thank you for your patronage. Six thousand liang, in gold!”

The Grand Princess cried poverty: “Where on earth would this palace have that much gold? Why don’t you just sell me instead?!”

Jiang Miao: ?(?????)?

*Good grief! A dignified Grand Princess is actually acting like a deadbeat!*

*Shut the door and release the ghost!*

chapters.title: Scaring the Old Man to Death!
chapters.content:
Before releasing Yingge, Jiang Miao decided to give the Grand Princess one chance.

"Your properties are everywhere in this Dafeng Dynasty, and yet you claim you don't have any? Are you trying to bully me for being young and ignorant?"

The Grand Princess said indignantly, "I do have plenty of properties, and I earn a fair bit, but I can't help it if my imperial brother is a big spender! Paving roads, building bridges, digging canals, planting trees, rescuing the old and the destitute... it's all my money being spent!"

Only then did Jiang Miao learn that the elderly in the Dafeng Dynasty were cared for, the young were nurtured, and the people were well-fed and clothed, and this domineering female CEO had played a massive part in it.

She immediately felt a surge of respect. "It was my shallowness. Silver it is, then."

The Grand Princess smiled and praised, "Miaomiao is so sensible! I'd be content if my son had even half of your sense."

Chi Ge: "..." May I just ask, was it really necessary to pit us against each other like that?

The Grand Princess pointed at the three imperial physicians who were still unconscious. "Just take these three as a free bonus, and don't make a fuss over a little petty cash."

Jiang Miao waved her small hand and said magnanimously, "A bonus is a bonus!"

She strode over to the three old men and swiftly kicked each of them in the chest with the tip of her foot...

Mo Beishu let out a cry of alarm. "Not so hard." Don't go kicking them... to death...

Her warning came too late.

"Ouch~~~" Physician Su let out a miserable scream and snapped back to consciousness.

The other two old physicians fared better; they didn't scream, presumably because it didn't hurt.

Regaining their wits, the three old men slumped on the ground, huddled together, and looked around vigilantly.

Not seeing that terrifying ghost, Yingge, they let out a long, heavy breath.

Scaring the old man to death!

Physician Su cautiously stole a glance at Jiang Miao, his eyes filled with terror.

Is, is this really the abandoned daughter of the Jiang family?

Why had he never heard before that she could catch ghosts?

No, he had to hurry home and warn Yue'er; this girl was someone they couldn't afford to cross, and they must never provoke her again.

And that Jiang Jinhua from the Jiang family could no longer be associated with either, it was because of Jiang Jinhua that they got mixed up with this girl in the first place!

He should also call off the marriage arrangement with the Jiang family's second young master.

In short, they must not have anything to do with anyone from the Jiang family.

Just in case she unleashed a ghost, his Su family members wouldn't be able to handle the fright.

At this thought, Physician Su scrambled to his feet, hurriedly took his leave of the Grand Princess, Prince Ye, and the Heir, and bolted like a wisp of smoke.

The other two physicians also felt a lingering chill down their spines and hurriedly took their leave as well, figuring they would need at least half a month of rest to recover their vitality.

The Grand Princess didn't dawdle either. She prepared to send people to help Jiang Miao deliver the silver to the inn, but then said with some concern:

"It really is inconvenient for you to live at an inn. With so much silver, it's bound to attract envious eyes. Why don't you..."

Jiang Miao interrupted her, "You don't need to worry, I have my ways."

With that, she waved her small hand, and all six thousand taels of silver actually vanished into her beggar's pouch.

Yet the beggar's pouch still looked utterly flat, as if the silver had just been eaten by it.

Everyone: =0101000004610903·03=0101000004610903·03=0101000004610903·03=0101000004610903·03=0101000004610903·03

An immortal!

No, not an immortal, a deity, immortals aren't this slovenly.

The Grand Princess finished what she was going to say: "I originally intended to gift you a residence, but it seems that won't be necessary."

Jiang Miao: I slipped up. She just wanted to show off, and as a result, she lost a house.

Still, no residence could beat an inn; from there, she could have a clear view of the Jiang residence. Just the other day, she had watched the Jiang family eat whole roasted lamb.

Chi Ge's jaw dropped, unable to close it for a long while.

The moment he snapped it shut, he instantly cast aside past grievances and walked toward Jiang Miao with enthusiastic steps.

He slid to his knees and grabbed her thigh. "Miaomiao, take me as your disciple!"

Jiang Miao kicked him away in disgust.

Every fiber of her being spelled out refusal.

"The spiritual energy here is already thin to begin with. If I teach you, every breath of spiritual energy you take is one less breath for me. Absolutely not."

Chi Ge refused to give up and questioned her:

"Don't you want to spread the Great Dao and absorb more believers?"

Jiang Miao smiled with disdain.

"Spread the Great Dao? Believe if you want, scram if you don't. Don't disrupt Laozi's ascension!"

Grumbling, Chi Ge stood up. His kneeling was all for naught.

Smelly girl!

Just as annoying as when she was a kid!

Jiang Miao's eyes suddenly rolled, and rubbing her chin, she said leisurely:

"However..."

"You name it!"

Chi Ge seamlessly connected and dropped to his knees once more.

The Grand Princess: My fist is acting up again!

Mo Beishu: This Prince also really wants to become a disciple...

Shen Nan: My good friend is a deity, and I'm proud of it!

Amidst Chi Ge's expectant little gaze, Jiang Miao smiled sinisterly:

"The koi fish personally raised by His Majesty carry imperial Qi and are truly supreme nourishing treasures. If you can manage to fetch me a couple, I might just consider it." Taking you as my lackey, that is.

"Four!" Chi Ge held up four fingers. "Two for you, two for me. Back then I took the blame while you ate the meat, this time you must split it evenly with me!"

"Oh?"

Jiang Miao slanted her eyes at him, drawing out the tail end of her tone.

Chi Ge immediately changed his tune, "Five! Three for you, two for me!"

"That's more like it!" You're truly a simpleton (Er), but I am a six (Liu).

Jiang Miao reached out her palm and high-fived him!

The Grand Princess pressed her temples. Why was her head suddenly spinning?

Perhaps eating a couple of her imperial brother's koi fish would make her feel better.

...

The Jiang Residence's Small Garden.

Half the garden's wisteria bloomed overnight.

The garden was dyed in a dreamy shade of purple, slender and soft vines swaying gracefully in the breeze.

The petals fluttered lightly with the wind, and a faint fragrance lingered all around.

Jiang Jinhua sat leisurely swinging on a swing among the wisteria trees, opening a letter that Su Yue'er had a maid secretly deliver to her.

She had barely read two lines when her expression abruptly changed.

Jiang Miao was actually capable of catching ghosts?!

How could this be?

It wasn't that she didn't believe ghosts existed in this world, but rather that she didn't believe Jiang Miao had the ability to catch them!

In the lower volume of the *Luban Book* she had stolen from her adoptive father, there were indeed records of methods and incantations to communicate with the netherworld.

She had also secretly tried it a few times, but every time she felt the door to another world opening toward her, she would find herself unable to continue reciting the incantation.

Furthermore, after each attempt, her body would grow weak for several days, so she dared not try rashly anymore.

Fortunately, there was a yellowed piece of paper tucked inside the book, recording many spells, so she had concentrated on studying those instead.

Yet up to now, she had only mastered a few spells of little practical use, such as the locating spell, which could only find things she had accidentally misplaced.

Instead, the little fortune-gathering array she had set up for herself had worked, quickly leading the Marquis's estate to find her and bring her home, casting off her lowly commoner status to become a pampered young lady once again.

Therefore, Jiang Jinhua was quite confident in her own talent in this area.

Give her time, and she would surely master all the spells within it. By then, what could she not have precisely when she wanted it?

Precisely because she had tried and understood it, she knew all too well just how difficult it was to learn ghost-catching skills!

Yet Jiang Miao, the very person who had stolen her glory, wealth, and affection for fourteen years, actually possessed an ability she couldn't learn!

A layer of gloom rose in Jiang Jinhua's eyes, her fingertips digging straight into her palms. "No! Absolutely impossible!"

She crumpled the letter in her hand into a tight ball, leaped off the swing, and hurried toward Jiang Huai's room.

Servants had said that Jiang Huai used to be the closest to Jiang Miao, so he should know something...

Jiang Huai was getting a headache from reading, and seeing Jiang Jinhua come to find him正好 gave him a temporary escape from his misery.

He greeted her happily, "Hua'er, why are you here? Come on in..."

chapters.title: Speak Ill of You and You Get Mad Again
chapters.content:
Jiang Jinhua offered a bow, glanced at the open books spread across his desk, and said apologetically, "Did Hua'er disturb Third Brother?"

"No, no, how could you?"

Jiang Huai complained with a bitter face, "I'm just not cut out for studying. Father insists on forcing me to read, my head is killing me."

Jiang Jinhua pursed her lips and smiled. "Then if Third Brother doesn't like studying, what does he like to do?"

"Of course I like practicing martial arts!" Mentioning martial arts made Jiang Huai look much more spirited. "My dream is to be a great general."

The founding ancestor of the Jiang family was a great general who fought across the realm alongside the Taizu Emperor.

Only then did they secure the wealth and nobility that blessed their descendants.

Yet ever since his great-grandfather's generation, the Jiang family had not produced a single military general, nor any high-ranking civil officials, leaving the family increasingly in decline.

If their father hadn't suddenly caught the Emperor's eye and become the Minister of Rites, the Jiang family would likely have already fallen out of the capital's circle of power.

However, Jiang Huai believed that since the Jiang family earned its marquisate through military merits, safeguarding this honor required following the path of their founding ancestor.

He simply didn't want to waste his time on studying.

A look of admiration appeared on Jiang Jinhua's small face. "Third Brother has grand ambitions and will surely achieve his dream."

This expression pleased Jiang Huai, who said in pleasant surprise, "You think so too?"

Jiang Jinhua nodded heavily. "Hua'er believes that with Third Brother's ability, you will definitely achieve your dream!"

The hand Jiang Huai held by his side clenched tightly, deeply moved within his heart.

He raised a hand to pat Jiang Jinhua's head, sighing with emotion, "You truly are my biological sister. Unlike that annoying pest Jiang Miao, who only knows how to bring me down."

"Oh? What did she say to you?"

Jiang Jinhua asked, maintaining a calm facade.

At the mention of Jiang Miao, Jiang Huai said with indignation, "She said my physical foundation is poor, and rather than wasting time practicing martial arts, I'd be better off studying hard, there might be a chance I could become a military secretary by a general's side..."

"How could she say such a thing?" Jiang Jinhua knitted her delicate brows, sighed lightly, and led Jiang Huai by the hand to sit down.

"Third Brother, don't be angry either. She's just a delicate young lady raised at home, what does she know about these things? She was probably just talking nonsense off the top of her head, don't take it to heart."

These words sounded like she was comforting Jiang Huai, but in reality, they dismissed Jiang Miao as narrow-minded and ignorant.

Jiang Huai heartily agreed, "Exactly! She stays cooped up at home all day, what principles could she possibly understand?"

Jiang Jinhua followed up on his words: "Third Brother, she didn't like going out in the past. Was she very fond of reading, painting, and things like that?"

Jiang Huai let out a light snort of contempt, his face written all over with disdain.

"Her?"

"Have you ever seen that yellow cat? That's the one she keeps. All day long she's either sleeping or strolling aimlessly around the courtyard, and the rest of her time is spent teasing the cat."

"She knows nothing of the zither, chess, calligraphy, or painting, let alone needlework. Mother used to worry she wouldn't even be able to get married!"

Jiang Jinhua continued probing, "How come I heard her fortune-telling is quite accurate? Could it be that some master taught her these things?"

"Tch, you actually believe that?"

"What master would she have? Even the tutors hired to teach her reading and writing were driven away in anger by her one after another."

Jiang Huai cast a worried look at her. "Hua'er, you mustn't be so naive. Jiang Miao must have hired a bunch of shills to spread rumors that her fortune-telling is accurate so she can scam people. Don't let her trick you."

Hearing Jiang Huai describe Jiang Miao's daily life in such detail, Jiang Jinhua felt somewhat more at ease.

She knew it! Jiang Miao used to be a sheltered young lady who never stepped out of her chambers; how could she possibly have learned fortune-telling and ghost-catching?

Just as her third brother said, Jiang Miao must have hired plenty of shills to help build her reputation.

As for what Su Yue'er said about Jiang Miao catching ghosts, who knew where that ridiculous rumor came from?

She was just a fake whose biological parents were nobodies, possessing nothing more than some unpresentable, petty cleverness. How could she possibly be more capable than her, Jiang Jinhua?

However...

Jiang Jinhua casually glanced over at Jiang Huai.

She remembered hearing Mother mention that Third Brother was born in the lunar month of yin, on the day of yin, at the hour of yin. If she used his blood to cast spells, wouldn't she achieve twice the result with half the effort?

"Meow~ Meow~~~"

From outside the courtyard suddenly came a shrill cat cry and the chaotic footsteps of servants.

Jiang Huai abruptly stood up and pulled open the door, just in time to see that fat, chinless yellow cat squatting not far away, staring right at him with wide eyes.

Jiang Huai looked away in disgust and asked the servants,

"What's going on?"

In the courtyard, a maid and a manservant hurriedly bowed in salute and replied,

"Reporting to Third Young Master, the cat that Miss, no, the cat Jiang Miao used to keep suddenly rushed into Young Miss's room and knocked over a lot of things."

Upon hearing this, Jiang Jinhua's heart skipped a beat.

She rushed out and sharply demanded of the maid,

"What did it knock over?"

The maid answered cautiously, "Replying to Young Miss, that cat knocked over all the porcelain in your room, smashing them all over the floor. And I don't know if it got hurt, but there's blood everywhere..."

Hearing this, Jiang Jinhua's vision went dark, and she almost fainted.

With her small face tightly pulled, she rushed toward her room without uttering another word.

Jiang Huai followed closely behind her, offering continuous comfort, "Hua'er, don't be upset. If the porcelain is broken, we'll just have Father buy you some more."

Jiang Jinhua was feeling irritable inside and had no wish for him to tag along. Taking a deep breath, she turned her head and softened her tone:

"Third Brother, go help them catch the cat. Don't let it run off."

She was going to strip that hateful cat's skin and pull its tendons while it was still alive!

Thinking that was a fair point, that only by catching the culprit could her sister vent her anger, Jiang Huai turned away to catch the cat instead.

Jiang Jinhua hurried back to her room. She didn't care at all that the porcelain was shattered.

Yet when she laid eyes on those patches of brownish bloodstains on the floor, a fierce glint instantly shot from her eyes!

That was the mother-child-linked heart blood she had painstakingly collected over a great deal of hardship, mixed with special medicines to keep it from coagulating.

She had previously used half of it to set up the fortune-gathering array, and the remaining half was originally intended to be used after her marriage to set up an array that would make her husband hopelessly devoted to her.

However, after returning to the Jiang residence, she immediately realized that what she needed right now was to win the affection of her parents and brothers, so she used all of it to set up this array instead, she had been heartbroken over it.

And now, her array had been ruined by a mere beast!

This was the capital city, a place where she was a stranger. Where on earth was she supposed to collect so much mother-child-linked heart blood again?

"Jiang Miao!"

Jiang Jinhua curled her fingers into tight fists, venomously hissing Jiang Miao's name.

It was bad enough that she had stolen her glory and wealth for over a dozen years, but now even the beast she kept had come to ruin her plans!!!

...

Jiang Miao, who was currently the object of Jiang Jinhua's jealous hatred, was propping one leg over the other, leisurely half-reclining on a flower bed while chewing on a blade of grass and directing Chi Ge to roast fish.

From the modest backyard of the Chenghuang Temple in the suburbs drifted a barbecue aroma that caused the God of the City inside the hall to shake his head incessantly.

"Can you even roast fish or not?" Jiang Miao cast a disdainful look at Chi Ge. "Time to sprinkle the salt!"

Chi Ge's fair face was smeared with black soot, the result of Jiang Miao insisting he tend the fire and mess up his face.

Suppressing his temper, Chi Ge said, "I couldn't originally, but didn't I just learn?"

Jiang Miao curled her lips. "Cumin, cumin."

Panicking, Chi Ge scrambled to find the cumin powder.

Just as he finally found it, Jiang Miao shoved him aside.

"Move aside, you're ruining good things!"

Chi Ge felt immensely wronged. "Am I really that clumsy?"

After sprinkling the cumin powder and flipping the grilled fish, Jiang Miao spared him a sidelong glance.

"Speak ill of you and you get mad again."

Chi Ge: "..."

Enduring it for a moment, his curiosity finally got the better of him, and he took stuttering little steps over to Jiang Miao's side. "What did you used to tell people about me?"

"That you're a clumsy blockhead, obviously."

Far from fearing she might damage a youth's fragile heart, Jiang Miao was entirely, brutally honest.

"How am I a blockhead?"

"Well, you're not a blockhead, it's just that your Imperial Uncle still thinks to this day that you were the one who stole and ate his pet koi fish."

"Ahhhhh~~~ Can you not bring that up?"

Jiang Miao's rebellious streak flared up. "I'm just kindly helping you reminisce!"

Note ①: Mother-child-linked heart blood is purely fictional, created solely to serve the plot, so please don't take it too literally.

chapters.title: The Eccentric Emperor Who Named Koi Fish
chapters.content:
Chi Ge went berserk.

Thinking about the past made his blood boil.

Back then, Jiang Miao was not even as tall as his shoulder, yet she dared to execute a "urine escape" from the imperial banquet, sneaking off under the cover of a moonless night to steal the koi fish, only to run right into him.

Out of sheer curiosity, he had quietly followed behind her.

Jiang Miao found an abandoned palace, stood at the doorway, and beckoned to him, calling out sweetly, "Come here, I'll show you a treasure."

Curious, he walked over, only to be knocked unconscious with a brick.

He saw it clearly, the brick was as big as two of his palms, and covered in pitch-black mud...

When he woke up, Jiang Miao was already gone, leaving behind only an extinguished campfire and a few fish skeletons.

While he was dazed, rubbing his still-throbbing head, the emperor and the eunuch guards found him.

It wasn't a big deal at first, just considered children playing around and running amok; the emperor even smiled and told him not to be afraid.

That was until the emperor saw the head of the koi fish he personally fed. Two heads.

The emperor immediately wailed in grief, "A-Shun! A-Sui!"

And then Chi Ge was personally beaten by the emperor. He tried to explain that Jiang Miao stole and ate the fish, but he ended up getting beaten even harder, the reason being that he did something bad and tried to frame someone else.

When he got home, he received a double-beating from the Grand Princess and her husband.

He explained again, and was beaten yet again, and again, and again.

The reason? For being stupid enough not to call for help when he saw someone doing something wrong, and instead walking right into the trap.

To this day, he still couldn't understand why Jiang Miao bothered to roast the fish, yet specifically left the fish heads unroasted. The incriminating evidence was just too obvious.

Were fish heads not delicious?

Jiang Miao kindly explained to him, "I was afraid your wise and mighty uncle wouldn't recognize that those were the fish he raised."

Chi Ge still couldn't wrap his head around it.

"Wouldn't destroying the corpse be better? Why bother with the extra step?"

"Oh, mainly because when I approached the koi pond, I bumped into someone. It was bound to come to light sooner or later, so call that being prepared for a rainy day."

Chi Ge gnashed his teeth, "Crafty!" So she had intended to frame him all along.

"I'm also a wolf in sheep's clothing!" Jiang Miao reached out, grabbed a roasted fish, and brought it to her mouth.

Chi Ge immediately shut his mouth and lunged for a roasted fish.

"Ah~" A miserable scream rang out.

Chi Ge stared at Jiang Miao with wide eyes, "Aren't you afraid of the heat?"

"Eating it while it's hot yields better results," Jiang Miao bluffed casually.

Chi Ge forgot that Jiang Miao's words were as unreliable as an old crone's mouth; baring his teeth and shivering, he reached out to grab a roasted fish, shifting it from his left hand to his right, not even daring to let it touch his lips as he brought it to his mouth.

It seemed that absorbing energy for cultivation was no easy task after all...

Jiang Miao was like a cat; she quickly devoured her three roasted fish and stared longingly at the remaining one in Chi Ge's hands.

Chi Ge quickly blocked her line of sight, warning vigilantly, "Don't even think about snatching food from the tiger's jaws. I got this in exchange for two beatings, you can't be this heartless!"

Jiang Miao was intensely curious, "Why two beatings?"

"Uncle already beat me once, and the beating from my mom and dad is still pending. My mom said they'll beat me together once my dad gets back."

Chi Ge grumbled indignantly:

"My mom is just jealous; she wanted to eat some too, but I didn't help her steal any."

Jiang Miao: "Since you've already stolen them, a couple more wouldn't make a difference."

Chi Ge hurriedly picked up his other roasted fish.

"That won't do. I've already stolen Uncle's virtues of prudence, caution, wisdom, and beauty; all that's left is prosperity and peace, which is Uncle's bottom line. If I eat into his bottom line, I might get stripped of my title as Heir."

Jiang Miao's eyelid twitched. The fish even had names!

What a bizarre family.

She couldn't resist a biting remark: "You're living worse than a few fish..."

Chi Ge: Σ(っ°Д°;)っ

He no longer wanted to take her as his master. If he did, he'd sooner or later commit patricide against his master!

"Meow~~~"

Suddenly, a familiar cat's meow echoed in the garden.

Jiang Miao sprang up, and in pleasant surprise, ran toward the source of the sound, "Fat Orange!"

"Meow-meow~"

A plump yellow furball leaped down from the Chinese scholar tree and landed securely in Jiang Miao's arms.

It raised its emerald-like, translucent large eyes, looked at Jiang Miao with a wronged expression, and extended a paw to point at her while meowing incessantly, as if accusing her of leaving without a word and abandoning her cat.

At a single glance, Jiang Miao spotted a three-inch-long, half-centimeter-deep wound on its chubby belly, which was still oozing blood. Her heart ached instantly.

"Fat Orange, how did you get hurt?"

Fat Orange couldn't speak. It raised a paw, pointed toward the direction of the imperial capital, and let out a particularly miserable cry.

"Don't panic."

Jiang Miao covered the wound with her hand, closed her eyes, and chanted incantations under her breath.

Unseen by anyone, the wound healed at a speed visible to the naked eye. Fat Orange squinted in comfort, its little paws tightly hugging Jiang Miao's hand, while its big round face rubbed against her affectionately over and over again.

Jiang Miao withdrew her hand and quickly began calculating with her fingers. A moment later, a chilling coldness surfaced in the depths of her eyes.

Though her spiritual power was currently limited, she managed to vaguely divine some information.

Fat Orange had entered a place reeking of gloomy yin energy. Perhaps out of an animal's instinct for self-preservation, it had destroyed everything emitting that yin energy.

Afterward, it was cornered by a group of people. Jiang Huai slashed a blade at its belly; fortunately, it dodged quickly enough to avoid being killed, and managed to scramble over the courtyard wall and escape.

Jiang Miao sneered. She couldn't care less about how such demonic stuff existed in the Jiang household; she only felt a sense of injustice for Fat Orange.

Fat Orange's actions had actually saved the Marquis's Mansion, yet it was almost killed by an oblivious Jiang Huai. This karma was going to cost him dearly!

When she was driven out of the mansion that day, it all happened so suddenly. Fat Orange had wandered off somewhere, and fearing that the pampered cat would suffer hardships following her, she had planned to get settled first before sneaking back to steal it out, but instead, she had almost caused its death.

The little fellow had great fortune, actually managing to run this far to find her. That cleverness certainly came from her.

Jiang Miao didn't mind Fat Orange's dusty coat either. She gently stroked its fur and said softly, "I will never leave you behind again."

"Meow-meow-meow~" Fat Orange stamped two paw prints onto her collar, its big eyes filled with a warning look: If you leave me behind again, I'll die to show you!

Unfortunately, Jiang Miao couldn't understand.

Chi Ge followed the sound and found them. Seeing a greasy, fat cat in Jiang Miao's arms, his eyes widened in shock.

"Cat meat doesn't even taste good, why did you catch it?"

Jiang Miao glanced at him sideways, "This is Fat Orange, the cat I used to raise."

Chi Ge let out a sigh of relief. He had been terrified of hearing Jiang Miao claim that cat meat was great for nourishment...

He raised the fish skeleton with the meat picked clean and brought it to Fat Orange's mouth, "Meow-meow, want some fish?"

Fat Orange rolled its eyes dramatically and turned its head away in disgust.

What kind of nonsense is this? As wicked as humans!

Jiang Miao started walking outward, "Let's go."

Passing through the main hall of the City God Temple, Chi Ge instinctively looked back and instantly felt the hair all over his body stand on end.

Terrified, he screamed, "Miao... Miao... Miao-miao..."

"Meow... meow~" Fat Orange chimed in with a meow.

Jiang Miao whipped her head around and bared her teeth, "From now on, you are not allowed to call me Miao-miao!"

Chi Ge pointed a trembling finger at the statue of the City God, "H-he... how did his eyes close?"

It wasn't his first time at the City God Temple. When he arrived today, he had even paid his respects, and he remembered very clearly that the City God's eyes had been wide open back then.

Yet at this moment, the City God had his eyes closed as if he were asleep. Mud idols could open and close their eyes, tell me, would you be scared or not?

---

chapters.title: Gossip is Best Accompanied by Company
chapters.content:
Jiang Miao swept her gaze up to the City God's face and narrowed her eyes.

The City God gave a start and hurriedly popped his eyes wide open, looking full of vigor.

Only then did Jiang Miao leisurely say to Chi Ge:

"Your eyes were playing tricks on you just now!"

Chi Ge looked at the City God again, rolled his eyes back, and fainted on the spot.

Jiang Miao: "..."

She pointed at the City God and cursed, "If you're going to slack off, pick a better time! Do you believe this grand immortal will burn your temple down?"

The City God kept his mouth tightly shut, his brows drooping, taking the scolding without a retort.

He had just thought that since some bigshots were here, nothing bad would happen, so he decided to catch a quick nap...

He hadn't rested in ages...

A god's life is a life too!

Jiang Miao glared at him fiercely and dragged Chi Ge away.

The City God's brow instantly relaxed back to normal. The temple was saved!

He rejoiced inwardly, feeling as though this ancestor had forgotten about their ten-year pact, not even mentioning it today.

He was truly overthinking it; Jiang Miao just didn't want her secrets overheard by Chi Ge. What if she turned out to look like a fool? Where would her face be?

When Chi Ge woke up, he found himself half-leaned against the fork of an old ginkgo tree, at least thirty feet off the ground. Terrified, he used all four limbs, hugging the trunk tightly like a sloth.

"Meow~~~"

Fat Orange's cry came from beside his ear, and Chi Ge inexplicably felt that the creature was mocking him.

Seeing Jiang Miao sitting on a tree branch, swinging her legs and stretching her neck to look ahead, the rock in his heart finally dropped back into place.

Good thing he hadn't been abandoned.

He muttered, "Why'd you drag me up a tree for no reason?"

Without looking back, Jiang Miao said excitedly, "Look over there quickly, the Marquis of Yongning's wife is going to commit suicide!"

!!!

Chi Ge was startled and shifted into a safer posture to crane his neck and look.

The Marquis of Yongning's Mansion was not far away, and from his high vantage point, he had an unobstructed view.

In front of the grand gates, a richly dressed woman with disheveled hair sat on the ground, holding a golden hairpin to her own throat while her other hand flailed wildly in an unconscious manner, as if trying to ward something off.

With reddened eyes, she shrieked at the top of her lungs, "Husband, save me! Save me..."

Several surrounding servants looked as though they wanted to rush forward to stop her from committing suicide, yet they dared not act rashly.

The Marquis of Yongning wore a look of utter anxiety. Several times he approached her, only for the golden hairpin in her hand to dig another hole in her neck... and he was forced to back down.

She was killing herself, yet crying out for help.

Chi Ge was utterly dumbfounded.

"If she wants to kill herself, why is she screaming for help?"

Jiang Miao gave a heh-heh chuckle.

"Want to eat a melon [hear the gossip]? One hundred taels!"

Chi Ge felt deeply aggrieved, but unable to resist the temptation, he reluctantly took down his money pouch and handed it over.

He gnashed his teeth, "My monthly allowance is down to just this much. I'll pay the rest next month."

Jiang Miao looked at him with utter disdain, "I've never seen such a poor imperial generation descendant!" Yet her hands were slick and practiced at pocketing the money.

Then, with a flick of her small hand, before Chi Ge could even see what she had done, a flash of fire vanished instantly, and right after that, he saw several people suddenly appear around the Marquis of Yongning's wife.

No, those weren't people, they were ghosts!

All female ghosts!

One had a pale-white face with bulging eyes and a tongue hanging agonizingly long.

Another had a pitch-black face; at night, probably only those two ghostly white eyeballs would be visible, as if she had died of severe poison.

A third had missing limbs, wriggling along like a caterpillar and leaving behind a long trail of bloodstains...

Most terrifying of all was a pregnant female ghost whose high-mounded belly had a massive gash ripped open, from which an infant's head poked out. The infant's mouth gaped wide, its sharp teeth snapping open and shut...

Three female ghosts entangled the Marquis of Yongning's wife, jointly forcing her hands to saw at her own throat, while the "caterpillar" ghost spun in circles to cheer them on.

Chi Ge rolled his eyes back...

This time, Jiang Miao was prepared. With a backhand slap, she slapped a talisman onto his forehead, "Freeze!"

Awakening instantly from the brink of fainting, Chi Ge found himself completely immobilized, unable to even blink his eyes... forced to watch ghosts.

After this shock, he actually felt a bit less scared. The ghosts were afraid of Jiang Miao, so what was he supposed to be afraid of?

Seeing that the dagger in the Marquis of Yongning's wife's hand had already broken through her skin, he stammered in a rush:

"Aren't you a ghost catcher? Hurry up and save her!"

Jiang Miao shot him a sidelong glance.

"The essence of gossiping, you see, is to accompany them. You don't fan the flames, you don't meddle too much. Advise if you can; if you can't, just watch."

Chi Ge urged anxiously, "Then go advise her! The Marquis of Yongning is a loyal and virtuous general. Our Dafeng Dynasty has been able to remain stable to this day precisely because he repeatedly repelled foreign enemies. How can you let ghosts harm his wife?"

Jiang Miao stroked her chin, looking roguish. "I did advise her, but she wouldn't listen."

Chi Ge: "How did you advise her?"

Jiang Miao: "I told her that doing this wouldn't actually kill her, and she needed to think of another way. But they didn't believe me."

Chi Ge: "???"

Jiang Miao kindly explained to him:

"The Marquis of Yongning's wife still has remaining allotted lifespan. No matter how hard they try, they won't be able to kill her."

Chi Ge laughed out of sheer anger, "Is that what I meant? You're a Daoist priest, and instead of thinking about saving people, you're thinking about helping ghosts come up with ways to harm people. It's simply... simply appalling!"

Jiang Miao looked at him as if bestowing care upon a mentally disabled person, "I admire most that simple-minded look in your eyes when you view all things in the world!"

She pointed over, "Those women were all concubines of the Marquis of Yongning. The one with her tongue hanging out, everyone thought she hanged herself, but actually, the Marquis's wife ordered someone to string her up."

"The poisoned one? Poisoned by her."

"The pregnant woman? Fed sleeping drugs during childbirth, resulting in two corpses in one grave."

"The one with no hands or feet? Her limbs were hacked off by her."

Chi Ge's mouth fell open. He instinctively tried to shake his head, but couldn't.

Unconvinced, he argued, "Impossible. The Marquis of Yongning's wife is the daughter of the Elder Grand Tutor, renowned for her virtue and benevolence..."

Yet his voice grew softer and softer as he spoke, faintly sensing that Jiang Miao couldn't possibly be talking nonsense.

His handsome brows furrowed tightly.

He said solemnly, "If the Marquis of Yongning's wife truly committed such heinous acts, she must be brought to justice. If she gets killed by ghosts like this, no one will ever know her true face."

Jiang Miao chuckled.

"Splendid! That's what I think too."

Chi Ge said with frustration, "Then why won't you untie me? I'll go find people from the Dali Temple to investigate."

"Naive!" Jiang Miao watched the female ghosts wrestling with the Marquis of Yongning's wife while replying, "Under what identity will you report the case? Do you have evidence? The families of these deceased victims haven't even stepped forward, what business is it of yours to stick your neck out?"

"You agreed she should be brought to justice too!" Chi Ge protested unconvinced.

Jiang Miao rolled her eyes and turned her head to look at him.

Chi Ge shifted his gaze slightly and saw her long, curled eyelashes fluttering gently. Sunlight filtered through the layers of tree leaves, sliding across her lashes, radiant and dazzling.

His heart inexplicably began to race wildly.

Then he heard Jiang Miao ask with a crafty glint in her eyes, "The Marquis of Yongning has heavy military merits; the emperor must have given him lots of rewards, right?"

Chi Ge nodded blankly, suddenly struck by an ominous premonition.

Sure enough, Jiang Miao narrowed her eyes craftily. "Go tell him that if he wants to know why his concubines died unnatural deaths, he should bring money to find me. One thousand taels per life."

Chi Ge's slightly fluttering romantic feelings instantly turned as calm as still water.

The words squeezed out from between his teeth, "Does your grandmaster know you're this money-grubbing?"

Jiang Miao: "None of his damn business!"

"Achoo!"

As soon as the words left her mouth, she sneezed, hurriedly covered her mouth, and looked up at the sky.

She rolled her eyes and muttered inwardly, "That's about enough... Big deal, I'll share a little bit with you, alright?"

She rubbed her nose, instantly feeling relieved.

Chi Ge resignedly agreed, sticking out his neck defiantly as he said:

"I'm not helping you hoard wealth, I purely want to seek justice for the wrongfully dead!"

Jiang Miao praised with a beaming smile, "What a fine youth, upholding the Five Virtues and Four Beauties."

With that, she ripped the talisman off his forehead and kicked him straight down the tree with one foot.

"Go uphold justice, young man!"

chapters.title: I'm sticking with my master forever, and he swallowed the key
chapters.content:
"┻━┻~Aaaaa~┻━┻" Chi Ge screamed in terror, closing his eyes: My life is over!

Eh?

Why didn't it hurt when his butt hit the ground? It even bounced a bit...

He looked up at Jiang Miao with little stars of adoration in his eyes.

As expected of an immortal, boundless in magical power! Terrifying indeed!

Taking her as a master, this master must be taken!

He was going to stick with his master forever, and he had swallowed the key!

He clenched his fists, puffed out his chest, and walked toward the Marquis of Yongning’s residence.

Today's business must be done beautifully so the master could see his ability!

Meanwhile, the Marchioness of Yongning, who had been resisting the persecution of the female ghost for a good hour or two, finally ran out of strength. With a "clink," her golden hairpin dropped to the ground.

Her fingers twitched like a chicken's claw, her arms went paralyzed, and they hung down like two noodles.

The female ghost bared her teeth in anxiety, using all her ghost-strength to pull at the Marchioness's arm.

She couldn't pull it, she simply couldn't pull it.

The ghost infant was equally anxious, grinding its teeth until smoke came out.

Its mother floated up, trying to make the ghost infant bite the Marchioness of Yongning's neck, but alas, the ghost infant couldn't move its neck, and its forehead was too prominent, so its mouth couldn't reach.

It bit until its jaws were sore and still couldn't reach...

Chi Ge watched anxiously, wanting to rush up and drag the infant over to put it on the Marchioness of Yongning's neck.

If all else failed, couldn't it bite somewhere else on her body?

You guys are only dead in body, your minds are still alive, right?

As the Marquis of Yongning scooped up his wife and walked into the estate, Chi Ge finally snapped back to reality. How could he be giving ideas to a female ghost?

If the Marchioness of Yongning had committed crimes, please use the law to punish her, instead of letting idiots anger her to death!

He hurriedly shoved aside the onlookers and gave chase. "Wait for me."

Everyone in the Marquis's household knew this young lord and didn't dare stop him, letting him dash right up to the Marquis of Yongning.

The Marquis was already agitated and anxious because of his wife's sudden madness, wanting only to find an imperial physician as soon as possible to check on her. He gave Chi Ge no pleasant look.

In a stiff voice, he said, "This Marquis has important matters at home and truly has no time to entertain the Heir. Please return."

As a prominent military general of the Dafeng Dynasty holding heavy troops and making successive contributions, he wasn't afraid of offending a little heir. The current emperor was wise, and the Eldest Princess was also deeply sensible of righteousness; they would never harbor resentment against him over such a trivial matter.

If it were the past, Chi Ge would have snorted coldly and turned on his heel to leave. At this moment, thinking of flawlessly completing the task Jiang Miao had given him, he had no choice but to swallow his pride and seek the comprehensive view.

Seeing that he was about to be "politely escorted out" by the estate servants, he blurted out without thinking, "Everyone has scriptures that are hard to chant. Did you know your house has five?"

Marquis of Yongning: ???

"Those four concubines of yours are four books, plus this one, that's five!" Chi Ge pointed at the wife in the Marquis's arms and held up five fingers.

The Marquis's face went completely black. His gaze turned sharp, and he rebuked, "If the Heir is too idle, you might as well go listen to operas or read storybooks, instead of coming to treat this Marquis's family affairs as a joke!"

Chi Ge mimicked Jiang Miao's unfathomable, mysterious smile. "This young master knows everything that happens in your household. Do you believe it? Those concubines of yours..."

He suddenly leaned close to the Marquis's ear and lowered his voice, "They all died with grievances unredressed, angry that you didn't uphold justice for them. They are all standing right over there watching you!"

A patch of dark clouds suddenly blocked the warm sun, and a gust of wind materialized out of nowhere, rustling the withered leaves and creating an eerie, ghostly atmosphere.

The Marquis of Yongning felt the hairs on his body stand on end. His heart trembled, and a strong sense of unease welled up.

"What do you mean?"

His four concubines had all met with misfortune while he was away on military campaigns. Though he had doubts, upon seeing the airtight evidence and the perpetrators brought to justice, he had no choice but to accept his fate.

A high-ranking monk had once divined his fate as hard and fatal to his wives and children; he simply assumed he had implicated them.

From then on, he never took another concubine to avoid unjustly harming human lives.

Hearing Chi Ge's implication now, was there still a hidden story within this that he didn't know?

Chi Ge took a step back, placed one hand behind his back, raised his chin, and said with haughty pride, "Does the Marquis still think this young master is meddling in other people's business?"

The Marquis hesitated for a moment, then finally gritted his teeth and said, "Please, Heir, come into the estate and sit."

Chi Ge felt a secret thrill. The feeling of insight into another's secrets while the person involved remained completely in the dark, waiting for him to provide the answers, made him feel a bit floaty.

After settling his wife, the Marquis of Yongning finally came to the front hall.

With a heavy gaze, he sized up Chi Ge for a moment and said coldly:

"If the Heir knows something, you might as well speak frankly."

Chi Ge leisurely sat down in the Luohan chair, picked up a teacup, and blew on the tender green tea leaves floating on the surface. Watching the leaves rise and sink gave him an inflated sense of having destiny in his hands.

He lazily raised his eyes to look at the Marquis.

Slowly putting down the teacup, his very first words were like a blade: "The Marquis has neither sons nor daughters. After a hundred years, there won't even be anyone to hold your spirit tablet. Pitiful and lamentable!"

The Marquis of Yongning abruptly clenched his fists. For a split second, his thought was how to escape scot-free after beating this little bastard to death.

After all, he was a military general who had spent half his life on horseback and had the blood of countless people on his hands. This burst of anger radiated a frenzied, bloodthirsty, and stern murderous aura that rolled toward Chi Ge.

The young master, who had been putting on a mystic act just a second before, shivered in fright and hurriedly shouted:

"Don't be rash..."

The Marquis didn't make a sound, his stern and freezing gaze locked tightly onto Chi Ge's face. Chi Ge felt that if he said even one wrong word, the other party would hack him to pieces.

Not daring to speak any more nonsense, he blurted out, "Your four concubines died unnatural deaths, they were all murdered by your wife!"

The Marquis's thin lips pressed into a line, the storm in the depths of his eyes leaking out entirely, and his strong, powerful arm abruptly reached toward Chi Ge.

Chi Ge dropped and rolled away, shouting miserably, "I have evidence!"

!!!

At these words, the Marquis's hand paused. He narrowed his eyes to scrutinize Chi Ge, as if judging whether he was lying.

Chi Ge's back was soaked with sweat as he let out a long, ragged breath.

Damn it, the Great General's murderous aura scared the baby half to death...

He blurted out quickly, like setting off firecrackers:

"Their wronged spirits are right outside the Marquis's estate! Just now, they came to exact revenge on your wife and forced her to commit suicide. I know you won't believe it, but don't disbelieve it just yet, just listen to me finish."

Seeing that he didn't seem to be lying, the Marquis calmed down slightly and said in an icy voice:

"How can the Heir see ghosts... them?"

Finally turning to the main topic, Chi Ge breathed a sigh of relief, climbed back up, and sat down properly.

He cleared his throat and said:

"As it happens, this young master was recently entangled by a ghost, and a high-level master saved me."

"This young master simply took her as my master. My master can not only capture ghosts, but she also has the ability to let mortals see ghosts."

The Marquis's expression changed, instantly believing him by fifty percent.

He believed ghosts existed in the world; leaving aside how many supernatural events there were on the battlefield, there had certainly been a few that defied rational explanation.

Moreover, being well-traveled and knowledgeable, he had naturally heard that such high masters truly existed in the world, only he had never had the fortune to meet one.

He leaned forward toward Chi Ge, asking with a serious expression:

"May I ask where this high master comes from?"

Where did she come from?

Chi Ge's mouth twitched, his head buzzing a little.

How was he supposed to answer this?

Damn it, if his master's identity were revealed, he feared the Marquis's sandbag-sized fists would beat the crap out of him...

"What? Does the Heir not know how to make up a story anymore?" The Marquis narrowed his eyes dangerously.

Chi Ge gave a start, his mouth uncontrollably replying:

"Jiang Miao, my master is Jiang Miao!"

The Marquis hesitated for a moment, frowning. Why did this name sound somewhat familiar?

Suddenly, he recalled how a few days ago, his wife had mentioned that the Marquis of Xuanyuan’s residence had found their biological daughter and driven out the impostor who had been impersonating the Jiang family's young lady.

That impostor seemed to also be named Jiang Miao, and she was reportedly setting up a stall in the capital to fortune-tell for people.

"Could it be that Jiang Miao from the Marquis of Xuanyuan's residence?"

Chi Ge swallowed hard and nodded slightly.

The Marquis of Yongning clenched his back teeth until they ached to control the urge to beat this little bastard up.

He abruptly stood up and rebuked sternly:

"That Jiang Miao has bad character, swindles people through falsehoods, and has a notorious reputation. Yet you actually use such a person to mock this Marquis!"

"Leave! I won't see you out!", before I lose control of my fists!

***

chapters.title: A god's life is hard, better to be a pig
chapters.content:
Chi Ge quickly said, "Hey, don't disbelieve me. My master is an immortal. If you don't believe it, go ask Imperial Physician Su, or my mother, or my second brother..."

The Marquis of Yongning closed his eyes, suppressed the anger in his heart, flicked his sleeves, and left.

Chi Ge: "..."

Fine, the mission failing wasn't his fault; it was because his master had a bad reputation.

Since the master of the house had this attitude, he, a dignified young heir, couldn't be bothered to linger here either.

Walking out of the Marquis of Yongning's residence, he glanced back and spat, "Bah! There'll come a time when you'll be begging this young master!"

Given his master's temperament, by then those five thousand taels would probably increase tenfold.
