Seeing Chi Ge return dejected, Jiang Miao knew at once things hadn't gone well. Looking at his guilty yet defiant little expression, she was amused.

She considerately comforted him, "Don't be discouraged. There are new blows every day; hardships might be late, but they will never be absent. After all these years, you should be used to it by now."

She didn't really care if the business fell through; anyway, her small goal had been overfulfilled, her purse was bulging, and she could live a thriftily lazy life forever.

Chi Ge: Angry 😤=(o｀ω′)ノ

He didn't want to take her as his master anymore.

Yet he didn't forget to drop bad words about the Marquis of Yongning: "The Marquis of Yongning said you have bad character, swindle people through falsehoods, and have a notorious reputation. He didn't believe me."

Jiang Miao felt a pain in her chest from anger, then realized she didn't have a chest, and her anger instantly vanished.

She jumped down from the tree, more agile than the fat tabby cat in her arms. "Let's go, it's time to eat."

Chi Ge said with a bad mood, "Didn't we just eat? A foot-long crucian carp, isn't eating three of them enough to stuff you?"

Jiang Miao slanted a glance at him. "Can't I be hungry again? Being pretty can't be used as a meal."

Chi Ge: "..."

Calling herself pretty, this shamelessness had his mother's style back in the day.

"I'm out of money. How about we go home to eat?" Chi Ge was poor and lacked confidence.

Jiang Miao righteously refused, "No, it feels more secure to eat using my own money."

Chi Ge raised a hand to his chest, his heart aching.

All your money was mine to begin with... He decided to eat a little more.

After dinner, the Crucian Carp Duo parted ways, each returning to their respective homes.

That's right, the inn was now Jiang Miao's home.

To express his apology for owing her money, the innkeeper had upgraded her to a guest suite for free. Now, Jiang Miao was also a high-end person living in a suite, and the innkeeper had fully achieved making her feel at home.

Under the orange candlelight, the scene of a human and a cat snuggling together was warm and touching.

Jiang Miao read a storybook to the fat tabby. The tabby listened with great relish, occasionally making meow sounds of different pitches as if commenting on the plot.

Just as the tabby cat was listening to the most exciting part, where the scholar and the female ghost were getting intimate, Jiang Miao patted its big head. "Be a good boy, go to sleep."

Fat Tabby: ?

We're about to read the part where the scholar and the female ghost hook up, the candle is blown out, and you're telling me to sleep?

The next second, it fell fast asleep.

Jiang Miao leaped directly out of the window, never taking the ordinary path.

Using the Shrinking the Ground into an Inch technique, she arrived at the City God Temple in no time.

In the dark, the City God shuddered several times.

Damn it all, destiny was coming for him after all!

Jiang Miao didn't waste words; her fingers flicked rapidly, folding a few gold ingots and burning them away. Without even a visible flame, a wisp of smoke drifted straight into the City God's nostrils.

The City God twitched his nose. *I'm inhaling!*

If you ask which family's ingots are the strongest, the Jiang clan's reputation is renowned.

When she finished, Jiang Miao sat cross-legged in front of the City God and leisurely said:

"The ten-year period has arrived; it's time for you to fulfill your promise."

Ten years ago, Jiang Miao, who had lost her memories of the past, had immediately sought out the City God to inquire about her identity.

The old man had bitten his tongue and refused to say.

After being thoroughly beaten up by Jiang Miao, he had wept and confessed that he had promised someone else never to expose the matter, and that person had even forced him to swear a deadly oath that once broken, his body and soul would be completely obliterated.

Jiang Miao couldn't very well force someone to have their body and soul obliterated on the spot, so she had said, "Opportunities are left for those who are prepared. I'll give you ten years to prepare. When the time comes, you can either hang out with me or have your body and soul obliterated, pick one."

City God: ?

Aren't I already hanging out with you, dammit?

Clearly, you're the one who forced me to swear the oath, and now you're forcing me to break it!

Seeing Jiang Miao looking like she would send him back to his ancestral home right now if he didn't agree, he could only give a perfunctory assent.

Anyway, this ancestor had a fickle temperament and never stayed in one place for ten years; by then, who knew where she'd go to wreak havoc on another City God?

Better a fellow Taoist die than this poor priest. Perfect!

At this moment, his ten-year dream was shattered in a single morning. The City God closed his eyes. I'm tired, let the world end!

Jiang Miao was amused.

"Playing the dead pig isn't afraid of boiling water with me?"

With a flick of her fingers, a faint blue flame danced to life, and the City God felt his chrysanthemum tighten.

He couldn't forget it, this ancestor was the one who had used this exact fire to burn his backside back then to force him into swearing the oath.

That feeling... ε(┬┬﹏┬┬)3

In a flash of inspiration, he finally opened his clay mouth.

"I'll hang out with you! I'll hang out with you! But you can't just ignore your little brother's life, right? I can only give you hints, and you have to go find the answer yourself."

A clay bodhisattva opening its mouth to speak, it was as bizarre as bizarre could be.

If Chi Ge were here, he'd pass out from fright again.

Jiang Miao touched her chin, pondering for a moment, then looked at him with disdain.

"As timid as a mouse, I have reason to suspect you bought your way into the civil service. But I'm curious, who is the bastard that forced you to swear that oath? My enemy?"

The City God gnashed his teeth internally. *Yes, that person is a total bastard!*

Outwardly, however, he smiled flatteringly. "Isn't the first hint arriving right now? That person is also in the capital; you should keep an eye out."

Hearing this, Jiang Miao immediately beamed with joy, looking exceedingly smug.

She just knew it, the catalyst to uncovering her identity was right here in the capital!

Her divinations rarely deceived her, except when the "rarely" happened a bit too often...

Delighted, she burned a few more ingots for the City God.

The City God accepted them with a pounding heart. As for what this ancestor would do to him when she eventually realized she'd been conned, he wasn't going to think about it anymore.

A god's life is hard; it's better to go to the beast realm and be a pig.

***

Marquis of Yongning's Residence.

The Marchioness of Yongning, Madam Duan, looked at the Marquis with red, aggrieved eyes.

"This concubine has been married to my lord for fifteen years; does my lord still not know this concubine's character?"

"How, how could you listen to the slander of outsiders and actually come question whether the deaths of Concubine Song and the others had something to do with this concubine? You might as well not have stopped me today and let this concubine die..."

Looking at his wife, who was weeping like a pear blossom in the rain and on the verge of fainting, a wave of guilt washed over the Marquis.

That's right, his wife came from a distinguished family, and his father-in-law was upright and strict. How could the daughter he raised be such a vicious person?

He could only blame himself for letting the young heir's words throw his mind into chaos.

Yet, the scene earlier today when his wife was about to stab herself with a golden hairpin had indeed been truly bizarre, as if controlled by some external force.

He couldn't help but recall the "ghosts" Chi Ge had mentioned.

With complicated emotions, the Marquis reached out to wipe the tears from Madam Duan's face and pulled her into his embrace.

"It was your husband's fault. Concubine Song and the others died mysteriously, and my heart has always felt... It's just that my fate is too harsh and has harmed them."

Madam Duan covered his mouth.

"How could it be the Marquis's fault? They lacked blessings, and it's also because this concubine's temperament is too soft, allowing them to lord it over the estate and thus incur the resentment of the servants, meeting such tragic ends. It's all this concubine's fault."

This wasn't the first time Madam Duan had said things like "they lorded it over the estate."

Yet today, for the first time, the Marquis of Yongning doubted the truth of her words. Leaving aside whether those concubines really were overbearing, would a daughter raised in the Grand Tutor's household really not know how to manage a household?

chapters.title: Go, Scare the Marquis of Yongning Out of His Wits
chapters.content:
The Marquis of Yongning lowered his murky, unreadable gaze and tightened his embrace around her a little more.

"I've been back in the capital for a few days now. Tomorrow, let's go visit your father and mother."

At these words, Madame Duan trembled violently, her face turning instantly pale.

She didn't dare step out of the estate at all; just going out during the day had gotten her entangled by those few bitches.

She had invited a master to perform rituals in the mansion, so they couldn't get in, but outside was a different story...

She feared those bitches were still wandering outside the estate at this very moment. Once entangled by them, she might not have today's good fortune again.

This time, her husband had rendered a great service again and promised to petition for an official title of honor for her. She hadn't even seen the envious looks of those noble ladies yet; how could she die?

Her lowered eyes rolled a few times, and clutching her chest, she said:

"This concubine is in poor health, and I fear that if my parents see me looking like this upon returning to my maiden home, they will worry. It would be better to wait a few days."

The Marquis of Yongning looked at her deeply, but said nothing and agreed.

That night, the main gates of the Marquis of Yongning's mansion were repeatedly battered by the sound of "bang, bang, bang," yet when opened, there was no one outside.

At first, the servants thought it was someone playing a prank, so they guarded behind the door, planning to open it quickly the moment someone knocked.

Yet still there was no one outside, not even a stray cat or dog.

In the blink of an eye, let alone a person, not even a cat or dog could run that fast, could they?

Terrified, the servants tumbled and crawled to report to the Marquis of Yongning.

Madame Duan was shivering with fright, clutching desperately at the Marquis of Yongning as he tried to get up to take a look. "Husband, don't go. This concubine is worried someone is plotting to harm you."

The Marquis of Yongning calmly pried open her fingers and said warmly:

"Wife, do not be afraid. Your husband is righteous and upright; how could he be harmed by someone playing supernatural tricks?"

When he uttered the word "ghost," he deliberately emphasized it.

Madame Duan's heart fluttered. She lunged over, wrapped her arms around his waist, and buried herself piteously in his chest. "Husband, this concubine is scared..."

"Those who do no wrong in life do not fear midnight knocks on the door. I'll go take a look and be right back." The Marquis of Yongning pushed her away, draped a robe over his shoulders, and got out of bed.

Madame Duan forced her limp body to hold up, feeling too guilty to speak further. After he walked far away, she muttered with trembling lips:

"I'm not afraid, I'm not afraid. The master said they cannot get close to my husband..."

Everyone who knew the truth had been dealt with by her. There was absolutely no one in this world who could expose the things she had done. As long as she didn't go out, those few bitches couldn't harm her.

Thinking of this, her mood gradually calmed down.

Tomorrow, she would dispatch her wet nurse to Qingfeng Taoist Temple once more to invite the Daoist priest to perform a ritual. No matter how much silver it cost, she had to get rid of those bitches!

If she never went out, her husband would become suspicious...

Outside the Marquis of Yongning's mansion, Yingge stood with her hands on her hips, scolding the four female ghosts in front of her.

"I told you that the Marquis of Yongning has a murderous aura even stronger than an executioner's. Can you possibly get close to him? But you wouldn't believe me, you just wouldn't believe me. You really have no brains!"

The hanged female ghost went "shh-ha" to pull her tongue back in before she could speak.

Gazing at the ugly ghost in front of her who was missing half her head, she was utterly speechless. How could she have the nerve to say *they* had no brains?

Had she forgotten to look in a mirror?

Besides, one look at her attire showed she wasn't a woman from a respectable family. What qualifications did she have to talk to them?

"This is our business, what does it have to do with you?"

"This is our business, what does it have to do with you?" the other three female ghosts chorused, nodding in agreement.

Even the ghost infant in the belly blinked its eyes in agreement, though unfortunately it could neither speak nor nod.

Yingge tilted her head and thought for a moment. "Oh yeah, what *does* it have to do with me? I was just watching the show. You guys continue, I'll sneak out to watch again tomorrow."

Oops, she had forgotten her main mission while watching the fun. What was it that My Lady had told her to go out and do?

In a fluster, Yingge floated away...

Meanwhile, at the main gates of the Marquis of Yongning's mansion, the Marquis stood guard until dawn, and the knocking never sounded again.

Frowning, he recalled Jiang Miao's words. Could it really be haunted?

Tomorrow he would go inquire where there were adept masters and invite one to the mansion to take a look.

It was a pity the State Preceptor had been in seclusion for many years; otherwise, inviting him to make a trip here would surely bring the truth to light.

After the morning court session, the Marquis of Yongning was pondering whom to ask about finding an adept master when he looked up and spotted Senior Physician Su not far away.

He instantly remembered the young heir's words and hurriedly intercepted him.

"Senior Physician Su, I heard you know about Jiang Miao?"

Upon hearing Jiang Miao's name, Senior Physician Su's shoulders shuddered. With an old, stern face, he waved his hand and said, "I don't know, I don't know, this old man doesn't know her."

With that, he hurried away without even a farewell.

*Damn it, don't let me near anyone bringing up that little star of disaster! She's too much trouble!*

The Marquis of Yongning's face darkened, making him all the more convinced that Chi Ge was pulling his leg.

Seeing Senior Physician Su's attitude toward her as if avoiding venomous snakes and scorpions was enough to show what kind of person she was!

After inquiring for half a day without finding any adept masters, and with his military duties pressing, he put the matter aside.

...

In the inn, Jiang Miao finished reading all the pulp fiction to the chubby orange cat, then held out her hand to Yingge, who was boiling water and brewing tea nearby.

"Where is the pulp fiction you went to steal for me?"

Yingge's hand trembled. Only then did she remember that this was what My Lady had told her to do last night.

She had gotten distracted watching the fun and completely forgot, unable to remember it no matter what, so she had returned crestfallen.

At this moment, she didn't dare conceal the truth and timidly said, "My Lady, as your humble servant passed by the Marquis of Yongning's mansion last night, I watched the commotion for a while and forgot all about it. Please don't be angry, I'll go steal them right now."

"A commotion at the Marquis of Yongning's mansion?"

At these words, both Jiang Miao's and the chubby orange cat's eyes lit up with the fire of gossip.

"Tell me about it."

Yingge curled her lip in disdain and said, "Those female ghosts are stupid to the core. They only know how to crash against the manor gates and don't even know to climb over the walls. Even when I told them, they wouldn't listen."

Jiang Miao and the orange cat exchanged a glance: An idiot calling others idiots, what a rarity.

Still, considering they were her own ghosts, she patiently explained, "The Marquis of Yongning's mansion has had Daoist priests perform rituals, so they can't get in. They were just trying to give people a fright."

"Ah? There are rituals?" Yingge patted her chest in lingering fright. "Good thing they didn't give me a pleasant look; I was originally planning to help them sneak inside to scare people..."

Those female ghosts were actually quite nice.

Jiang Miao rolled her eyes. Had her own revenge been settled yet? She still had the leisure to poke her nose into other people's business.

Yingge floated over timidly and grievance-stricken. "My Lady, can you give your humble servant some good items so I can save face in front of them? They really look down on me."

Jiang Miao rolled her eyes and thought of a plan. "It's not entirely out of the question. Tell them to steal all the pulp fiction in the entire city for me."

Yingge beamed with joy. My Lady was truly wonderful; not only did she help her save face, but she also found her some coolies.

Jiang Miao rummaged through her beggar's bundle, pulled out a piece of white jade, crafted a minor magical artifact on the spot, and handed it to Yingge. "Go on, scare the Marquis of Yongning out of his wits!"

At night.

In the outer courtyard of the Marquis of Yongning's mansion, a terrified scream suddenly rang out.

"A ghost!"

The Marquis of Yongning bolted awake, rushing out with his sword in hand without even putting on his outer robe.

A few flickering clusters of oil lamp light pierced the darkness, and the servants who heard the screams rushed out as well.

An old wet nurse pointed at the hazy, flickering bushes and stammered, trembling all over:

"Song... Song Concubine, I saw Song Concubine..."

chapters.title: The Young Heir = A Flappy-Jawed Gossiper
chapters.content:
Without a second word, the Marquis of Yongning vaulted into the bushes and quickly checked around, but didn't find even a ghost's shadow.

He turned back, his longsword instantly resting against the wet nurse's neck.

He demanded sternly, "What did you see? If you dare to lie, you die!"

The wet nurse's legs went weak, and she collapsed to her knees on the ground, tears and snot streaming down her face.

"Marquis, spare my life! This old slave wouldn't dare lie. Just now, this old slave got up to use the chamber pot, and in a daze, I saw a white figure hanging from that tree."

"This old slave thought it was some drying clothes that had fallen onto the tree and wanted to go pick them up, but when I walked closer, I clearly saw it was Concubine Song."

"Her eyeballs were almost popping out, and her tongue was pulled super long, exactly the same as when she hanged herself that day. This old slave was scared out of my wits, which is why I screamed out loud..."

Hearing this, the servants present all shrank their necks, not daring to look at those bushes ever again.

In the first few days after Concubine Song's death, the mansion had also been haunted. Some people even heard her crying out her grievances, and soon after, those people were sold off by the mistress.

The mistress had invited a Daoist priest to perform rituals, and only then had the mansion quieted down.

How could this be happening again?

The Marquis of Yongning's thick brows furrowed tightly. A moment later, he withdrew his longsword and issued a stern warning to the crowd:

"She must have seen things! Let this matter end here, and no one is allowed to speak of it again!"

The crowd scattered in panic, none daring to utter an extra word. They had been warned by the mistress before; anyone who dared wag their tongue in front of the Marquis would suffer the best fate of being sold away.

Yet not long after, shrieks rang out one after another from the servants' quarters.

This time it was even more terrifying. Some said they saw Concubine Li, whose limbs had been hacked off, crawling toward them.

Others said Concubine Mei was holding a pitch-black bowl of poison and telling them to drink it.

The Marquis of Yongning finally realized this matter was not simple. One person seeing things could be explained away, but it was impossible for everyone to hallucinate at the same time!

As soon as dawn broke, the Marquis of Yongning immediately headed to the Ministry of Punishments, pulled out the case files of the three concubines who had died accidental deaths, and examined them meticulously several times over.

Yet no matter how he looked, he couldn't find a single loophole.

Was the culprit simply too thorough, or had the culprit truly already faced justice?

However, since the mansion was haunted, it meant those concubines held lingering grievances. If this matter wasn't resolved, the household would likely never find peace.

The Marquis of Yongning finally took Chi Ge's words seriously and immediately set off for the Princess's Manor.

Since nothing could be gotten out of Senior Physician Su, Her Highness the Princess should at least grant him some small measure of face.

Chi Ge was just preparing to go find Jiang Miao when he heard a servant report that the Marquis of Yongning was requesting an audience. He was instantly delighted.

His buttocks, which had just left the chair, firmly planted themselves back down.

The Princess looked bewildered. "Didn't I tell you to take bird's nest to Miao Miao? Why haven't you left yet?"

Chi Ge smugly declared, "Your son used divination and calculated that I can make some silver today. Mother, just watch and see."

The Princess looked him up and down. "Oh, how rare. Can you actually make money?"

Chi Ge rubbed his hands together and said with some embarrassment, "To not hide it from Mother, your son owes Miao Miao eighty taels again..."

The Princess extended a finger and poked him fiercely on the forehead, gritting her teeth as she whispered:

"I see you'll be sold off by Miao Miao sooner or later, and you'll even help her count the money!"

Chi Ge stiffened his neck and retorted, "That's impossible, Father said nobody would want me even if I were given away for free."

What a proud thing to say!

The Princess: "..." Should she endure the pain and give birth to another one...

The Marquis of Yongning's arrival interrupted the mother-and-son exchange. After some polite pleasantries, the Marquis cut straight to the point:

"Your Highness, this subject has come to inquire about someone."

The Princess said graciously, "Speak."

The Marquis glanced at Chi Ge. "I heard from the Young Heir that you know Jiang Miao, who was driven out of the Marquis of Xuanjiao's household, is capable of catching ghosts?"

The Princess also glanced at Chi Ge. It had only been two days, and her little hound had already become Miao Miao's running dog, going around publicizing her?

She asked the Marquis, "I wonder why the Marquis is asking about this?"

The Marquis was somewhat surprised. Had the Young Heir not mentioned his family's affairs to the Princess?

Had he changed his gossipy habits?

Hesitating for a moment, he poured out the whole story so that the Princess would understand the severity of the matter and thus not conceal information about Jiang Miao.

"Such a thing actually happened?"

The Princess was so surprised she almost failed to conceal the gleam of gossip in her eyes.

"Your wife is truly formidable. Even though we are in the same capital, this palace has never heard of several lives being lost in the Marquis's household."

The Marquis felt a wave of awkwardness, momentarily unable to tell whether she was praising him or mocking him.

Chi Ge let out a huff.

"Mother, you must show mercy and tell him about Miao Miao's abilities. I kindly told him, and not only did he refuse to believe me, he almost beat your son up!"

The Marquis felt even more awkward and immediately understood that Chi Ge's words were not false. He hurriedly stood up, cupped his fists, and apologized.

"The Young Heir jests. How would I dare use force against you? It was I who listened to one-sided accounts and mistakenly assumed Jiang Miao was, as rumors say, a... a..."

Thinking that he would likely need to ask Jiang Miao for help, harsh words simply couldn't pass his lips.

"Unprincipled, a charlatan, of infamous reputation." Chi Ge slanted a look at him. "What's hard to say? I already told Miao Miao all of it."

The Marquis: "..."

He was still that same flappy-jawed gossiper!

The Princess let out a "pfft" of laughter, rubbed her temples, and said, "Then the Marquis had better prepare to bleed heavily. When that girl asks for silver, her mouth is bigger than a lion's."

The Marquis's attention wasn't on the silver; instead, he asked with joy, "Judging by Your Highness's words, Jiang Miao really can catch ghosts?"

The Princess nodded slightly.

Looking at him reproachfully, she said, "Miao Miao is a good girl, and the Marquis is also a person of discernment. How could you judge a person's character based solely on what others say?"

At this moment, the Marquis lowered his posture to the extreme and hurriedly replied, "It was this subject who was shallow. I hope Your Highness will not take offense."

The Princess sighed.

"What does it matter whether this palace takes offense or not? What you should worry about is whether Miao Miao takes offense."

That girl was extremely petty. Because Senior Physician Su had snapped at her a few times, she had kicked him right in the chest.

"To tell you the truth, after Miao Miao performed her ritual, we actually saw ghosts. On that day, this palace witnessed with her own eyes how she brought that female ghost to absolute submission. Entrusting your household's matter to her will certainly resolve it."

Hearing this, the Marquis felt a surge of excitement and bowed deeply to the ground.

"Many thanks to Her Highness the Princess for guidance."

The Princess unhurriedly raised her teacup, lowered her eyes to take a light sip, and calmly said, "This is the Marquis's family matter after all. You had better make your own decision, Marquis."

Chi Ge was terrified that Jiang Miao's business deal would fall through. He abruptly stood up and declared with righteous indignation, "Princes break the law the same as commoners. Under the bright blue sky, does the Marquis intend to disregard the law and shield his wife?"

A chill ran through the Marquis's heart.

If Jiang Miao's abilities were real, once the human and ghost sides confronted each other and pinned the crime on his wife, he feared even he wouldn't be able to cover it up.

Yet leaving the house to be haunted without intervention wasn't an option either.

After pondering for a long time, he said, "I must ask the Young Heir to speak with your master and invite her to my mansion to take a look."

It would be best if she could send them away; as for the rest, they could talk about it later.

Chi Ge instantly beamed with joy.

"That's more like it! I knew the Marquis wasn't some muddle-headed fool who can't tell right from wrong. Five hundred taels, that's my agency fee."

The Princess spat out a mouthful of tea, completely losing her composure.

So *this* was how this little hound made money?

This business acumen took after his father, unconventional to say the least.

chapters.title: Her family really does have billions in assets to inherit!
chapters.content:
The Marquis of Yongning was stunned. Five hundred taels? Just for a referral fee?

How much would the master herself cost?

Though the emperor's rewards were bountiful, he had spent most of them aiding wounded soldiers and the orphans of those who had fallen in battle...

Thinking of his household expenses, he felt a sudden tightness in his chest.

Perhaps he should just let the ghosts keep haunting the place? Maybe they would eventually get tired of it?

It wasn't impossible for humans and ghosts to coexist. They weren't strangers, after all...

Wasn't saving some silver to help the soldiers a better idea?

Seeing the hesitation on his face and fearing the deal would fall through, Chi Ge anxiously urged, "If you think it's too pricey, I'll knock off two hundred taels. That's my absolute lowest price! My master is a bit difficult to talk to, and high-level experts always have their quirks. You understand!"

The Princess secretly sighed.

She retracted her previous thought.

When it came to business negotiation tactics and psychological warfare, this brat understood absolutely nothing. He had inherited zero of his father's quick-witted, foxy cleverness!

He must have taken after her eldest brother, whose IQ halved the moment he saw money... Her heart was so tired.

The Marquis of Yongning looked ashamed. "If your master's price is too high, I'm afraid I won't be able to afford it."

Chi Ge's eyes rolled around, and rubbing his hands together, he suggested, "How about this: you pay me three hundred taels as a referral fee first, and I'll have my master come over to take a look at your estate. You two can discuss the price then. If you can't reach an agreement, I'll refund half of the referral fee."

Even if he had to refund half, he'd still have one hundred and fifty taels left. After paying back the eighty taels he owed Jiang Miao, he'd still make a profit of seventy taels. If he stayed vigilant and didn't let her trick him again, he could easily scrape by until next month's stipend!

The Marquis of Yongning thought about it and decided it was within his tolerance, so he fished out three one-hundred-tael silver notes.

Chi Ge reached out to take them, but the Marquis clutched the notes tightly, refusing to let go as he sought reassurance one last time.

"You must make it clear to your master that the price can be negotiated later."

"No problem, I'll bring my master to your house today," Chi Ge promised readily, finally snatching the silver notes into his grip.

After the Marquis of Yongning left, the Princess slapped Chi Ge across the forehead and scolded him with her hands on her hips.

"Is that head of yours just for show? He hadn't even said anything, yet you went ahead and lowered the price!"

Chi Ge raised a finger, shook it, and said with a mysterious air,

"You don't understand. I'm fishing here. First, I hook the fish; once it's on the line, it's just meat on my cutting board! Besides, I can still hit Miao Miao up for an agency fee!"

With that, he picked up the bird's nest the Princess had prepared for Jiang Miao and strutted away, head held high!

The Princess blinked. The brat's retreating figure suddenly looked so tall and imposing. Could this be her business acumen passed down to him?

Wait, no, when did the brat become Miao Miao's apprentice?

Can Taoist priests get married and have children?

Her family really does have billions in assets to inherit!

Two quarters of an hour later, Jiang Miao was eating bird's nest while sighing inwardly. In a society where imperial power reigned supreme, having money meant nothing; you had to have status!

In this day and age, even bird's nest was a tribute item. Regular marquises and dukes couldn't even afford to eat it, you had to attain the rank of a commandery princess or something.

No, being a commandery princess was too weak; at the very least, you had to be the Imperial Preceptor!

Chi Ge finished explaining the Marquis of Yongning's request.

Jiang Miao waved a hand casually. "It's fine, money isn't important."

It didn't matter if the Marquis was reluctant to pay in silver; she could trade for other things. Those would be much more valuable than silver!

*Money isn't important? Then why did you fleece my family of six thousand taels?* Chi Ge thought to himself.

But he didn't dare say that out loud. Swallowing his conscience, he buttered her up: "I've appreciated your noble disposition, treating wealth like mere dirt, ever since I was a kid! So, you won't object to me taking a commission, right?"

"My throat was practically dry before he finally agreed to invite you over to take a look. I've contributed both hard work and merit."

Jiang Miao swallowed her final mouthful of bird's nest, crossed her arms, and cast a sidelong glance at him.

"Do I look like gold to you?"

Chi Ge nodded earnestly. "Back when you were just a mediocre little good-for-nothing in the Marquis of Xuan远's household, you finally started shining. So intrinsically, you must be gold."

As long as she gave him a commission, he'd be willing to praise her for having culture even if she said 1+1=5!

Jiang Miao: "..." *You got played around by a good-for-nothing like me, and you still have the nerve to call me a good-for-nothing?*

She sneered.

"You've got it wrong. I'm pure iron, the iron of an iron rooster!"

Chi Ge: "..."

Good thing he hadn't apprenticed himself to her; following an iron rooster meant all you got to eat was farts!

Still, live and learn. Next time, he'd just have to demand a bigger referral fee!

With so many wealthy and powerful households in the capital, which family didn't have a few souls who had died unjustly?

Before long, the Koi Duo set off for the Marquis of Yongning's estate, each harboring their own secret agendas.

As soon as they stepped into the front courtyard, Jiang Miao's gaze sharpened. "There's evil Qi!"

Chi Ge shuddered, quickly hiding behind her and grabbing her clothes as he looked around in a panic. "Where? Where is the evil Qi?"

Jiang Miao pointed at a group of people walking toward them, amongst whom was a Taoist priest. "Him!"

The Marquis of Yongning looked at Jiang Miao and Chi Ge with a complicated expression, his gaze finally resting on the half of Chi Ge's body that was poorly concealed.

He regretted it!

His wife had invited Master Changsongzi of Qingfeng Temple to perform rituals and draw talismans, even giving everyone in the household an anti-ghost talisman, and the whole package cost only a hundred taels.

And yet, as a dignified Marquis, he had been conned out of three hundred taels by a young marquis who hadn't even reached adulthood... His heart ached.

Madame Duan was unaware of the agreement between the Marquis and Chi Ge, but she recognized Jiang Miao at a glance.

Instantly, her mood soured. She furrowed her brows in disgust and snapped, "What are you doing here at my house?"

Before Jiang Miao could reply, she harshly scolded the butler who had led them in.

"Steward He, why do you let just anyone into the estate? Such a cheap, lowly wretch will defile the grounds of our Marquis's residence. Why haven't you thrown her out yet?"

A cheap, lowly wretch?

Defiling the grounds of the Marquis's residence?

Jiang Miao wasn't even angry yet, but Chi Ge exploded with rage.

Abandoning any fear of evil Qi at the moment, he leaped forward, his face dark as he barked,

"Who are you calling a cheap, lowly wretch? Is that how the old Grand Tutor taught his daughter to speak? Uttering filth the moment you open your mouth, this young marquis thinks *you* are the one defiling the Marquis of Yongning's estate!"

Chi Ge held a noble status and had grown up accustomed to looking down on others. Even though he was only a fourteen-year-old boy, putting on airs like this was quite intimidating.

Only then did Madame Duan clearly see who the speaker was.

Her expression stiffened, and she hastily whipped up a strained smile.

"This humble wife was unaware of Your Lordship's arrival; I hope the Young Marquis will forgive this offense..."

Her heart was pounding frantically. *Oh no, I've inadvertently offended the Young Marquis.*

She mentally cursed: *What qualifications does that Jiang Miao have to be walking alongside the Young Marquis, who is more precious than imperial princes in this dynasty?*

*Isn't she supposed to be reduced to swindling people on the streets?*

Chi Ge also noticed the slender Taoist priest standing behind her.

The man wore a red Taoist robe embroidered with an intricate Bagua diagram, and on his back he carried a wooden sword with a gleaming, polished hilt. He had a fair face, long beard, and refined features.

Right now, he was looking at them indifferently, his gaze carrying a trace of hard-to-detect contempt and disdain. Aloof and reserved, he cut the exact image of an otherworldly master.

After his intimate contact with ghosts, Chi Ge held a deep sense of awe toward such people, and his aggressive aura deflated instantly.

Still, he stiffened his neck and lodged an aggrieved protest with the Marquis of Yongning.

"One matter should not involve two masters. The Marquis clearly agreed to let my master come take a look, so why did you go find someone else?"

Having just finished psyching himself up, treating the one hundred and fifty taels as money thrown to the dogs, the Marquis of Yongning had calmed down.

He replied neither servilely nor overbearingly, "This is Master Changsongzi, the abbot of Qingfeng Temple. He was invited by my wife; I was unaware of it beforehand."

"However, since Master Changsongzi has already handled the affairs of my household, we won't trouble the Young Marquis's master."

"Handled?"

Jiang Miao laughed aloud.

She pointed at Changsongzi. "Him?"

With a solemn expression, Changsongzi chanted, "Immeasurable Heavenly尊," and said proudly, "I advise this good citizen not to be arrogant and insult this poor Taoist, otherwise the Heavenly Dao will punish you!"

Jiang Miao scoffed. "You?"

"There is no place for the likes of you to speak here!" Madame Duan lifted her chin and looked at Jiang Miao with loathing.

"Jiang Miao, others may not know your background, but this Madam does. No matter what tricks you used to swindle the Young Marquis, this Madam advises you to pull back from the brink before it's too late, otherwise... Heh..."

Jiang Miao rolled her eyes so hard they nearly vanished.

"Heh your sister! Big babies, come out and give her a 'heh'!"

chapters.title: Divine Sword, Divine Bitchy Attitude
chapters.content:
Madam Duan: "?" She didn't have a sister...

Jiang Miao gave a wave of her small hand, and a flash passed before everyone's eyes, a flicker of firelight seen only dimly.

A moment later, five female ghosts appeared in the courtyard.

Three of them, whole in limb, clung tightly to Madam Duan's body, the hanged ghost's long tongue draping right across her face.

The one with no hands or feet was wriggling its way toward her with great effort.

Only Yingge stood off to the side, eyes bright and wide, her face half lit up with excitement.

Yes, finally, my lord was making her move!

"Ahh..." The Marquise of Yongning locked eyes with the hanged ghost, her eyeballs nearly popping out, and let out a shrill, terrible scream before fainting dead away.

Chang Songzi rubbed his eyes in shock, then collapsed limply to the ground, shrieking in terror.

"Gh, ghost, it's a real ghost!"

The Marquis of Yongning stared at the four female ghosts in utter shock. Even he, who had killed countless men on the battlefield, felt his scalp crawl at the sight.

"Madam Song, Madam Li, Madam Mei, Madam Feng!"

Jiang Miao tilted her chin toward the ghost infant. "And there's your son too. Surprised?"

The Marquis of Yongning stepped forward urgently, his gaze locked on the ghost infant's small face, straining to make out its features through that murky darkness.

He suddenly grew emotional. This child really did look like him...

Madam Feng reached out and pressed the ghost infant back into her belly, glaring at the Marquis with disdain. He didn't deserve to look at his son!

The Marquis's heart ached as if cut with a knife. If that child had been born safely, wouldn't he be old enough now to study martial arts and letters alongside him?

Was it truly Madam Duan who had killed the two of them?

He asked, his voice hoarse, "Madam Feng, back when your labor went wrong..."

"Went wrong? It was your kind and generous wife who ordered her wet nurse to drug Sister Feng, leaving her too weak to give birth, and that's why she and the child both died!"

Madam Song cut in sharply, her face full of resentment.

This man's judgment was hopelessly one sided. Back when she'd noticed Madam Duan's malice toward them and hinted at it delicately, he'd cursed her out thoroughly, accusing her of slandering his wife out of spite, and docked three months of her stipend.

Ha, before those three months were even up, she'd been hanged in the front hall by his kind and generous wife.

She wished more than anything she could whip her tongue out and strangle him with it right now.

She hated that ghosts simply didn't have the strength to harm the living.

The four female ghosts, armed with the little talisman Yingge had given them, weren't the least bit afraid of the Marquis's aura of killing intent, and unleashed their grievances all at once.

Madam Mei gave a chilling little laugh. "My lord, how surprising that you still recognize this concubine. You once said you loved this fair, snow white skin of mine best. I imagine you still love this complexion now, since Madam Duan always did understand your tastes so well, didn't she?"

Madam Li also wriggled her way closer to the Marquis. She'd never been able to get near him before, but maybe now she could get a bite in.

Madam Feng gritted her teeth. "Why bother wasting words on him? Let's kill Madam Duan first!"

"Hang her!"

"Poison her!"

"Cut off her hands and feet!"

"Drug her!"

The four ghosts shouted at Yingge all at once.

Yingge rolled up her sleeves. "Got it!"

She was so excited, finally her time to shine had come!

She pulled out the rope, poison, blade, and drug she'd prepared and charged forward.

Jiang Miao: "..."

She slapped a talisman on Yingge's back without even turning around. "Freeze!"

Foolish ghost, are you just here to be someone else's blade so you can look good doing it?

By this point, the Marquis of Yongning could no longer deceive himself; the deaths of these concubines had nothing to do with Madam Duan.

His body rigid, he slowly turned to look at the unconscious Madam Duan, then said in a heavy voice to the steward:

"Go, fetch the Grand Tutor here."

Fortunately the steward had already seen Consort Mei's ghost once before, so he had at least a little experience and didn't wet himself in fright. He hurried off wiping sweat to fetch the man.

Chi Ge shouted vaguely, "Miaomiao, tell him how much this is going to cost first."

The Marquis of Yongning also came back to himself and turned to look at Jiang Miao.

He truly couldn't connect this strange little Daoist priestess in front of him with someone of great skill, but he understood it was through her methods that he'd been able to see the concubines at all.

He cupped his fists toward her. "May I ask, can the master release their souls to reincarnation?"

Jiang Miao narrowed her eyes. "Small matter."

The Marquis felt a wave of relief. His concubines had died so tragically; the least he could do besides bringing Madam Duan to justice was to let them go to their next lives in peace.

Even if it cost him his entire fortune.

Bracing himself to be charged an enormous fee, he asked tentatively, "May I ask how much silver the master requires?"

"Talking about money, how vulgar."

Jiang Miao gave him a reproachful look. "If the Marquis is truly grateful, just give me that sword you've got gathering dust in your storehouse."

The Marquis's eyes narrowed.

How did she know there was a sword in his storehouse?

That sword was something he'd dug up years ago while digging traps on the border.

He'd examined it many times and never been able to tell whether it was valuable or not; it was completely covered in bronze rust, and he couldn't even pull it out of its sheath.

He'd only brought it back because the sheath was carved with mysterious inscriptions and gave off an ancient aura.

He'd nearly forgotten about it entirely until she brought it up today.

Could that sword be some kind of ancient divine artifact?

Seeing that he hadn't answered, Jiang Miao pouted. "What, can't bear to part with it?"

The Marquis suddenly saw the situation clearly.

However precious that sword might be, it was still just a lifeless object. To have the chance to form a good connection with someone of such power was a bargain he could hardly pass up.

No need to bankrupt himself after all.

He turned at once and personally went to the storehouse to retrieve the sword.

Jiang Miao's eyes lit up as she stared at the sword, and the moment she took it, she drew it out with a single swift motion.

The Marquis only saw a flash of cold light, and the air around them seemed to grow noticeably colder.

The four female ghosts let out a scream and huddled together trembling, staring at the sword in terror.

Instinctively, they could sense the intensely yang, unyielding energy radiating from that sword, which was exactly what could overpower them.

Madam Li quickly wriggled her way into the middle of the group to hide, oh heavens, that scared the ghost out of her!

The Marquis was utterly astonished.

This little girl looked like she didn't have any strength at all, so how had she pulled that sword free?

He'd once had the strongest soldier in his army try, and even he hadn't managed it.

Jiang Miao gave the long sword a rakish whistle. "First of the Month, oh First of the Month, would you look at this damned fate of ours, meeting again, aren't we?"

The glinting cold sword let out a mournful hum, its glow dimming instantly.

Chi Ge figured that if the sword could talk, it would probably just say "bad luck."

In fact First of the Month's actual thought had one more line to it: damn it, of all the terrible fates, ending up in this jinx's hands!

Chi Ge asked curiously, "This sword's called First of the Month? Why not Fifteenth?"

Jiang Miao explained with great enthusiasm.

"Funny you should ask, there really is a Fifteenth."

"First of the Month has four younger brothers, named Fifteenth, Wait a Moment, Show Mercy, and I Concede Defeat. First and Fifteenth have the worst tempers, all about looking death in the eye and not backing down from a fight."

"The last three each get more cowardly than the last, and the moment things look bad they immediately shout 'Wait a moment! Show mercy! I concede defeat!'"

Chi Ge's face twitched, clearly not buying any of it.

"Yeah right, a sword with a temper? That can talk? Have it say something, let's hear it!"

"Zzzt!"

First of the Month let out a piercing buzzing hum and shook violently, how dare you look down on a sword?

It wanted to fly over and give him a good slash.

Chi Ge clutched his head and let out a pained yelp, blood immediately gushing from his nose...

He glared resentfully at First of the Month. Damn it, why is a sword this petty?

Jiang Miao tapped the blade with a finger. "Naughty. Who taught you to bully the weak?"

First of the Month instantly behaved itself.

The weak Chi Ge wiped his bloody nose and casually smeared it on the Marquis, gazing at Jiang Miao with pure admiration.

He was starting to think about asking to become her disciple again...

The Marquis of Yongning wanted to kneel before Jiang Miao.

A living Bodhisattva!

To think he'd unknowingly brought an evil object into his own home, fortunate that the master's discerning eye had caught it and taken it away, otherwise if First of the Month ever went berserk, who could possibly stand against it?

chapters.title: Filial Piety Reaching New Heights
chapters.content:
Chang Songzi, paralyzed on the ground as he watched this scene, felt his little heart nearly burst with terror. Carefully and stealthily, he began inching toward the courtyard gate.

Based on his years of swindling, no, traveling the pugilistic world, his intuition told him he could not afford to provoke this fellow practitioner.

Of the thirty-six stratagems, running away is the best!

Jiang Miao seemed to have eyes on the side of her head. Grasping Chu Yi, she casually flicked her wrist.

In an instant, the red Taoist robe on Chang Songzi shattered into fragments and drifted to the ground, revealing a set of undergarments covered in patches...

Jiang Miao looked at him sideways.

"Lam Ching-ying caught ghosts his whole life and could only wear a yellow robe. What rank are you? How dare you wear a red one?①"

Chang Songzi hugged his body and shivered, not even daring to feel heartbroken over the red robe he had spent a fortune to have made.

It sounded like that Lam Ching-ying was a truly supreme expert, yet spoken from this little Taoist nun's mouth, he sounded like a little brother. That meant this little Taoist nun was even more formidable than the one surnamed Lam!

Not to be provoked! Absolutely not to be provoked!

Wiping away tears, he cried:

"This humble one is just trying to earn a mouthful of food. Your Excellency, in your great magnanimity, please just treat this humble one as a fart and let me go..."

Jiang Miao kicked him into the corner.

"Magical girls don't fart. Stay on the side and wait for sentencing!"

With that, she flicked Chu Yi forward, and Chu Yi obediently hovered right beside Chang Songzi's neck, a mere 0.01 centimeters away from his carotid artery.

If he dared to run, it would immediately pierce his throat.

Madam Duan, who had slowly regained consciousness, happened to witness this scene. Her eyes rolled back, and she promptly fainted again.

Chi Ge: "..."

He looked at the Marquis of Yongning and sneered, "Your wife is truly fragile. Weak and wicked, quite a rare find."

Jiang Miao suddenly stared at him. Why had the parents' palace at the Riri-Yue corners of this guy's forehead suddenly turned greenish-blue?

She pinched her fingers and calculated rapidly.

Solemnly, she said, "Chi Ge, something has happened to your father. Hurry home and take a look."

Chi Ge: ???

His heart began to beat wildly. "No, you're joking, right?"

Jiang Miao unceremoniously dug out a piece of white jade and shoved it into his hand. "Hurry up, place this white jade right against your old man's chest. I'll come over as soon as I'm done here."

Chi Ge finally believed Jiang Miao wasn't joking with him and asked anxiously, "How much longer are you going to be messing around?"

Jiang Miao glanced at him. "What's the panic? Your old man isn't going to die just yet."

Chi Ge heaved a sigh of relief, patting his chest. "Scared the heir to death. Then I'll watch the end before I leave."

If he didn't get to see Madam Duan confront the female ghosts, he wouldn't feel satisfied...

The Marquis of Yongning twitched the corner of his eye, suddenly feeling that not having a son might not be such a bad thing.

Having no heir to carry on the family line was still better than being angered to an untimely death by a rebellious brat, right?

Jiang Miao gave a嘿嘿 (hehei) chuckle. "Fine. Three hundred taels of hush money, otherwise I'll tell your mother that you didn't go back to see your father just because you wanted to watch the show."

Chi Ge clutched the agent's fee that hadn't even grown warm yet, and raged, "Does your ancestor know your conscience is this black? One hundred taels at most, and not a single copper coin more!"

As he spoke, he slapped two silver notes into her hand. "One hundred taels for hush money, eighty taels returned to you, give me twenty taels change!"

The Marquis of Yongning looked at this one and then at that one, somewhat unable to comprehend the dynamic between this master and disciple.

A teacher for one day is a father for life, what kind of karmic sin did Grandmaster Jiang commit to take in such a rebellious disciple?

Just as they were talking, the steward and the Elder Grand Tutor hurried over.

The old man had a head of silvery hair, looked spirited and robust, and walked like the wind, leaving the steward behind by several large steps.

He wore the yellow riding jacket personally bestowed by the Emperor, charging over with an imposing and fierce aura.

He slapped his chest with loud *pa-pa* sounds and demanded in a full, resonant voice:

"Didn't you say the Marquis's estate is haunted? Where's the ghost? Roll on out and let this old man take a look!!!"

The steward exchanged a meaningful glance with the Marquis of Yongning, signaling that he hadn't told him about Madam Duan's affair.

The Marquis of Yongning understood and gave a junior's bow to the Elder Grand Tutor.

"Father-in-law, please keep calm..."

The old man caught sight of his beloved daughter collapsed on the ground, and his expression instantly turned furious.

He harshly interrupted the Marquis, grabbed him by the collar, and questioned, "What did you do to my girl?"

The Marquis of Yongning was, after all, a heavily trusted high official and major general; how could he tolerate such discourtesy?

Frowning, he broke free from the old man's grip, his expression turning cold as well.

"Today, I invited Father-in-law here precisely to let you see with your own eyes what good deeds your fine daughter has done!"

The old man narrowed his eyes and scanned his surroundings, then caught sight of the disheveled Chang Songzi, causing his heart to skip a beat.

Could it be that his daughter was caught red-handed committing adultery with someone?

No, this weakling looked like a pauper at first glance, and more importantly, he wasn't even as good-looking as his son-in-law. His daughter really had poor taste.

With this speculation, his imposing aura weakened by thirty percent.

Still maintaining his airs, he asked, "Then tell me what good deeds my daughter has done."

The Marquis of Yongning cupped his fists in salute to Jiang Miao. "Please cast your spell, Master..."

"Hold on!" The old man looked suspiciously at Jiang Miao. "Isn't this the Marquis of Xuanyuan's daughter? What kind of master is she?"

Suddenly recalling the gossip that had been spreading like wildfire recently,

he flicked his wide sleeve and rebuked with a stern face, "The trick of haunting the Marquis's estate must be her doing, right? As a dignified Marquis of Yongning, you're actually being led around by the nose by a naive, wet-behind-the-ears little girl, simply absurd!"

Yingge gave a "heh" and abruptly floated in front of the old man. "Daring to scold my Lord, old man, do you want to die?"

The Elder Grand Tutor leaped backward a step, scanning his surroundings vigilantly. "Who's speaking?"

He had heard it clearly, it was a woman's voice, yet that abandoned daughter of the Marquis of Xuanyuan hadn't opened her mouth at all.

Where did this voice come from?

Jiang Miao rubbed her fingers, conjuring a tiny cluster of flames that flickered and vanished.

The next instant, the old man saw a female ghost missing half her head, nose-to-nose with him, just a hair's breadth away from pressing against his face.

His eyes rolled back, and he fainted dead away from fright.

The Marquis of Yongning: "..."

Jiang Miao let out a "pfft" of laughter.

So Madam Duan's habit of fainting at the drop of a hat wasn't an act; it was genetic.

She said to the Marquis of Yongning:

"Sorry, I actually don't like to laugh, unless I can't help it."

Only after the Elder Grand Tutor had passed out did Chi Ge dare to make a sound, muttering, "This old man is still as annoying as ever!"

He casually picked up a potted flower, pulled it out by the roots, shook off the dirt, and scooped a basin of water from the pond.

*Splash!* He poured it right over the heads of the Elder Grand Tutor and Madam Duan.

His dad was still waiting for Jiang Miao to save him; he didn't have time to wait for them to wake up on their own.

Manual fast-forward.

Stung by the cold water, the Elder Grand Tutor and Madam Duan woke up simultaneously, violently sitting up in the exact same motion.

Too impatient for their nonsense, Chi Ge pointed at the four female ghosts and shouted loudly:

"You, you, you, and you, hurry up and come confront Madam Duan! The sooner you finish, the sooner this Heir can wrap up and clock out!"

Only then did the Elder Grand Tutor notice there were other people in the courtyard.

No, other *ghosts*.

He recognized one of the ghosts; she was his own daughter's distant cousin, whom he had personally dispatched people to escort from their hometown to the capital.

"Song Wan, aren't, aren't you dead?"

Song Wan whooshed right up in front of him.

"Do I look alive to you?"

The old man's hair stood on end all over his body, and he kicked his legs as he scrambled backward rapidly. "Don't come closer..."

Terrified that the old man would faint from fright again and delay him from going home to see his father, Chi Ge quickly stopped Song Wan.

"Stop scaring him. Start with you, tell us how Madam Duan harmed you!"

*Note ①: According to folk legends: 1st-rank Taoists wear gray robes, 2nd-rank lay practitioners wear blue robes, 3rd-rank True Immortals wear black robes, 4th-rank Celestial Masters wear yellow robes, 5th-rank Immortal Masters wear red robes, 6th-rank Taoist Ancestors wear purple robes, and above the 6th rank are white robes.*

---

chapters.title: Beat the Son and Then Set Off
chapters.content:
Song Wan bowed toward Jiang Miao, thanking her for giving the few of them a chance to clear their names.

Then, pointing furiously at Madam Duan, she said:

"Two years ago, just as the Marquis set off for the frontier, Madam Duan couldn't wait to instruct her wet nurse and my maid Cuiliu to suffocate me in the middle of the night, hang me from the crossbeam, and then make Cuiliu the scapegoat. Madam Duan first ripped out Cuiliu's tongue so she couldn't argue her case, and reported to the authorities that because I usually mistreated Cuiliu, she took revenge on me."

Song Wan spoke fluently, explaining the cause and effect in just a few words.

The Marquis of Yongning's face turned ashen, and he asked through clenched teeth, "Why did Madam Duan kill you?"

Song Wan grew even more furious, shrieking shrilly:

"Does the Marquis still want to protect this poisonous viper at a time like this? Why kill me? Could the Marquis possibly think she was truly willing to share her husband with others?"

"Whenever you rested in any of our rooms for even one extra night, Madam Duan would secretly torment us behind the scenes. It's not like we never told you, why come asking a ghost now?!"

"I didn't! That's not true!"

Regaining her wits, Madam Duan hurriedly defended herself. "Husband, please do not listen to her lies! If concubine were truly as she claims, why would concubine bother personally arranging concubines for you?"

Jiang Miao, having somehow dug out an oil pancake, was munching on it and mumbled vaguely, "A whore wanting to set up a memorial arch." *(T/N: meaning someone wanting to commit a vile act while maintaining a virtuous reputation)*

"Shut your mouth! What kind of thing are you? It's not your turn to speak here!" The Elder Grand Tutor's face was as black as the bottom of a wok. He didn't dare scold a ghost, but couldn't he scold this destitute outcast of a Jiang Miao?

Jiang Miao glanced at him. "I generally don't hit old men, unless I can't help it!"

With that, she raised her right leg, and without using any apparent force, kicked the old man right next to Chang Songzi. Chu Yi immediately pivoted, its sword tip resting against his neck.

A lethal weapon that moves by itself!!!

The Elder Grand Tutor stared in terror, clutching his stomach in a cold sweat of fear as aggrieved tears streamed from his eyes and mouth.

Madam Duan shrieked wildly, "Husband, kill her quickly! She's a demon..."

The limbless Madam Li squirmed over to her side, saying eerily, "Madam, you talk too much. Your screaming is making concubine very annoyed. I want to bite you."

Frightened out of her wits, Madam Duan turned pale as paper, collapsing onto the ground and trembling at the corners of her lips, unable to utter a single word for a long time.

Suppressing the disgust toward Madam Duan deep in her heart, the Marquis of Yongning asked Madam Li and the others:

"How did you all die?"

"Is the Marquis blind? I was personally fed poison by your good wife. Would the Marquis like to taste some?" Madam Mei sneered.

Yingge considerately floated over, handed a packet of arsenic to the Marquis of Yongning, and looked at him eagerly.

The Marquis of Yongning: "..."

Madam Feng's eye rims turned red as she said with grief and indignation, "When I was in labor, Madam Duan personally brought over a bowl of medicine, claiming it was ginseng soup, and fed it to me. Who knew it was actually a drug to induce deep sleep? Pity my child, who never even got to see the light of day, and died along with me..."

The Marquis of Yongning's gaze fell upon her still-prominently rounded belly, and his own eyes turned red.

Protruding veins bulged on the back of his tightly clenched fists as he felt his heart being savagely pierced by a sharp awl, strike after strike, hurting so much that he could barely stand steady.

He spoke with remorse, "It was my fault for failing to recognize people's true colors, for trusting Madam Duan too much and causing you all to die unjustly. It's my fault! I promise, I will definitely return justice to you!"

Hearing this, the four concubines all fell silent.

At the same time, they felt the resentment weighing upon their hearts dissipate by a fraction.

What they wanted most was simply justice; they had only thought of destroying Madam Duan for revenge as a last resort. Now, their wish was finally fulfilled.

The Marquis of Yongning slowly turned his head to look at Madam Duan.

Husband and wife for ten years, and only today did he see through this wife, who had always been gentle and kind in his heart, to realize she possessed the heart of a scorpion.

He had never blamed her for being unable to bear him children; even after taking concubines, he had never favored them over his wife, and moreover, feeling indebted to her, he had always given her the utmost respect and dignity.

What more was she dissatisfied with?

Disappointment, heartache, disgust... a complex mixture of emotions converged in his eyes.

Madam Duan didn't even dare to meet his gaze.

Taking a deep breath, the Marquis of Yongning instructed the steward in a deep voice, "Go invite the Magistrate of Shuntian Prefecture to judge this case!"

"Hold on!" Seeing that the general trend was lost, yet still hoping to save his daughter's life, the Elder Grand Tutor anxiously said, "Ask the Marquis of Yongning to write a letter of divorce! This old man will personally take my daughter back, and we won't even want her dowry, consider it compensation to you!"

Chu Yi hesitated slightly. The little demon star didn't say she wanted to poke this old man, so should it poke him or not?

Jiang Miao looked at the Marquis of Yongning with a half-smile.

The Marquis of Yongning gave the Elder Grand Tutor a cold look. "Since the Grand Tutor has disregarded state law, this Marquis will report it to His Majesty. This matter must be handled impartially; you need say no more."

The Elder Grand Tutor instantly slumped, tears streaming down unceasingly. "I only have this one daughter, I'm begging you..."

Pointing at the four ghosts of Madam Li, the Marquis of Yongning raged, "Did the four of them not have fathers or mothers? I am also the father of my child!"

Jiang Miao nodded slightly. *Not bad, you actually have your head screwed on right.*

She clapped her hands at Chi Ge, who was watching with great relish.

"Let's go, your old man is about to not hold on much longer."

Chi Ge's expression shifted. "Ah, then hurry up!"

Jiang Miao fished out a stack of talismans and handed them to the Marquis of Yongning. "Later when the Magistrate arrives, burn these talismans and you'll be able to see them. Once I'm done handling things, I'll come back tonight to send them off to reincarnation."

The Marquis of Yongning expressed his thanks.

Jiang Miao lifted her foot and left.

Chang Songzi weakly raised his hand. "E-Expert, what about me?"

*Wuwuwu*, that evil sword was still there; he didn't dare run away on his own...

Jiang Miao dropped two words: "Wait."

How utterly annoying, every single one of them was a pest. She suspected she'd die of overwork and sudden death before she even remembered who she was!

She'd be leaving even earlier than the Marquis of Xuanyuan's family!

No sooner had the koi duo stepped out of the Marquis's estate than Chi Ge said rapidly:

"My dad is even richer than my mom. Later you should ask for a bit more, and split some with me. Fifty percent is not too much, ten percent is not too little, I'm very easy to talk to."

Actually, he wasn't all that worried about his old man; with Jiang Miao around, dying was harder than living.

That's right, he was blindly worshiping her just like that!

Inside the Eldest Princess's Estate, a whole crowd of imperial physicians had already arrived.

They were currently surrounding the Imperial Son-in-law for an expert consultation.

Imperial Physician Su, possessing the most senior credentials, stroked his beard and shook his head sagely.

"This old man observes that the Imperial Son-in-law's pulse is faint and his limbs are cold. This is a symptom of evil cold invasion. We must gradually expel the evil cold; under no circumstances should we use harsh medicine."

The Imperial Son-in-law, Chi Chongrui, lay weakly on the beauty couch, his two dark circles as large as a panda's close relatives, his eyelids drooping powerlessly.

Internally, he was cursing up a storm.

*Cut the crap, what evil cold?!*

He knew his own situation. A month ago, he had acquired a small sword from an old peasant, visually estimated to be a product of the Bronze Age. He had cherished it endlessly, playing with it in his hands every single day.

Suddenly, an old man had sought him out, offering to buy it off him. When he refused, the old man sneered, dropped a "not knowing what's good for you," and left.

Shortly after, he had begun feeling his soul grow unstable, spending the majority of his day in deep slumbers.

He knew he was finished for.

His transmigrated soul from another world was probably about to be tossed back into the furnace for remolding.

Never mind imperial physicians; even if Hua Tuo or Bian Que came back to life, they couldn't save him.

Too impatient to listen to the physicians bicker, Chi Chongrui looked eagerly at the Eldest Princess and said:

"Darling, hurry and fetch our son back. I still have one unfulfilled wish."

He hadn't beaten his son in a month; he needed to give him a beating before hitting the road.

chapters.title: Darling, I think I can still be saved!
chapters.content:
The Marquis of Yongning’s estate and the Marquis of Xuanyuan’s estate were in the same ward, practically facing each other across the street.

As Jiang Miao raised her eyes, she spotted a young man wearing a short jacket walking back and forth anxiously not far from the entrance of the Marquis of Xuanyuan’s estate.

With a quick mental calculation, this person shared a karmic tie with Jiang Qinhua!

She was instantly amused, the Marquis of Xuanyuan’s first tribulation had arrived!

She then took a closer look at the young man. His features were lean and handsome, and his frame was slender, making him look as though he lived in extreme poverty.

However, his lips were clearly defined, his nose large and prominent with a rounded tip, and his cheekbones full. At a glance, he was a person of resolute character and grand vision.

Moreover, with lion-like eyebrows and tiger-like eyes, and ears set higher than his eyes, he was unequivocally a rare talent for Daoist cultivation.

Jiang Miao’s hands itched; the thought of taking him on as an apprentice stirred within her.

Unfortunately, at this moment, the Prince Consort’s life hung by a thread, and there was no time to delay.

With a flick of her finger, Jiang Miao used spiritual energy to leave a mark on the young man before departing with peace of mind.

Upon arriving at the Eldest Princess’s estate, Chi Ge rushed frantically toward his father.

At the top of his lungs, he began to wail, "Father, your son has arrived too late..."

The Eldest Princess slapped him squarely on the back of the head with a "啪" (crack), her willow brows raised in anger, "Your father isn’t dead yet, what are you mourning for?"

The Prince Consort rolled his eyes with great difficulty and rasped, "Darling, where is my bamboo strip?"

Chi Ge instantly sprang to his feet, reaching out toward Jiang Miao, who was blocked behind the imperial physicians, and shouted, "Miao Miao, save me!"

The Eldest Princess’s eyes lit up, "Miao Miao has come too!"

Jiang Miao pushed past the imperial physicians and walked forward.

She stroked her chin and looked down at the Prince Consort.

"Darling, I suggest you stay calm and try to maintain a vegetative state. Otherwise, your soul will scatter by the end of the day."

Everyone: "???"

Imperial Physician Su subconsciously wanted to scold her, but fortunately remembering that this jinx must not be offended, he quickly covered his mouth and quietly took two steps back.

Right now, if the little jinx said the sun was square, he wouldn't object.

The other imperial physicians, however, knew nothing of Jiang Miao’s background. Seeing her dressed neither like a Buddhist nun nor a Daoist priest, and carrying a beggar’s sack on her back, they assumed she was a charlatan from the jianghu swindling the young marquis, and rebuked her with disdain:

"Where did this jianghu swindler come from? The Prince Consort is merely invaded by evil cold; cursing him with bad omens is a capital offense!"

Jiang Miao said leisurely, "I am currently saving your heads, don’t be ungrateful!"

"Absurd! What skills do you have? You even dare to spout nonsense about saving us!" the imperial physicians said dismissively.

Jiang Miao replied earnestly, "I can’t quite explain my skills, my moral character is dubious, I grow stronger the stronger my opponent is, and I excel at mutual destruction. Care to try?"

The imperial physicians trembled with rage, what kind of slippery rogue was this?

Seeing Jiang Miao’s poised and relaxed demeanor, the Eldest Princess felt greatly reassured, "Miao Miao, do you know what’s wrong with my husband?"

Jiang Miao nodded.

"Dismiss them."

At these words, the imperial physicians anxiously said, "Your Highness, you must not listen to this child’s nonsense. The Prince Consort’s condition is critical; he cannot be delayed by this quack."

The Eldest Princess chose to believe Jiang Miao unconditionally.

She waved her hand at them, "You may all withdraw. I have my own rewards for your trouble today."

Imperial Physician Su was the first to bow and take his leave.

Whether the Prince Consort could be saved or not was unimportant; the crucial thing was not to cross Jiang Miao.

The other imperial physicians still wanted to persuade her, but knowing the Eldest Princess’s absolute stubbornness, they all glared fiercely at Jiang Miao and departed unwillingly.

In their hearts, they cursed her eighteen generations of ancestors.

Who didn't know that the Eldest Princess and the Prince Consort possessed wealth to rival a nation? If they cured the Prince Consort’s illness, they would receive rewards greater than a year’s salary at the very least, only to have their business snatched away by this jianghu ruffian.

Odious!

Yet they also felt some perplexity, Head Physician Su was the most intolerant of swindlers and quacks, yet this time he hadn't even uttered a peep. How strange!

Once the people had cleared out, the Prince Consort rose abruptly from his bed of impending death, forcing his panda-eyes open wide as he looked at Jiang Miao with a mix of excitement and vigilance. This was a fellow countryman!

"May I ask which major corporation you used to work for? Peach Pinduoduo or some JD?"

Jiang Miao suddenly poked Chi Ge on the temple with a finger. Question marks appeared in the young marquis’s eyes, and he instantly passed out and fell asleep.

Only then did Jiang Miao speak:

"Big brother, you’re about to kick the bucket and yet you care where I used to work. Hand over your treasure."

A treasure?

The Prince Consort blinked, the ashen flesh of his face turning visibly red.

It couldn’t be what he was thinking, could it?

This kid seemed a bit lacking in propriety...

Jiang Miao: *Why is he blushing? Do souls get a flash of brilliance before death too?*

She instructed the Eldest Princess, "Get that little sword from his bosom and hand it to me."

The Eldest Princess hurried over and retrieved it.

The Prince Consort let out a massive sigh of relief, it was not what he had imagined...

The Eldest Princess took one look at the little sword, which emanated an ancient and mysterious aura, and hesitated, "Miao Miao, could it be this thing that offended the Prince Consort?"

Jiang Miao took it and casually tossed it into her beggar’s sack.

"No, this gadget is wicked, and he couldn't suppress it. I’ll keep it for him."

The Prince Consort: "..."

Jiang Miao’s expression turned serious.

"Your Highness the Eldest Princess, you know what’s going on with your husband, don't you?"

The Eldest Princess blinked her large eyes and said weakly, "Miao Miao, you don't think he’s been captured as a monster, do you?"

Jiang Miao understood in her heart.

She pondered and said, "He’s been messed with, which caused his soul and this body to experience a state of rejection. The imperial physicians weren't wrong; his condition is indeed an invasion of evil cold, but this evil cold is no ordinary evil cold. To put it bluntly, it’s the state of a dead person."

!!!

The Eldest Princess jumped in fright, "H-h-he still has breath, doesn't he? Miao Miao, look, he even has a shadow, he can't be a ghost..."

"Some people are alive, but they are already dead," Jiang Miao pronounced her verdict. "A few hours ago, this body of his was already dead, and now his soul is about to scatter as well."

The Eldest Princess froze, then instantly pounced on the Prince Consort, wailing loudly,

"Husband, if you abandon us orphans and widows, what will we do henceforth? Where is the silver? Where are the antiques?"

The Prince Consort used all his strength to push her face away.

"Darling, it’s fine even if you don't cry. You don't have to pinch yourself so hard."

The Eldest Princess stopped her wailing in a second, rubbed her thigh awkwardly while sucking in a breath of air, and cast a reproachful sideways glance at him.

"A person on the verge of death really is different, you even dare to expose me now."

As she spoke, her eye sockets turned red.

Looking pitifully at Jiang Miao, she puckered her little mouth and said, "Miao Miao, hurry and see if he can still be saved!"

Jiang Miao patted the Eldest Princess’s shoulder, "Congratulations, Your Highness. This Great Immortal has calculated that a fine physical vessel is going to kick the bucket at the Hour of Chou (1 to 3 AM) today. This Great Immortal shall help the Prince Consort borrow a corpse to resurrect his soul."

In a corner invisible to mortals, a netherworld runner clutched his iron chains and shivered, looking aggrievedly at Jiang Miao.

Could it be that his trip had been for nothing this time?

Was his performance quota for the month going to go down the drain?

Jiang Miao feigned blindness.

The Eldest Princess instantly lit up with starry eyes, the corners of her upturned mouth completely impossible to suppress.

So delighted that rosy clouds flew across her face, "Does this concubine still have this blessing? Would doing this... be a bit inappropriate?"

The Prince Consort looked up and sighed.

His soul was still alive, but he was already dead.

Giving up on the struggle, he said, "Don't bother, let me die. Give me the bamboo strip!" Once he finished beating his son, he would willingly embrace death.

The Eldest Princess’s brows turned fierce, "You try dying for me to see! Tomorrow I'll recruit a new Prince Consort, and then the new Prince Consort will spend your silver while beating your son!"

The Prince Consort once again rose abruptly from his bed of impending death and said resolutely, "Darling, I think I can still be saved!"

Jiang Miao laughed mischievously, "Alright, borrowing a corpse to resurrect a soul is SSS-difficulty. I need to go get some items to guarantee success."

With that, she grabbed the netherworld runner by the back of his collar and left. As she reached the door, she turned back and said, "Today’s fee is five thousand taels of gold, payable in installments. If you really don't have it, you can use the Emperor's pet animals as collateral."

Upon hearing "five thousand taels of gold," the Eldest Princess and her husband almost shouted in unison, "Forget it, don't save him."

Upon hearing the latter sentence, their faces broke into simultaneous smiles.

Only then did she ask what she was going to look for.

Jiang Miao tossed back a single sentence, "Ask fewer questions about affairs of the path," and bolted away in a flash.

---

chapters.title: Helping an Eminent Monk Enter Parinirvana Early
chapters.content:
Upon exiting the Eldest Princess’s estate, Jiang Miao put the netherworld runner down and asked,

"Are you afraid of me?"

The netherworld runner nodded timidly.

A glimmer of hopeful light ignited in Jiang Miao’s eyes, "Then do you know who I am?"

The netherworld runner: "???"

Your heroic deeds of fighting the Six Realms invincible and dumping three Upper Deities have already spread throughout the Six Realms. Who could possibly not know you?

Just as he was about to nod, he suddenly recalled the gossip he had heard earlier: how Lord Jiang had defaulted on romantic debts with three Upper Deities, overturned her carriage, and fled overnight.

His scalp instantly went numb. Good grief, this was a test!

As long as he dared to say he knew her, he feared Lord Jiang would silence him with a blade in the very next second.

The netherworld runner praised his own cleverness and shook his head like a rattle-drum.

Unwaveringly, he declared, "I don't know you!"

"Then why are you afraid of me?" Jiang Miao felt he was deceiving her.

Brilliant in his panic, the netherworld runner buttered up to her:

"This humble one is deeply captivated by your supreme, awe-inspiring aura, the kind that slays gods when gods appear and Buddhas when Buddhas appear, and couldn't help but feel reverence. The reason this humble one has lived a smooth life is entirely thanks to this keen insight!"

Jiang Miao felt somewhat disheartened. She could only bluff small fry like netherworld runners. Having been forced to borrow a shell to hide from debts, she surely wasn't any big shot; how could a mere little netherworld runner recognize her?

Never mind. In any case, the City God had said that the bastard who forced her to swear an oath not to reveal her identity was right here in the capital; she would run into him sooner or later, so there was no need to rush.

She pointed toward the direction of the Marquis of Yongning’s estate and said, "Go wait for me at the Marquis of Yongning’s estate. There are four ghosts there, enough for you to take back and report for duty. As for the Prince Consort’s ghost, just pretend you let out a fart!"

The netherworld runner was overjoyed. He had thought the task couldn't be completed, but who would have thought he could exceed expectations.

His performance metrics were saved now!
