Gratefully, he bowed to Jiang Miao. *Who said Lord Jiang was difficult to deal with? She’s actually quite a nice person...*

Jiang Miao cast an invisibility illusion, used the Earth-Shrinking technique to quickly leave the city, and arrived at the True Awakening Temple on Eastern Mountain outside the city.

To let the Prince Consort borrow a corpse and resurrect his soul, she still needed something Buddhist, an eminent monk’s sarira (relic).

This was the Prince Consort’s second time borrowing a shell, and his soul had already suffered trauma. Forcibly shoving it into a new body would cause extremely severe adverse reactions.

There was a 50% chance he would become an idiot, and the other 50%... consequences were inauspicious.

With a sarira, it would be different. With the blessing of an eminent monk’s merit, he could be spared the intrusion of heaven and earth’s forces upon his soul, and it even had the effect of stabilizing the soul.

In matters like this, Buddhism had some substance to it.

Mainly, they preached universal salvation and would rather consume themselves inwardly to help others.

Unlike Daoism, where unless it concerned the great义 of the nation, the motto was "better a fellow Daoist die than poor貧 Daoist," leaning heavily toward external consumption...

It was also the Prince Consort’s good fortune that his ancestors had accumulated virtue, allowing him to encounter her, a high master, just as an eminent monk of the True Awakening Temple was about to enter Parinirvana (pass away).

However, the Prince Consort couldn't wait, so she decided to discuss it with the eminent monk and ask him to enter Parinirvana a little earlier.

Anyway, Buddhism spoke of the "Six Auspicious Times," meaning twenty-four hours a day, every minute and second was auspicious and smooth, a little earlier or a little later wouldn't make much difference...

The True Awakening Temple was bustling with incense, and since it was the blooming spring season, worshippers coming to offer incense arrived in a continuous stream.

Just as Jiang Miao was preparing to sneak into the rear hall, she caught sight of Jiang Qinhua and her former mother devoutly kneeling and kowtowing before the Buddha.

Madam Jiang muttered incantations under her breath, and Jiang Miao couldn't help but prick up her ears to eavesdrop.

"I beseech the Bodhisattva to bless the believer Jiang Su-shi’s daughter, Jiang Qinhua, to successfully marry Prince Ye. This believer is willing to revere the Buddha and keep a vegetarian diet until the end of her days..."

Prince Ye?

Hearing this, Jiang Miao was amused. This former mother of hers had grown quite ambitious; previously she only wanted her to marry someone of equal social standing, but now she was eyeing the imperial family.

And it was even that guy trailing purple smoke.

Not to mention, this taste was actually quite good.

Jiang Qinhua devoutly pressed her palms together, though she didn't know what she was praying for in her heart.

Jiang Miao shook her head. Burning dozens of cash worth of incense while praying for tens of millions in wishes, even a dog would shake its head at that.

Praying to an ascetic temple for marriage, asking a cloistered abbot about life... what a foolish child.

However, judging by the former mother’s physiognomy, she would suffer a bloody disaster today; asking the eminent monk to enter Parinirvana early might just let her catch the excitement in time.

Jiang Miao hurriedly slipped into the rear hall, and taking advantage of the monks' inattention, dashed through a small side door straight into the monks' residential courtyard behind the hall.

Beneath an ancient bodhi tree, an old monk with benevolent eyebrows sat serenely, his expression peaceful and calm as if he had transcended the mortal world and merged with heaven and earth.

The branches and leaves of the bodhi tree swayed gently, making a rustling sound. Sunlight filtered through the lush green leaves, casting rings of golden light upon his body.

Sanskrit-chanting monks sat solemnly around him in a circle. Dressed in simple monastic robes and holding prayer beads, they lowered their heads to chant scriptures. Their voices, low and powerful like celestial music, echoed through this sacred sanctuary beneath the bodhi tree.

Even with Jiang Miao’s untamed disposition, she could not help but lighten her steps and hold her breath.

She formed a Daoist hand-seal and bowed slightly toward the old monk; this truly compassionate and eminent monk deserved respect.

Sensing her presence, the old monk slowly opened his eyes and smiled slightly at her.

"Patron, you have come."

The monks did not stop chanting because of Jiang Miao’s arrival, nor did they even glance at her, as if no one perceived her existence.

Jiang Miao restrained her devil-may-care demeanor, chanted "Immeasurable Heavenly尊" (Wuliang Tianzun), and said softly,

"Master, I want to borrow something of yours."

The old monk shook his head slightly, a trace of regret on his face, "Patron, have you come for Patron Chi? Pity that this old monk’s dharma power is likely insufficient and cannot help him."

Jiang Miao wagged her finger, "Not so. I have come precisely to lend Master a helping hand; tempered with true fire, you will surely leave behind a sarira."

The old monk’s white eyebrows twitched slightly in disbelief.

"Patron, do not dupe this old monk. This old monk reckons his merit, compassion, and wisdom are all lacking, and he cannot produce a sarira."

Jiang Miao slightly raised her chin, full of confidence, and said,

"If I say you can, you can. Prince Consort Chi develops commerce and trade, bringing abundance and prosperity to countless commoners of the Dafeng Dynasty; he possesses great merit. Master helping him is helping all living beings, and your shortcomings will thus be made up for."

This statement was purely bluffing.

The scientific explanation was that the composition of a sarira included silicates, phosphates, calcium carbonate, and various oxides, all of which could be found in the human body.

When the temperature reached a thousand-plus degrees Celsius, certain substances in human bones would undergo fusion and crystallization through a series of chemical reactions during calcination.

When the temperature rose to around 1600°C, these crystals would agglomerate large enough, and that was a sarira.

As for the color, luster, and transparency of a sarira, they were related to the crystal structure, composition, and proportion of chemical substances within the crystals. ①

Of course, not just anyone’s sarira would do; this was merely being used as a vessel for the soul, and what truly played a role was the merit this eminent monk had accumulated over a lifetime.

The old monk pondered for a moment, "Then let it be as Patron wishes. Being able to help Patron Chi bestow grace upon the common people is this old monk’s fortune."

"Master has boundless merit!" Jiang Miao bowed in salute.

Immediately afterward, she rubbed her fingers, and a small, bright white spark danced on her fingertips. The temperature in the large courtyard instantly soared, resembling the scorching heat of midsummer.

"If Master doesn't mind, let’s begin now. Prince Consort Chi cannot wait."

The old monk remained calm and composed, wearing a compassionate smile, "Amitabha, please help this old monk enter Nirvana, Patron."

With that, he closed his eyes once more.

Jiang Miao flicked her finger, "Go." The flame seemed like a spiritual entity, lightly leaping onto the old monk.

In an instant, the bright white flame enveloped him entirely, making his sacred and solemn face glow radiantly.

The surrounding chanting of scriptures abruptly escalated, rolling waves of Sanskrit sounds pushing one after another, resembling the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss.

Jiang Miao sat cross-legged, her hands rapidly forming seals, her mind pristine and empty as she devoutly chanted:

"Boundless transcend the immortal source, vast and boundless naturally clear, all bearing the Great Dao’s power to subdue all demonic spirits... Entrusting our lives to the Supreme Lord, capable of eradicating all sins, the Heavenly Honored One expounds the scriptures to guide the floating life..."

No one could see that these very characters converged into a golden rainbow bridge falling beneath the old monk, while at the other end lay the endless path to the heavens...

---

Note ①: The scientific explanation of sariras in this paragraph is sourced from Zhihu.
